members.description: No tool computes the primordial tensor transfer function through the specific reheating -> radiation -> EMD -> reheating history and compares the suppressed gravitational-wave spectrum in the T_0/T_R plane against detector sensitivity curves; the card offers only qualitative GW-context estimates.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the tensor transfer function for the piecewise expansion history (modes entering during pre-EMD radiation, EMD, and post-EMD radiation) as a module on top of the paper's H(T) equations, parameterized by (T_reh, T_0, T_R, n_T), and overlay LISA/DECIGO/pulsar-timing sensitivity curves to produce quantitative constraint regions.

members.model_name: False-vacuum-island primordial black hole scenario
members.description: No FOPT stochastic gravitational-wave calculator is attached to the route: the GW counterpart observable has no computed spectrum for the benchmark (alpha_*, beta/H_*, T_*) points, so LISA/Taiji/TianQin testability cannot be assessed.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the standard sound-wave/bubble-collision/turbulence semi-analytic GW templates (LISA Cosmology Working Group fits, as in PTPlot) as a function of alpha_*, beta/H_*, T_*, and compare against LISA/Taiji/TianQin power-law-integrated sensitivity curves, jointly with the small-scale curvature-perturbation bound the card flags.

members.model_name: High-scale darkogenesis with leptodark messenger sphaleron transfer
members.description: No gravitational-wave spectrum has been computed for the first-order dark phase transition; the card quotes only a temperature range with no alpha, beta/H, or detector-specific signal estimate.
members.proposed_resolution: Compute the finite-temperature dark Higgs potential parameters (alpha, beta/H, T_*) with CosmoTransitions and map them through standard bubble-collision/sound-wave spectral templates to LISA and pulsar-timing sensitivity curves.

members.model_name: Low-scale darkogenesis with perturbative baryon transfer
members.description: No gravitational-wave spectrum has been computed for the first-order dark phase transition; only a broad transition-temperature range is quoted, with the first-order character itself estimated from a simplified finite-temperature potential.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the dark Higgs/singlet finite-temperature potential in CosmoTransitions to obtain alpha, beta/H, and T_*, then map through standard sound-wave/bubble-collision spectral templates to LISA and other detector sensitivity curves.

members.model_name: Z2-breaking complex singlet pseudo-Goldstone scalar dark matter
members.description: No released implementation of the cxSM finite-temperature effective potential exists for the phase-transition leg: computing (alpha_pt, beta/H, T_n) for the two-step SFOEWPT benchmarks and the resulting LISA-band GW spectrum currently requires rebuilding the thermal potential by hand.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the one-loop daisy-resummed cxSM thermal potential in CosmoTransitions (or PhaseTracer), extract alpha_pt, beta/H and T_n along the scan, and map to GW spectra with the standard sound-wave spectral fits against the public LISA sensitivity curve.

members.model_name: Higgs-portal vector dark matter with broken U(1)
members.description: No gravitational-wave spectrum pipeline exists for this model: the card's GW observable is route-level only, with no computation from CosmoTransitions nucleation output (alpha, beta/H, T_n) to a stochastic mHz spectrum or a LISA sensitivity comparison.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend the CosmoTransitions-based EWPT scan to extract alpha, beta/H, and T_n, feed them through standard sound-wave/turbulence spectral fits (PTPlot-style templates), and compare against the LISA power-law-integrated sensitivity curve to produce a GW detectability map over (lambda_2, m_s, v_s).

members.model_name: WIMPy leptogenesis inert-doublet dark matter with early matter domination
members.description: No packaged pipeline propagates this variant's early-matter-domination expansion history (T_end plus the matter-field dilution) into a primordial gravitational-wave spectral tilt/break Omega_GW(f) for confrontation with detector sensitivity curves; only semi-analytic results from related work exist.
members.proposed_resolution: Code the standard transfer of an inflationary or cosmic-string Omega_GW(f) through a matter-dominated-then-radiation history parameterized by T_end (following the turning-frequency treatment of the related EMD work, arXiv:2202.10474) and emit spectra ready to score against LISA/BBO/ET/CE curves.

members.model_name: WIMPy leptogenesis inert-doublet dark matter with fast expanding universe
members.description: No packaged pipeline propagates this variant's fast-expansion history (n, T_r) into a primordial gravitational-wave spectral tilt Omega_GW(f) for confrontation with detector sensitivity curves; only semi-analytic kination-like transfer results from related work exist.
members.proposed_resolution: Code the standard transfer of an inflationary or cosmic-string Omega_GW(f) through a stiff-fluid epoch parameterized by (n, T_r), producing the blue-tilted spectral feature and its frequency location, and emit spectra ready to score against LISA/BBO/ET/CE curves.

members.model_name: WIMPy leptogenesis inert-doublet dark matter with scalar-tensor gravity
members.description: No packaged pipeline propagates this variant's scalar-tensor-modified expansion history into a primordial gravitational-wave spectral distortion Omega_GW(f) for confrontation with detector sensitivity curves; existing semi-analytic transfer results cover EMD/kination-like histories rather than the scalar-tensor Hubble enhancement.
members.proposed_resolution: Numerically integrate tensor-mode evolution through the scalar-tensor H(z) enhancement and its relaxation to standard expansion before BBN for an inflationary or cosmic-string source, producing Omega_GW(f) spectra ready to score against LISA/BBO/ET/CE curves.

members.model_name: Scale-invariant singlet scalar dark matter
members.description: No tunneling/percolation pipeline covers this model's strongly supercooled, QCD-triggered regime: CosmoTransitions-style bounce solvers and the standard alpha/beta-H GW fit formulas assume a transition that completes above the QCD scale, whereas RG-consistent points here supercool past T_QCD and need QCD-catalyzed electroweak breaking treated explicitly.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend a bounce solver (CosmoTransitions or BubbleDet-based workflow) with the QCD-coupled finite-temperature effective potential for the scale-invariant two-singlet sector, track S3/T down through T_QCD to obtain percolation temperature, alpha and beta/H, and feed these into the standard sound-wave/collision GW spectrum fits (e.g. via PTPlot) for LISA-band forecasting.

members.model_name: Complex singlet scalar dark matter with restored CP and Z2
members.description: No implementation of the complex-singlet finite-temperature effective potential with high-T CP and Z2 breaking exists, so the phase-transition strength v_c/T_c, the verification of CP/Z2 restoration today, and the associated gravitational-wave spectrum cannot be computed.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the complex-singlet scalar potential with one-loop thermal corrections and daisy resummation in CosmoTransitions, scan for symmetry non-restoration at high T, and pipe the resulting alpha and beta/H into the standard sound-wave GW spectrum formulas (PTPlot templates) for LISA-band comparison.

members.model_name: Two-scalar Z2 Higgs-portal dark matter including singlet-only s-s' cross-couplings
members.description: No finite-temperature phase-transition solver covers this model: the a2/b2/c2 transition channels are identified only from selected analytic extrema of the one-loop finite-temperature potential, and no code computes the nucleation temperature, latent heat, or beta/H needed to turn the strong-EWPT claim into a gravitational-wave spectrum.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the two-singlet one-loop (plus daisy-resummed) finite-temperature potential in CosmoTransitions or a comparable bounce solver to trace the multi-step a2/b2/c2 histories, extract T_n, alpha, and beta/H, and feed standard sound-wave GW templates to produce a LISA-comparable spectrum.

members.model_name: Melting cosmic string scalar-field dark matter
members.description: No public cosmic-string SGWB code handles melting strings with temperature-dependent tension mu(T); existing loop-network spectrum calculators assume constant G mu, so the peaked Omega_gw(f) and f_peak for this model rest on a semi-analytic estimate that neglects backreaction and particle emission.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend an existing cosmic-string loop-network SGWB calculator (e.g. the LISA cosmic-string pipeline codes) to evolve loop formation and emission with a time-dependent tension mu(T) prescribed by the scale-free thermal model, validated against field-theory string simulations in a few benchmarks.

members.model_name: Two-body interacting superfluid dark matter around black holes
members.description: No waveform or wave-optics code exists for continuous gravitational waves lensed by an SMBH dressed with the two-body superfluid core, which the source proposes as a probe but does not implement.
members.proposed_resolution: Derive the wave-optics amplification factor for the black-hole-plus-superfluid-core mass profile and implement it in a GW lensing code, scanning source/lens geometry for Sgr A*-like configurations.

members.model_name: Scale-invariant two-singlet scalar dark matter
members.description: No implemented phase-transition pipeline exists for the two-singlet scale-invariant potential: bubble nucleation parameters (T_n, alpha, beta/H) and the stochastic gravitational-wave spectrum are not computed, only v_c/T_c is available, so the GW observable cannot be forecast.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the finite-temperature effective potential (with daisy resummation) in CosmoTransitions or PhaseTracer to compute nucleation parameters, feed them through standard sound-wave/turbulence GW spectral templates, and evaluate signal-to-noise against the LISA sensitivity curve over the relic-density-selected parameter region.

members.model_name: Low-mass CP-violating effective inert-doublet dark matter
members.description: No finite-temperature effective-potential implementation of the IDM plus dimension-six operators computes the two-step electroweak phase transition, so the intermediate vev v_phi, transition strength, nucleation rate, and wall velocity needed both to anchor the BAU and to predict the gravitational-wave spectrum are unavailable, fully blocking the GW follow-up observable.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend a CosmoTransitions-style solver with the D6-corrected one-loop daisy-resummed potential, trace the two-step transition to extract (alpha, beta/H, T_n, v_phi), and feed them into the standard sound-wave/bubble-collision GW fit formulas to place the signal against LISA-band sensitivity curves.

members.model_name: Dimension-six real singlet scalar Higgs-portal dark matter
members.description: The gravitational-wave observable rests only on static effective-potential criteria (v_c/T_c, sphaleron rate); no bubble-nucleation calculation (T_n, alpha, beta/H) or stochastic GW spectrum has been computed for the dimension-six singlet potential, so the phase-transition signal cannot be confronted with LISA-class sensitivity curves.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the tree-plus-thermal potential including the |H|^2 S^4 / M^2 operator in CosmoTransitions or PhaseTracer, compute bounce actions and nucleation temperatures across the two-step scan, and map (alpha, beta/H, T_n) to Omega_GW(f) with the standard sound-wave/turbulence templates.

members.model_name: Z3 inert doublet-singlet scalar dark matter
members.description: No public implementation exists of the Z3 doublet-singlet finite-temperature effective potential (with loop and thermal corrections) and the downstream T_n, alpha_PT, beta/H and stochastic GW spectrum computation; the GW observable currently rests entirely on source-paper figures.
members.proposed_resolution: Code the Z3 scalar potential with one-loop and daisy-resummed thermal corrections in CosmoTransitions, extract T_n, alpha_PT, beta/H from the bounce action, and feed standard sound-wave GW spectrum templates plus LISA-class sensitivity curves for SNR.

members.model_name: Three-body interacting superfluid dark matter around black holes
members.description: No waveform or wave-optics code exists for continuous gravitational waves lensed by an SMBH dressed with the three-body superfluid profile, which the source proposes as a probe but does not implement.
members.proposed_resolution: Derive the lensing amplification factor for the black-hole-plus-superfluid-core mass profile in the wave-optics regime and implement it in a GW lensing code, scanning source/lens geometry for Sgr A*-like systems.

members.model_name: Z2-symmetric complex singlet scalar two-component dark matter
members.description: No public implementation of the cxSM Z2-symmetric finite-temperature effective potential and SFOEWPT-to-GW pipeline (alpha, beta/H, T_n, GW spectrum) exists; the phase-transition step has null tool_or_code and the route lists an unnamed 'finite-temperature phase-transition code' as a required resource.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the cxSM one-loop finite-temperature potential (with daisy resummation) in CosmoTransitions or an equivalent bounce solver, extract alpha, beta/H and T_n over the paper's scan domain, and feed standard sound-wave/turbulence GW spectral templates compared against the LISA power-law-sensitivity curve.

members.model_name: Generalized no-scale inflation with PBH dark matter
members.description: The PBH abundance step is uncalibrated for these inflection-point benchmarks: f_PBH depends exponentially on the collapse threshold, window function, non-Gaussianity of the ultra-slow-roll perturbations, and critical-collapse treatment, so 'f_PBH near 1' benchmarks are not robust at the order-of-magnitude level.
members.proposed_resolution: Adopt a peaks-theory pipeline with a numerical-relativity-calibrated collapse threshold and critical-collapse scaling, include the leading non-Gaussian correction from the ultra-slow-roll to slow-roll transition, and quote f_PBH with a method-spread band for each benchmark instead of a single Press-Schechter value.

members.model_name: PBH dark matter from stiff reheating with a broken-power-law scalar spectrum
members.description: The PBH collapse threshold delta_c (and the associated critical-collapse mass relation) is not calibrated for formation during a stiff reheating epoch with w_re ~ 0.5-0.65; existing numerical-relativity thresholds target radiation domination, and f_PBH is exponentially sensitive to delta_c, so the predicted abundance carries orders-of-magnitude uncertainty (card: collapse threshold dominates the residual uncertainty).
members.proposed_resolution: Run numerical-relativity simulations of spherical (and representative aspherical) perturbation collapse for equations of state w = 0.4-0.7, tabulate delta_c(w, curvature-profile shape) and the critical-collapse scaling, and publish the threshold tables for use in reheating-era Press-Schechter/peaks abundance calculations.

members.model_name: Non-Abelian axion-inflation primordial black hole dark matter
members.description: The PBH abundance is computed with Gaussian Press-Schechter statistics and an assumed collapse threshold delta_c, yet f_PBH is exponentially sensitive to both; no model-specific non-Gaussianity or threshold calibration exists for this spectrum shape.
members.proposed_resolution: Compute the non-Gaussian statistics of zeta sourced by the gauge-scalar instability and calibrate the collapse threshold for the resulting peaked spectrum using numerical relativity collapse simulations or established peak-theory/compaction-function prescriptions.

members.model_name: LIGO-mass primordial black hole dark matter
members.description: The merger-rate prediction depends on extrapolated low-mass halo mass functions, concentration-mass relations, and internal velocity distributions far below simulated scales, which the card flags as the dominant uncertainty (halo_rate_model validity entry, extrapolation_risk high), leaving the predicted rate uncertain at the order-of-magnitude level.
members.proposed_resolution: Run high-resolution N-body/zoom simulations of PBH-dominated cosmologies (including Poisson isocurvature power from PBH discreteness) down to the smallest bound halos to calibrate the low-mass halo mass function, concentrations, and velocity dispersions entering the capture-rate integral, and publish the calibrated fitting functions.

members.model_name: Classically conformal B-L double-inflation primordial black hole dark matter
members.description: No PBH mass-function calculator with a controlled collapse-threshold and non-Gaussianity treatment is attached to the model; the card notes f_PBH can shift by orders of magnitude with threshold and tail assumptions, so the abundance recast is not yet quantitative.
members.proposed_resolution: Adopt and wire in a public PBH-abundance pipeline (threshold-statistics/peaks formalism with critical collapse, e.g. a PBHbeta-style calculator) fed by the computed spectrum, with the collapse threshold calibrated against published numerical-relativity threshold values for the relevant spectral shape.

members.model_name: Primordial black hole dark matter from a non-minimal curvaton scenario
members.description: The PBH abundance is computed with a Gaussian density tail and a hand-picked threshold delta_c = 0.51 within a 0.4-0.7 systematic range, while the card flags exponential sensitivity of f_PBH to non-Gaussian tails and threshold choice; no calibrated non-Gaussian abundance treatment specific to this curvaton scenario exists.
members.proposed_resolution: Propagate the curvaton non-Gaussianity from the perturbation solver into a non-Gaussian PBH abundance formalism (compaction-function statistics with numerical-relativity-calibrated, shape-dependent thresholds a la Musco et al.) and quote f_PBH(M) with a threshold-systematic band instead of a single delta_c.

members.model_name: SU(5) inflection-point inflation primordial black-hole dark matter
members.description: The mapping from the model's P_zeta spike to (M_PBH, f_PBH) is uncalibrated: collapse threshold delta_c, window function, and non-Gaussianity corrections shift f_PBH by orders of magnitude for a fixed spectrum, and the card records no chosen prescription or mass function.
members.proposed_resolution: Compute the PBH mass function from the model's numerical P_zeta using peak theory with the nonlinear (compaction-function) threshold prescription, bracketing systematics by comparing Press-Schechter and peaks with published window-function choices.

members.model_name: Asteroid-mass PBH dark matter from string-wall catastrogenesis
members.description: The GW production efficiency used for the catastrogenesis stochastic background is imported from domain-wall simulations outside this model's biased multi-vacuum (N>1) string-wall regime, leaving the predicted Omega_GW amplitude uncalibrated at the factor level needed for detector forecasts.
members.proposed_resolution: Extract the GW efficiency parameter directly from the same lattice simulations proposed for the collapse calibration (or dedicated GW-sourcing runs of biased Z_N networks), reporting efficiency as a function of N and bias so the analytic spectrum can be normalized consistently with the PBH prediction.

members.model_name: Inflection-point inflation primordial black-hole dark matter
members.description: The PBH abundance is exponentially sensitive to the assumed collapse threshold (delta_c = 0.414) and window-function choice, and the card notes this is fixed by assumption rather than calibrated for this spectrum's shape.
members.proposed_resolution: Replace the fixed-threshold Press-Schechter treatment with peaks-theory abundance using a shape-dependent threshold calibrated on numerical-relativity collapse simulations for the model's narrow spectral peak, propagating the threshold uncertainty into f_PBH.

members.model_name: Dissipative-inflation primordial black hole dark matter
members.description: No calibrated mapping exists from the full (non-Gaussian) curvature distribution produced by the dissipative thermal noise to the PBH mass function and f_PBH; the card notes exponential sensitivity to collapse threshold and perturbation statistics, and Gaussian threshold-collapse formulas can misestimate f_PBH by orders of magnitude.
members.proposed_resolution: Compute the PBH abundance directly from the sampled non-Gaussian P(zeta) of the stochastic solver using compaction-function/peaks statistics with a collapse threshold calibrated on numerical-relativity simulations of peaked-spectrum profiles, and propagate the same statistics into the induced-GW normalization.

members.model_name: Reverse-engineered ultra-slow-roll primordial black hole dark matter
members.description: The PBH mass function from the reverse-engineered plateau carries uncalibrated collapse-threshold and USR non-Gaussianity systematics; because f_PBH is exponentially sensitive to these, the headline asteroid-mass abundance prediction is currently order-of-magnitude at best.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement a compaction-function/peak-theory mass-function calculator that takes the plateau P_R(k) plus the USR-induced local non-Gaussianity, with the collapse threshold calibrated against published numerical-relativity critical-collapse results for the relevant spectral shapes and thermal-history epochs.

members.model_name: Subsolar-mass primordial black holes from monochromatic curvature perturbations
members.description: The PBH abundance mapping is only implemented in the delta-function Press-Schechter/Carr approximation; the collapse threshold delta_c, window-function choice, finite spectral width, and non-Gaussianity are uncalibrated, and the source itself states the abundance is uncertain by orders of magnitude depending on scheme.
members.proposed_resolution: Replace the Carr formula with a peak-theory abundance calculation using a numerical-relativity-calibrated collapse threshold and critical-collapse scaling, extended to finite-width curvature spectra and leading non-Gaussian corrections, and propagate the resulting f_PBH uncertainty band into the PTA/microlensing recast.

members.model_name: Gauss-Bonnet-corrected single-field-inflation primordial black hole dark matter
members.description: The PBH abundance is computed with Gaussian statistics, a simple threshold delta_c = 1/3, and collapse fraction gamma = 0.2, whereas ultra-slow-roll spectra require critical-collapse, window-function, and non-Gaussianity corrections that can shift f_PBH by orders of magnitude; the card flags this high-sensitivity assumption explicitly.
members.proposed_resolution: Recompute beta(M) and f_PBH(M) for the model's spectra using modern peaks-theory or compaction-function statistics with numerical-relativity-calibrated thresholds and critical-collapse scaling, including the local non-Gaussianity induced by the ultra-slow-roll phase, and propagate the spread as an abundance systematic.

members.model_name: Non-singular-bounce generated primordial black hole dark matter scenario
members.description: The PBH mass function and f_PBH are obtained from monochromatic threshold statistics without a specified collapse threshold prescription or an extended-mass-function treatment, so the claimed 1e-3 < f_PBH < 1 windows carry uncalibrated threshold/window-function uncertainty and cannot be confronted consistently with mass-function-dependent microlensing limits.
members.proposed_resolution: Couple the resummed spectrum to a standard PBH abundance calculator using peaks-theory or compaction-function threshold statistics with numerically calibrated delta_c, produce the extended mass function, and recast the Subaru/HSC and compiled microlensing bounds using the public extended-mass-function method and constraint data (PBHbounds-style curves).

members.model_name: Primordial black hole dark matter from an early stiff/kination epoch
members.description: The PBH collapse threshold delta_c and critical-collapse mass relation are not numerically calibrated for horizon re-entry during a stiff epoch with 1/3 < w <= 1, and beta(M) is exponentially sensitive to delta_c, so the predicted f_PBH(M) carries an uncontrolled order-of-magnitude uncertainty.
members.proposed_resolution: Run numerical-relativity collapse simulations across the stiff-era equation-of-state range (extending a spectral collapse code such as SPriBHoS to w > 1/3 backgrounds) to calibrate delta_c(w) and critical-collapse scaling, and fold the calibrated thresholds into the Press-Schechter/peaks abundance formula.

members.model_name: Supercooled FOPT primordial black hole dark matter with magnetogenesis
members.description: The PBH abundance (tuned to f_PBH = 1) hinges on the collapse threshold delta_c for late-nucleating overdense patches during a supercooled FOPT, which the card flags as the dominant uncertainty; no simulation-calibrated value of delta_c exists for this vacuum-energy-dominated collapse scenario, only threshold choices carried over from standard radiation-era collapse.
members.proposed_resolution: Perform numerical-relativity simulations of the collapse of late-nucleating false-vacuum Hubble patches embedded in the reheated plasma to calibrate delta_c and the resulting mass relation as functions of beta/H and the supercooling strength, and publish the fit for use in the semi-analytic abundance formulae.

members.model_name: SU(5) x U(1) hybrid-inflation primordial black hole dark matter model
members.description: f_PBH depends exponentially on the collapse threshold delta_c and on non-Gaussianity of the waterfall perturbations, but only a Gaussian Press-Schechter estimate with an assumed window function is available, leaving the abundance uncertain by orders of magnitude.
members.proposed_resolution: Compute the non-Gaussian probability distribution of waterfall curvature perturbations (from the gap_1 stochastic simulation) and recalculate PBH formation with peaks theory or compaction-function criteria calibrated on numerical-relativity collapse thresholds.

members.model_name: Multi-bumpy inflation primordial black hole dark matter
members.description: The PBH abundance from each peak is exponentially sensitive to the collapse threshold and to non-Gaussianity of the enhanced modes, and the route only carries spherical/ellipsoidal Press-Schechter prescriptions without numerical calibration for this spectrum shape.
members.proposed_resolution: Calibrate delta_c and the abundance prescription against numerical-relativity collapse results for the actual peak profile shapes (compaction-function/peak-theory treatment), and propagate the USR non-Gaussianity of the bump-crossing modes into beta(M).

members.model_name: Solo-bumpy inflation primordial black hole dark matter
members.description: The PBH abundance is exponentially sensitive to the collapse threshold delta_c and to non-Gaussianity of the enhanced modes, and the route only carries spherical/ellipsoidal Press-Schechter prescriptions without numerical calibration for this peak profile.
members.proposed_resolution: Calibrate delta_c and the abundance prescription against numerical-relativity collapse results for the actual peak profile shape (compaction-function/peak-theory treatment), and propagate the USR non-Gaussianity of the bump-crossing modes into beta(M).

members.model_name: Quantum-well stochastic-inflation primordial black hole dark matter
members.description: The compaction-function collapse threshold delta_c and critical-collapse parameters used in the formation-probability step are calibrated with numerical relativity on Gaussian-like density profiles; no calibration exists for the exponential/heavy-tailed curvature profiles produced by quantum-well stochastic diffusion, and the card flags threshold and window-function choice as a systematic that shifts the abundance exponentially.
members.proposed_resolution: Run numerical-relativity PBH collapse simulations (extending existing radiation-era collapse codes of the Musco type) on representative density profiles drawn from the stochastic-delta-N heavy-tailed PDF, and fit delta_c and the critical exponent as functions of the profile-shape parameter for use in the semi-analytic formation step.

members.description: The PBH collapse threshold and mass-function mapping are uncalibrated for horizon re-entry during or after kination (w near 1), yet f_PBH is exponentially sensitive to the assumed threshold.
members.proposed_resolution: Run numerical-relativity or Misner-Sharp collapse simulations of super-horizon perturbations in a kination-dominated background to calibrate delta_c(w) and the critical-collapse mass relation, then feed the calibrated threshold into the Press-Schechter/peaks mass-function step.

members.model_name: Sgoldstino-stabilized canonical Kahler non-oscillatory PBH dark matter model
members.description: The PBH collapse threshold and mass-function mapping are uncalibrated for horizon re-entry during or after kination (w near 1), yet f_PBH is exponentially sensitive to the assumed threshold.
members.proposed_resolution: Run numerical-relativity or Misner-Sharp collapse simulations of super-horizon perturbations in a kination-dominated background to calibrate delta_c(w) and the critical-collapse mass relation, then feed the calibrated threshold into the Press-Schechter/peaks mass-function step.

members.model_name: Primordial black hole dark matter from EEFToI dispersion enhancement
members.description: The mapping from the enhanced (oscillatory) P_R(k) to a PBH mass function relies on a collapse threshold and monochromatic approximation that are uncalibrated for this spectrum shape; the card flags that a broad or oscillatory mass function changes the relevant integrated limits.
members.proposed_resolution: Apply a peaks-theory plus critical-collapse pipeline with a shape-dependent threshold (calibrated from published numerical-relativity collapse results) to the actual EEFToI spectrum, producing an extended mass function beta(M) and f_PBH(M) rather than a monochromatic estimate.

members.model_name: PBH-remnant dark matter from kination/runaway-quintessence production
members.description: The PBH formation threshold and collapse fraction during kination domination (w=1) are not calibrated by simulations; since the remnant abundance is exponentially sensitive to the curvature tail and threshold, the beta(P_R, w) mapping in step s2 carries order-of-magnitude uncertainty.
members.proposed_resolution: Run numerical-relativity collapse simulations of superhorizon curvature perturbations in a stiff-fluid (w=1) background to fit the threshold delta_c(w) and shape dependence, then insert the calibrated threshold into the Press-Schechter/peaks beta calculation, including non-Gaussian tail corrections for the attractor-potential spike.

members.model_name: PBH-remnant dark matter from matter-era mini-PBH production
members.description: The mini-PBH formation efficiency during the early matter-dominated (pressureless) era is not calibrated: the beta(P_R) mapping in step s2 relies on semianalytic collapse statistics whose anisotropy and angular-momentum suppression factors are uncertain by orders of magnitude, and the card notes the abundance is exponentially sensitive to the curvature tail.
members.proposed_resolution: Run N-body/numerical-relativity simulations of nonspherical collapse in a pressureless post-inflationary background to calibrate the matter-era formation fraction (anisotropy and spin suppression) as a function of the spike amplitude and duration of the matter era, and package the fit as a drop-in beta(P_R, w=0) function for the abundance calculation.

members.model_name: PBH-remnant dark matter from radiation-era mini-PBH production
members.description: The P_R(k)-to-beta step has no calibrated treatment of the collapse threshold and non-Gaussian high-sigma tail for radiation-era mini-PBH formation from an attractor-inflation spike, and beta is exponentially sensitive to these choices.
members.proposed_resolution: Calibrate delta_c and the tail statistics for this spike class using peak theory plus existing numerical-relativity collapse results, and package the result as a beta(P_R; w) calculator with quantified threshold and non-Gaussianity uncertainty bands.

members.model_name: Primordial black hole dark matter from step-feature single-field inflation
members.description: The PBH abundance mapping uses Gaussian Press-Schechter statistics with an assumed delta_c, while the card notes non-Gaussian tails can shift f_PBH by orders of magnitude for these sharp oscillatory spectra; no calibrated threshold/statistics prescription exists for this feature class.
members.proposed_resolution: Calibrate the collapse threshold and abundance statistics for oscillatory step-feature spectra using peaks theory with the model's full power spectrum shape and numerical-relativity threshold results for the corresponding compaction-function profiles, replacing the fixed delta_c = 0.45 Gaussian mapping.

members.model_name: VAS supergravity a4 quartic-superpotential asteroid PBH dark matter
members.description: The PBH abundance is computed with radiation-era Gaussian Press-Schechter statistics and a fixed threshold delta_c=0.45, which is uncalibrated for the non-Gaussian, USR-enhanced spectra this model produces; the card itself notes non-Gaussianity or different collapse thresholds can strongly change f_PBH.
members.proposed_resolution: Recompute f_PBH(M) with a peak-statistics or compaction-function treatment including the USR non-Gaussianity of this potential, using threshold values calibrated on numerical-relativity critical-collapse results for the benchmark's peaked P_R(k) shape.

members.model_name: VAS supergravity b3 quartic-superpotential asteroid PBH dark matter
members.description: The PBH abundance is computed with radiation-era Gaussian Press-Schechter statistics and a fixed threshold delta_c=0.45, which is uncalibrated for the non-Gaussian, USR-enhanced spectra this model produces; the card itself notes non-Gaussianity or different collapse thresholds can strongly change f_PBH.
members.proposed_resolution: Recompute f_PBH(M) with a peak-statistics or compaction-function treatment including the USR non-Gaussianity of this potential, using threshold values calibrated on numerical-relativity critical-collapse results for the benchmark's peaked P_R(k) shape.

members.model_name: PBH dark-matter subcomponent from running-index inflation in radiation domination
members.description: The abundance-to-merger-rate translation depends on an assumed binary-formation and survival prescription; clustering and disruption effects that the card flags as dominating the interpretation are uncalibrated for this narrow-peak mass function.
members.proposed_resolution: Run N-body simulations of early-forming PBH binaries embedded in the model's predicted clustering environment to calibrate disruption-corrected merger efficiency, and propagate the correction as a systematic band on f_PBH^LIGO.

members.model_name: Conformal hidden-QCD dark meson model
members.description: The finite-temperature NJL condensate-plus-singlet effective potential and the iterative O(3) bounce calculation that yield S3/T, T_n, alpha, and beta/H are not packaged in any public code, so the GW spectrum and DECIGO/BBO SNR cannot be recomputed away from the two quoted benchmarks.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the paper's V_eff(S, sigma, T) in CosmoTransitions or BubbleProfiler, compute the bounce action and nucleation temperature over (lambda_S, lambda_HS, y_i, Lambda_H), and chain to standard sound-wave GW formulae with the finite sound-wave-lifetime correction, validating against the BP1/BP2 beta/H and SNR values.

members.model_name: First-order phase-transition rescued self-interacting fermion dark matter
members.description: The dark-sector finite-temperature potential (singlet FOPT scalar plus assisting complex scalar) is not implemented in any named phase-transition solver, so alpha, beta/H, and T_RH for the MeV-scale transition cannot yet be scanned.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the model's finite-temperature effective potential in CosmoTransitions (or PhaseTracer) to compute nucleation temperature, alpha, and beta/H over the parameter space, checking the BBN/CMB-safe benchmark conditions.

members.model_name: Neutrinophilic singlet dark matter DS_M1
members.description: No dark-sector thermal-history solver covers the singlet phase-transition timing and the BBN/recombination light-species bookkeeping for the keV-scale S and phi/a states, leaving the bbn_cmb_singlet_mass_constraint and dark_phase_transition_timing checks qualitative.
members.proposed_resolution: Analyze the singlet scalar potential with CosmoTransitions to bound the phase-transition temperature, and track the light-singlet energy density through neutrino decoupling with a coupled dark-sector temperature evolution code to compute Delta N_eff at BBN and recombination for comparison with Planck/BBN limits.

members.model_name: Fermion-mediated dark matter from bubble expansion
members.description: No released implementation of the singlet-assisted electroweak finite-temperature effective potential with bounce/nucleation calculation plus bubble-wall friction exists for this model, so T_nuc, transition strength, and whether the wall reaches the ultra-relativistic branch cannot be computed, and everything downstream depends on these outputs.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the SM + real singlet finite-temperature potential in CosmoTransitions (or a modern equivalent bounce solver), add the leading-order and NLO friction pressure terms to solve for gamma_w, and validate against the paper's benchmark table of nucleation temperatures and wall regimes.

members.model_name: Recycled ultra-heavy dark matter
members.description: No public calculator exists for false-vacuum pocket statistics, particle trapping, and the filtered relic fraction in a dark-sector first-order phase transition; the paper relies on a custom semi-analytic pocket model.
members.proposed_resolution: Build a public FOPT pocket/trapping module on top of CosmoTransitions-style bubble-nucleation output, parameterized by m/T_*, bubble-wall velocity, and portal thermal-contact rate, outputting trapped and filtered fractions.

members.model_name: Stiff-era scalar field dark matter for electroweak baryogenesis
members.description: No tool computes the actual baryon yield for electroweak baryogenesis in a nonstandard stiff-era expansion history: the route only checks the sphaleron washout condition with enhanced H(T), and existing EWBG transport/sphaleron-rate codes assume radiation-dominated expansion.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend a finite-temperature EWPT pipeline (CosmoTransitions for the |H|^6 potential plus standard transport equations for the CP-violating source) to take an arbitrary H(T) from the SFDM background integrator, outputting the surviving baryon asymmetry and the washout factor as functions of (Lambda, rho_sfdm/rho_rad).

members.model_name: Z3-conserving NMSSM neutralino cosmology scenario
members.description: No public implementation of the Z3-conserving NMSSM finite-temperature effective potential exists for evaluating the strong first-order electroweak phase transition criterion used by the source scan; the finite-temperature step is only a private source calculation.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the scale-invariant Z3 NMSSM one-loop daisy-resummed finite-temperature potential in CosmoTransitions or PhaseTracer, validate against the paper's F(gamma)=0 / baryon-washout criterion, and couple it to the NMSSMTools spectrum scan.

members.model_name: ALP-triggered supercooled-phase-transition primordial black hole dark matter
members.description: No implementation exists of the supercooled ALP-sector phase-transition dynamics: the model's finite-temperature Coleman-Weinberg potential, bubble nucleation rate, beta/H, transition strength, and reheating temperature over the (f_a, g) plane are not computable outside the paper.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the radiative U(1)-breaking scalar potential with the SU(2) gauge-sector running in CosmoTransitions (or a bespoke bounce solver for the near-conformal flat direction) and output nucleation/percolation parameters and T_RH on an (f_a, g) grid.

members.model_name: Higgs-portal dark matter from relativistic bubble expansion
members.description: No released implementation of the singlet-assisted electroweak finite-temperature effective potential with bounce/nucleation calculation plus bubble-wall friction exists for this model, so T_nuc, transition strength, and access to the tuned fast-wall branch cannot be computed, and all downstream observables depend on these outputs.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the SM + real singlet finite-temperature potential in CosmoTransitions (or an equivalent modern bounce solver), add friction pressure terms to solve for gamma_w, and validate against the paper's benchmark nucleation temperatures and wall regimes.

members.model_name: Classically scale-invariant SU(2)_X vector dark matter
members.description: No public, model-specific pipeline exists for the conformal SU(2)_X RG-improved effective potential, bounce action, and percolation/reheating viability check; the card records no associated code and notes the numerical potential/bounce machinery was not run, so T_p, transition completion, and the GW spectrum inputs cannot be recomputed.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the SU(2)_X + scalar doublet model in CosmoTransitions or PhaseTracer with the RG-improved one-loop finite-temperature potential, add the percolation-temperature and reheating-completion criteria from the primary analysis, and output (T_p, alpha, beta/H) for the GW template stage; validate against the primary paper's percolation-restricted parameter space.

members.model_name: Supercool radiative-symmetry-breaking phase-transition PBH dark matter
members.description: No public implementation of the classically scale-invariant U(1)_D effective potential with the non-minimal gravitational coupling exists to compute the nucleation action, T_n, alpha, and beta/H_n for the supercooled transition; all transition thermodynamics currently come from the source paper.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the one-loop Coleman-Weinberg plus thermal U(1)_D potential including the xi phi^2 R term in CosmoTransitions (or FindBounce), and validate the bounce-action tracking through deep supercooling against the paper's benchmark region.

members.model_name: FOPT-enabled forbidden-decay scotogenic right-handed-neutrino dark matter
members.description: No public implementation of the scotogenic inert-doublet one-loop finite-temperature effective potential with an FOPT scan producing T_n, T_s, alpha, and beta/H, which every route in the card starts from.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the inert-doublet plus RHN finite-temperature potential in CosmoTransitions (or an equivalent bounce/nucleation code), scan for T_n < 34 GeV with T_s > T_Sph > T_n, and export alpha and beta/H for the GW pipeline; validate against the paper's benchmark points.

members.model_name: Z_3 pseudo-Goldstone complex-singlet dark matter
members.description: No public implementation of the Z3 complex-singlet finite-temperature effective potential (including the mu_3 cubic soft-breaking term and the two-step transition pattern) exists in a phase-transition scanner, so v_c/T_c, alpha, and beta/H cannot be recomputed for new parameter points.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the Z3 complex-singlet scalar potential with one-loop and daisy-resummed thermal corrections in CosmoTransitions or PhaseTracer, validate against the paper's strong two-step EWPT benchmarks (m_S ~ 1-2 TeV, |theta| > 0.2), and expose alpha and beta/H as outputs.

members.model_name: SU(2)_X supercooled vector dark matter sudden-freeze-out model
members.description: No numerical finite-temperature effective-potential and bounce-action implementation exists for the SU(2)_X Coleman-Weinberg potential; the card's transition parameters (T_n, T_end, alpha, beta/H_*) rest on benchmark-level analytic formulae whose wall-dynamics and reheating uncertainties dominate the error budget.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the two-doublet H-S scalar potential with SU(2)_X gauge corrections in CosmoTransitions (or an equivalent bounce solver such as BubbleProfiler), scanning g_X, lambda_HS, lambda_S to output T_n, alpha, beta/H_* over the supercooled regime.

members.model_name: Dark SU(2)_D neutron-decay freeze-in dark matter
members.description: The SU(2)_D finite-temperature phase transition has no solver implementation: transition temperature, alpha, and beta/H needed for quantitative stochastic GW spectra are not computable from the card's assets (tool named only as CosmoTransitions-style).
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the SU(2)_D scalar potential with gauge-boson thermal corrections in CosmoTransitions or PhaseTracer, extract (T_n, alpha, beta/H) across (g_D, lambda, v_D), and feed the standard FOPT GW templates to recover the primary benchmark GW regions.

members.model_name: Low-scale darkogenesis with perturbative baryon transfer
members.description: No quantitative calculation of the dark-number asymmetry from the first-order SU(2)_D phase transition exists; the CP-violating bubble-wall dynamics and dark-sphaleron washout are treated only by analytic requirements, with no transport-equation code for the hidden sector.
members.proposed_resolution: Adapt electroweak-baryogenesis tooling to the dark sector: derive the finite-temperature dark Higgs potential and bubble-wall profile with CosmoTransitions and solve CP-violating transport equations for the dark doublets to predict the asymmetry versus dark couplings and wall velocity.

members.model_name: First-order phase-transition Friedberg-Lee-Sirlin Q-ball dark matter
members.description: Nucleation rates and the transition temperature rest on thin-wall, fast-transition analytic approximations; the model's one-loop finite-temperature potential has not been implemented in a numerical bounce solver, which the card flags by listing a phase-transition solver as a missing required code resource.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the FLS scalar potential with its one-loop thermal corrections in CosmoTransitions (or an equivalent bounce solver) to compute S_3/T, the nucleation temperature, and transition strength across the quoted m_phi ~ 3e2-1e4 GeV, T_c ~ 1e3-3e4 GeV region, replacing the thin-wall estimates.

members.model_name: Gauged lepton-number dark-sector CP-violating fermion dark matter
members.description: No public code computes the dark-sector electroweak-baryogenesis chain for this model: a first-order phase-transition profile with the U(1)_L-breaking scalar sector coupled to the CP-violating chi_L (m0 + lambda_c S) chi_R source, plus the transport equations that convert the dark chiral asymmetry into a baryon asymmetry through the Z-prime background.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the two-scalar (Phi, S, H) finite-temperature potential in CosmoTransitions to obtain the bubble-wall profile, then code the model's semi-analytic CP-source and transport equations (as written in the primary paper) as a wrapper that outputs the dark chiral asymmetry for given (lambda_c, eta, wall parameters).

members.model_name: Two-component WIMP-FIMP scalar dark matter with U(1) L_mu-L_tau
members.description: The finite-temperature phase-transition analysis relied on a modified, non-public version of CosmoTransitions; the multi-scalar effective potential of this U(1)_{L_mu-L_tau} model is not implemented in any public phase-transition code, so (T_n, alpha, beta/H) cannot be recomputed.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the model's one-loop finite-temperature effective potential (SM Higgs, U(1) Higgs phi_H, spectator dark scalars at zero VEV) in public CosmoTransitions or PhaseTracer and validate the nucleation parameters against the paper's benchmark GW spectra.

members.model_name: Hidden self-interacting Dirac dark matter with scalar-mediated first-order phase transition
members.description: No phase-transition calculator handles the hidden-sector first-order transition with an independent dark temperature (hidden-to-visible ratio xi) entering nucleation, alpha, and beta/H; existing public codes assume the transitioning sector shares the visible-sector temperature.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend CosmoTransitions or PhaseTracer to evaluate the effective potential and nucleation rate at a dark temperature T_d = xi*T, propagating xi into the Hubble rate and the alpha and beta/H definitions for the GW template.

members.model_name: GeV-scale mixed sneutrino dark matter with Dirac neutrinos
members.description: The vacuum-metastability bound on the large A_nu trilinear is not reproducible: the sneutrino-direction scalar potential and its bounce action are not implemented in any public tunneling code, so the key companion constraint on (A_nu, theta, m_snu1) rests on the unverified source calculation.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the MSSM-plus-right-handed-sneutrino scalar potential along the lepton-number-violating direction in CosmoTransitions or Vevacious, compute the Euclidean bounce action across the (A_nu, theta, m_snu1) plane, and validate against the source metastability boundary.

members.model_name: Two-scalar Z2 Higgs-portal dark matter without singlet-only s-s' cross-couplings
members.description: No public finite-temperature effective-potential implementation exists for this two-singlet potential: the scenario-d1 transition scan (T_c, v_c/T_c across the three-field space of extrema) was done with unreleased source code, and higher-order thermal corrections beyond the one-loop treatment are not implemented anywhere for this model.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the three-field (h, s, s') one-loop daisy-resummed thermal potential in CosmoTransitions (or PhaseTracer), reproduce the source scenario classification and v_c/T_c benchmarks, and optionally add dimensional-reduction corrections for robustness.

members.model_name: Scale-free electroweak-baryogenesis singlino dark matter
members.description: No public implementation of the high-scale nMSSM plus vector-like-multiplet finite-temperature effective potential exists, so the strongly first-order phase transition (phi/T > 0.9 benchmark region, bounce action, bubble-wall width) cannot be recomputed or scanned beyond the paper's simplified treatment.
members.proposed_resolution: Code the one-loop plus daisy-resummed thermal potential of the Higgs-singlet-vector-like sector into CosmoTransitions (or an equivalent bounce solver), scan (M_SUSY, lambda, k, charged-Higgs mass), and recover the phi/T > 0.9 benchmark region.

members.model_name: SUSY SU(2)_H confinement model with Z2- and R-parity dark matter
members.description: The claimed strong first-order electroweak phase transition (phi_c/T_c > 1) that underpins the benchmark and its triple-Higgs-coupling signature has no finite-temperature effective-potential implementation for this extended Higgs sector.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the mesonic extended-Higgs scalar potential in CosmoTransitions (or an equivalent finite-temperature effective-potential code) to compute phi_c/T_c across the parameter space and correlate it with the loop-induced lambda_hhh and Higgs-coupling shifts.

members.model_name: Extremely supercooled singlet scalar dark matter
members.description: No reproducible public pipeline computes the phase-transition history of this model in the extreme-supercooling regime: the required per-mille tuning of lambda_hs near the degenerate-phase line, high-precision bounce-action tracking, and a percolation (rather than nucleation) completion criterion at T_p of order 1 GeV are beyond the released configurations of generic tools like CosmoTransitions, and no model-specific code was published.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend a public bounce solver (CosmoTransitions or a DRalgo-matched dimensionally-reduced setup) with adaptive-precision action evaluation near the conformal limit, an explicit false-vacuum-fraction percolation criterion, and completion/reheating bookkeeping, releasing the xSM model files and benchmark scans (including the lambda_hs = 1.9694 benchmark) for validation.

members.model_name: Two-real-singlet light scalar dark matter
members.description: The strong first-order electroweak phase transition is established only with the source paper's mean-field tree-level-barrier treatment; no finite-temperature effective-potential calculation (daisy-resummed one-loop, gauge-consistent) exists for this two-singlet potential, so v_c/T_c cannot be evaluated reliably across parameter space.
members.proposed_resolution: Encode the two-singlet finite-temperature effective potential in CosmoTransitions (or an equivalent transition-finder) with one-loop Coleman-Weinberg and daisy corrections, and recompute v_c/T_c over the paper's viable points to test the mean-field strong-transition claim.

members.model_name: Two-state unified superfluid dark sector
members.description: No public galaxy-scale solver computes the superfluid condensate profile plus the phonon-mediated force for realistic baryon distributions, so the MOND-like radial acceleration relation prediction cannot be evaluated beyond the deep-phonon-limit analytic estimate, nor across the superfluid/normal-phase transition in clusters.
members.proposed_resolution: Build a nonlinear Poisson-plus-phonon boundary-value solver (axisymmetric, taking SPARC-like baryonic mass models as input) that solves the P(X) phonon equation with baryon coupling alpha and the condensate density profile, outputting rotation curves and the RAR for given (m, Lambda, alpha).

members.model_name: Dimension-six extended-inverse-seesaw Majoron dark matter
members.description: No public implementation of the dimension-six extended-inverse-seesaw Majoron finite-temperature effective potential exists for phase-transition tracing; the CosmoTransitions setup used by the paper is not released, so alpha_PT, beta/H, and the GW spectrum cannot be recomputed across (v_sigma, Lambda, m_h2).
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the one-loop daisy-resummed thermal potential including the lepton-number-preserving dimension-six scalar operators in CosmoTransitions or PhaseTracer, validate against the paper's plotted v_sigma-Lambda transition regions, and release it with benchmark input files.

members.model_name: Trapped-vacuum-bubble primordial black hole dark matter
members.description: The spherical field-evolution code that classifies subcritical versus supercritical trapped vacuum bubbles and sets the bubble-formation threshold is private to the authors; no packaged tool exists to recompute thresholds and comoving bubble sizes for other barrier potentials.
members.proposed_resolution: Obtain and release the paper's spherical inflaton-field evolution code, or reimplement a 1+1D spherically symmetric scalar-field solver on an FRW background with the paper's barrier potential and validate against the published critical-amplitude and f_NL~2.6 transition results.

members.model_name: Heavy-scalar-decay non-thermal warm dark matter
members.description: The combined Milky Way satellite (DES/Pan-STARRS1) plus strong-lensing flux-ratio likelihood that produces the m_nonthermal >= 107 keV bound is not packaged for direct use with this model's nonthermal transfer functions; only the thermal-equivalent WDM mapping connects the modified-CLASS output to the published limits.
members.proposed_resolution: Interface the modified-CLASS T(k) output with the public MW satellite likelihood (Nadler et al. DES+PS1 framework) and a lensing flux-ratio substructure likelihood, parameterized by half-mode mass or directly by the nonthermal T(k), so the 107 keV bound can be rerun and updated without the thermal-relic detour.

members.model_name: Two-state inelastic self-interacting dark matter
members.description: No public likelihood exists connecting the model's predictions (density profiles, subhalo Vmax functions, local speed distribution) to data; the card lists only 'profile and subhalo summary-statistic likelihoods; no public full likelihood identified' and the elastic-SIDM constraint set explicitly requires recasting for inelastic scattering.
members.proposed_resolution: Build an emulator of core sizes, central densities, and subhalo Vmax functions over (sigma/m, Delta/m_chi, f_excited) from the simulation grid and couple it to existing Milky Way satellite and dwarf-kinematics likelihoods, replacing the elastic-equivalent recast factor with a direct inelastic-parameter constraint.

members.model_name: Non-resonantly produced sterile-neutrino mixed dark matter
members.description: No public spectral likelihood exists for the XMM-Newton/Chandra 3.5 keV line searches; mixing-angle constraints on the sterile subcomponent must be reconstructed from published flux limits and rescaled by r_warm.
members.proposed_resolution: Reconstruct a line-search likelihood from published X-ray flux limits and stacked spectra for the standard targets (clusters, M31, Milky Way satellites), parameterized in line energy and flux so it rescales trivially with the sterile fraction r_warm.

members.model_name: Dissipative dark matter from multiple Standard Model sectors
members.description: No likelihood pipeline maps dissipative-halo predictions onto small-scale-structure data (Milky Way satellite counts, field velocity function, halo structure), so the small_scale_halo_phenomenology comparison remains pass/fail by eye.
members.proposed_resolution: Adapt existing Milky Way satellite likelihoods (DES plus Pan-STARRS style) and velocity-function datasets to consume the suppressed low-mass halo function and dissipative profiles produced by the steady-state solver or simulations, exposing N_sec and epsilon as likelihood parameters.

members.model_name: Simplified light FIMP with entropy-modified decay production
members.description: The Milky Way/M31 satellite constraint is applied as a hard semi-analytic threshold N_sat > 63 with an assumed subhalo-to-galaxy occupation, not as a probabilistic likelihood, so the exclusion boundary carries unquantified galaxy-formation systematics.
members.proposed_resolution: Recast the published DES+PS1 Milky Way satellite likelihood (which marginalizes over the galaxy-halo connection) onto the FIMP alpha-beta-gamma transfer-function parameterization instead of the thermal-WDM mass axis.

members.model_name: Simplified light FIMP with decay and scattering production
members.description: The Milky Way/M31 satellite constraint is applied as a hard semi-analytic threshold N_sat > 63 with an assumed subhalo-to-galaxy occupation, not as a probabilistic likelihood, so the exclusion boundary carries unquantified galaxy-formation systematics.
members.proposed_resolution: Recast the published DES+PS1 Milky Way satellite likelihood (which marginalizes over the galaxy-halo connection) onto the FIMP alpha-beta-gamma transfer-function parameterization instead of the thermal-WDM mass axis.

members.model_name: Exothermic Yukawa-potential interacting dark matter
members.description: No likelihood connects exothermic-YIDM parameters to Milky Way satellite counts or cluster consistency: existing satellite-abundance likelihoods are built for power-spectrum-suppression models, not for late-time evaporation of already-formed low-mass halos.
members.proposed_resolution: Once simulation-calibrated evaporation predictions exist, map them into the DES/Pan-STARRS Milky Way satellite likelihood framework via a modified subhalo-disruption term, and add cluster-scale sigma/m bounds evaluated at high velocities as a joint constraint.

members.model_name: Entropy-diluted light gravitino warm dark matter
members.description: The Milky Way satellite constraint is applied only as a conservative N_sat >= 63 counting criterion; no satellite-abundance likelihood is wired to the diluted-gravitino transfer function, and newer DES/PS1-based counts that would tighten the bound are not incorporated.
members.proposed_resolution: Map the diluted mixed-DM transfer function to a suppressed subhalo mass function via calibrated half-mode scaling and evaluate it in a Nadler-style DES/PS1 satellite likelihood (galaxy-halo connection marginalized), replacing the fixed N_sat >= 63 threshold with a proper posterior on (m_3/2, f_3/2, Delta).

members.model_name: U(1) late-decaying dark matter
members.description: The dwarf-halo kick-lifetime window has no likelihood (likelihood_available: no) — viability is judged by eye against cited simulation papers — and the cosmological invisible-decay constraint is only partially covered by recasts of decaying-DM analyses that are not exact U(1) pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone implementations.
members.proposed_resolution: Combine an existing two-body decaying-DM Boltzmann implementation (public CLASS decaying-DM extensions with mass splitting) with Planck plus matter-power/weak-lensing likelihoods, and add a Milky Way satellite-count/stellar-kinematics likelihood over the emulated halo response, parameterized in (epsilon, tau_chi_star, decayed fraction).

members.model_name: Low-reheat Standard Model neutrino warm dark matter
members.description: No matter-power, Ly-alpha, or substructure likelihood exists that accepts the low-reheat nonthermal neutrino T(k); the card marks con_low_reheat_matter_power as likelihood_available: no with recasting_needed: yes, and thermal-WDM mass bounds cannot be applied directly to this distribution.
members.proposed_resolution: Recast an existing Ly-alpha or Milky Way satellite-count likelihood in terms of a generalized transfer-function parameterization (e.g. alpha-beta-gamma fits) and map the low-reheat neutrino T(k) onto it, rather than through invalid thermal-WDM mass equivalents.

members.model_name: Leptophilic Sommerfeld-enhanced WIMP toy model
members.description: No likelihood exists that confronts the model's predicted sub-Earth-to-stellar-mass protohalo cutoff and its velocity-dependent scalar/pseudoscalar self-interaction with data: existing MW-satellite, stream, and lensing likelihoods probe halo masses far above the predicted M_cut range, and SIDM halo-structure bounds require a mediator-specific transfer-cross-section recast not packaged anywhere.
members.proposed_resolution: Build a recast layer that maps (m_chi, m_s, m_p, couplings) to sigma_T/m over dwarf-to-cluster velocities for spin-0 mediator exchange and evaluates it against published SIDM constraint surfaces, and couple the predicted M_cut to minihalo-sensitive probes (pulsar timing, photometric microlensing, and annihilation-boost limits from Fermi dwarf likelihoods) in one composite likelihood.

members.model_name: Z4 late-decaying dark matter
members.description: No public structure-formation likelihood exists for two-parameter late-decay kick models (v_kick from epsilon ~ 1e-5, tau ~ 1-10 Gyr): the dwarf-halo kick/lifetime window and the weak-lensing decay forecasts on the card are target regions and forecasts, not evaluable likelihoods (likelihood_available: no for both).
members.proposed_resolution: Build a (v_kick, tau) decaying-dark-matter likelihood from Milky Way satellite counts and subhalo mass functions (extending existing DES/PS1 satellite likelihood machinery) and wrap the published weak-lensing DDM forecast chains into a reusable likelihood module.

members.model_name: Effective neutrinophilic dark matter with late kinetic decoupling
members.description: No likelihood connects the predicted protohalo cutoff mass M_cut to observed small-scale-structure data; the card flags the missing-satellites interpretation as astrophysical with no direct particle-physics likelihood, and the route lists an empty likelihoods block.
members.proposed_resolution: Adapt an existing Milky Way satellite-count likelihood (DES/Pan-STARRS satellite census with a subhalo-population forward model) to accept a smooth-cutoff transfer function parameterized by M_cut, so the neutrinophilic suppression can be statistically confronted with data rather than compared to a qualitative missing-satellites target.

members.model_name: Two temperature dark matter (2TDM)
members.description: The Milky Way satellite-count constraint requires a subhalo-abundance likelihood with galaxy-halo connection and survey-completeness modeling; the card marks it only partially available, calibrated on WDM-like half-mode recasts rather than the 2TDM two-scale cutoff, and the likelihood assets were not run.
members.proposed_resolution: Adapt a public Milky Way satellite likelihood (DES+Pan-STARRS-type analysis with a calibrated galaxy-halo connection) to consume the 2TDM transfer function directly, mapping its two-scale suppression onto the subhalo mass function instead of the single half-mode-scale k_hm proxy.

members.model_name: Two-component cold dark matter with self-heated light component
members.description: The MCVF comparison is benchmark-level: no likelihood connects the simulated subhalo N(>V_max) to observed Milky Way satellite counts, and baryonic-feedback and halo-profile systematics were explicitly left untreated.
members.proposed_resolution: Adapt an existing Milky Way satellite likelihood (subhalo mass function conditioned on suppressed P(k), including a disk-disruption and galaxy-halo connection model) to this model's transfer functions, calibrated with a small suite of zoom-in simulations including baryonic corrections.

members.model_name: Multi-ultralight-axion mixed dark matter
members.description: No strong-lensing or stellar-stream subhalo likelihood is available recast for the multi-ULA halo/subhalo mass function; the cited exclusions near 2.1e-21 eV assume a single all-DM ULDM transfer function.
members.proposed_resolution: Recast public subhalo mass-function likelihoods from strong-lensing flux ratios and stellar-stream gap statistics in terms of the computed multi-ULA halo mass function, parameterized by the effective mass m_e and fraction f_12 instead of a single-ULA cutoff.

members.model_name: ETHOS-4 interacting dark-matter dark-radiation benchmark
members.description: No Milky Way satellite population likelihood exists for ETHOS-4: the missing-satellites and too-big-to-fail assessment is a qualitative comparison of simulated subhalo V_max functions with dwarf kinematics, so the benchmark's viability cannot be stated with confidence intervals in the (a4, r_DAO/r_SD, sigma_T/m_chi) space.
members.proposed_resolution: Couple the ETHOS-suppressed subhalo mass function (parameterized by the DAO/damping cutoff plus a velocity-dependent SIDM core response) to an existing satellite forward-modeling likelihood of the DES/PS1 type, calibrating the subhalo suppression and V_max modification on the existing ETHOS zoom simulations.

members.model_name: ETHOS-1 interacting dark-matter dark-radiation benchmark
members.description: The Milky Way satellite abundance and too-big-to-fail comparison is qualitative: no statistical likelihood connects ETHOS-1 predictions (subhalo V_max function, core densities) to MW satellite counts and kinematics, so the benchmark's viability cannot be quantified or combined with other constraints.
members.proposed_resolution: Adapt an existing MW satellite population likelihood (e.g. the DES/PS1 satellite-count framework with a subhalo-to-satellite connection model) to take ETHOS-1 subhalo mass/V_max functions as input, including a suppression parameterization calibrated on the zoom simulations.

members.model_name: Higgs-portal self-interacting dark matter with light scalar mediator
members.description: No halo-scale likelihood exists for the joint dwarf-core and cluster-shape SIDM constraint (likelihood_available: no); viability is judged against order-of-magnitude sigma_T/m bands without baryonic or halo-modeling systematics.
members.proposed_resolution: Build a likelihood from isothermal-Jeans SIDM halo modeling calibrated on existing SIDM N-body simulations, covering dwarf spheroidal kinematics, Milky Way satellite densities, and cluster shape/merger constraints as a function of sigma_T/m(v).

members.model_name: ETHOS-2 interacting dark-matter dark-radiation benchmark
members.description: The Milky Way satellite abundance and too-big-to-fail comparison is qualitative: no statistical likelihood connects ETHOS-2 predictions (subhalo V_max function, core densities) to MW satellite counts and kinematics, so the benchmark's viability cannot be quantified or combined with other constraints.
members.proposed_resolution: Adapt an existing MW satellite population likelihood (e.g. the DES/PS1 satellite-count framework with a subhalo-to-satellite connection model) to take ETHOS-2 subhalo mass/V_max functions as input, including a suppression parameterization calibrated on the zoom simulations.

members.model_name: ETHOS-3 interacting dark-matter dark-radiation benchmark
members.description: No likelihood exists for the Milky Way satellite abundance / too-big-to-fail comparison (likelihood_available: no) or for the cluster self-interaction consistency check; both are qualitative viability assessments requiring recasting.
members.proposed_resolution: Adapt an existing MW satellite population likelihood (e.g. the DES/PS1 satellite-count likelihood with a subhalo model conditioned on the ETHOS cutoff and SIDM core formation) and a cluster sigma_T/m constraint module, so satellite counts and kinematics constrain (a4, r_DAO, sigma_T/m_chi) statistically.

members.model_name: Neutrino self-interaction assisted sterile-neutrino freeze-in dark matter
members.description: The Milky Way satellite constraint can only be applied through an approximate mapping of the model's transfer-function cutoff onto thermal-relic WDM half-mode bounds; no direct satellite likelihood evaluation using the model's actual transfer function exists, and the mapping fails if the cutoff shape departs from WDM-like.
members.proposed_resolution: Run the model-specific P(k) from CLASS through a public DES/Pan-STARRS1 Milky Way satellite likelihood (Nadler-et-al-style subhalo-abundance framework), replacing the k_hm-to-thermal-WDM proxy with a direct evaluation over the (m4, sin^2(2 theta), m_phi, lambda) space.

members.model_name: Charged scalar field dark matter with dark photon
members.description: No likelihood pipeline exists for either constraint: Ly-alpha/satellite limits are only available as thermal-WDM templates that the card says must not be applied directly, and no Fermi-Bubble/gamma-ray likelihood with astrophysical foreground modeling is interfaced to the model.
members.proposed_resolution: Recast Ly-alpha and Milky-Way satellite likelihoods through the charged-SFDM transfer function once gap_1 closes (e.g. via area-criterion or emulator-based transfer-function matching), and interface a gamma-ray sky likelihood with Fermi-Bubble templates for the emission channel.

members.model_name: Cosmic-ray boosted sub-GeV gravitationally interacting dark matter with a spin-2 mediator
members.description: The mapping from generic light-mediator CRDM bounds (Borexino, Super-K, LZ) to the spin-2 GIDM couplings is flagged as recast_required: no derived translation of those complementary constraints into (m_G, c_SM/Lambda, c_DM/Lambda) space exists, leaving the benchmark's overall viability unquantified.
members.proposed_resolution: Derive the spin-2-specific visible final states and coupling combinations probed by Borexino, Super-K, and meson-decay constraints, and recast the published light-mediator CRDM limits into the model's (m_chi, m_G, Lambda) plane instead of quoting generic mediator bounds.

members.model_name: Asymmetric dark matter with Chern-Simons photon-current coupling
members.description: The loop-induced ADM-quark interaction from the dimension-six current-photon Chern-Simons operator has only an order-of-magnitude heavy-mediator estimate with simplified quark-charge/log factors; no dedicated loop-level matching and RG running to nuclear-recoil operators exists, so the claimed LZ exclusion of the 5 GeV benchmark is low-robustness.
members.proposed_resolution: Compute the one-loop matching of J_mu A_nu Ftilde/M^2 onto quark-level effective operators, run them to the nuclear scale with standard DM EFT running tools (e.g. runDM/DirectDM), and evaluate the recoil rate against the LZ exposure with a standard direct-detection rate code.

members.model_name: Dissipative dark matter from multiple Standard Model sectors
members.description: The local dark-plasma phase-space distribution at Earth, including detector shielding and dark-metal composition, has not been derived, and without it kinetic-mixing direct-detection rates cannot be computed from standard Maxwellian halo assumptions.
members.proposed_resolution: Derive the local dark-plasma density, temperature, and velocity distribution from the steady-state halo solution, model dark-electromagnetic shielding and capture by the Earth for epsilon~1e-10, and feed the resulting flux into standard nuclear/electronic recoil-rate codes with detector-specific efficiencies.

members.model_name: Z3 semi-annihilating inert scalar multiplet model
members.description: In the viable regions where tree-level Higgs/Z exchange is suppressed by hypercharge and CP-composition choices, the direct-detection signal is dominated by electroweak loop-level scattering, which is not calculated in the paper or available in standard tools for this multiplet content, so the direct-detection observable cannot be quantitatively evaluated precisely where the model lives.
members.proposed_resolution: Adapt the known electroweak-loop direct-detection calculations for minimal SU(2)_L multiplets (Hisano et al. style effective nucleon couplings) to the phi1/phi2 mixed neutral states, tabulate sigma_SI(m_DM, n_i, Delta m), and feed the result to DDCalc for XENON/LZ likelihood evaluation.

members.model_name: Dark anti-neutron asymmetric dark matter
members.description: The dark anti-neutron electric dipole moment coefficient g, which controls the entire direct-detection cross section, exists only as an O(1) tree-level estimate; no dark-QCD calculation (lattice or chiral effective theory) of the EDM induced by the dark vacuum angle has been performed for this confining dark sector.
members.proposed_resolution: Compute the dark-neutron EDM as a function of the dark vacuum angle and dark-quark masses by rescaling existing SM lattice-QCD nucleon-EDM results to the dark confinement scale, or by a dedicated dark chiral-perturbation-theory derivation, and publish g with a quantified uncertainty band.

members.model_name: Dark matter pearl vacuum-bubble model
members.description: No quantitative derivation exists of the pearl excitation and de-excitation microphysics: the probability of exciting a pearl while it slows in shielding, the resulting ~3.5 keV electron emission spectrum in a detector, and the predicted DAMA-LIBRA/Xenon1T rate ratio are all undeveloped (the primary paper says so explicitly).
members.proposed_resolution: Derive the excitation spectrum of the domain-wall/electron-cloud bound system from the assumed skin tension and internal compressed-matter equation of state, then compute excitation cross sections on shielding nuclei and the de-excitation electron spectrum, yielding a falsifiable detector rate model for NaI and xenon targets.

members.model_name: Phantom hidden-sector sterile-neutrino dark matter creation
members.description: For the boosted-dark-matter extension, neither the local boosted flux normalization Phi_boost from vacuum decay nor an electron-recoil detector recast (XENONnT/DAMIC response and likelihood) exists for this model, so the direct-detection channel cannot be evaluated at all.
members.proposed_resolution: Derive the present-day boosted sterile-neutrino flux from the fitted vacuum-decay rate, then recast XENONnT electron-recoil data using the published detector efficiency and background model, following existing boosted-DM recast frameworks.

members.model_name: Fourth-generation U-antiquark dark atoms
members.description: The quantum-mechanical calculation of dark-atom binding and scattering with nuclei (binding energies and low-energy interaction of the helium-bound (UUU) composite with Na and other detector/terrestrial nuclei) does not exist; the primary text explicitly says the correct interaction description is under development, so DAMA compatibility, null-search consistency, and anomalous-isotope rates cannot be evaluated.
members.proposed_resolution: Derive the effective dark-atom/nucleus potential by solving the few-body quantum problem of the He-bound (UUU) cluster in the combined nuclear Coulomb and Woods-Saxon potentials (as attempted for O-helium), obtain binding energies and elastic/inelastic cross sections for Na, I, Xe, and Ge targets, and package them as a scattering-rate module for direct-detection recasts.

members.model_name: Pure-scalar inelastic coannihilation dark matter model
members.description: A dedicated inelastic nuclear-recoil calculation (s1 + nucleus -> s2 upscattering with the Delta threshold) was not performed, so direct-detection evasion is encoded only qualitatively and cannot be checked quantitatively against XENON1T/PandaX data.
members.proposed_resolution: Derive the inelastic Higgs-portal scattering rate with the kinematic threshold v_min(Delta) and halo-velocity integration, implementing it in an existing rate code such as WimPyDD or DDCalc modified for inelastic kinematics, and compare with XENON1T/PandaX exclusion data.

members.model_name: Conformal B-L pseudo-Goldstone dark matter
members.description: The loop-suppressed direct-detection cross section is asserted qualitatively but never computed: no numerical recoil cross section for the pseudo-Goldstone-nucleon scattering (including the effectively inelastic tree-level Z-prime channel into the heavier scalar partner) exists on the card.
members.proposed_resolution: Derive the loop-level elastic scattering amplitude through the Z-prime and scalar portals (and the inelastic tree-level channel with m_etaA/m_DM about 3), then evaluate against xenon-experiment limits with standard direct-detection tools to confirm the suppression quantitatively.

members.model_name: Z2-odd fermion dark matter annihilating to pseudo-Dirac sterile neutrinos
members.description: The one-loop matching of (lambda_H, y_chi) onto the effective Higgs-portal operator that controls spin-independent chi-nucleon scattering and the Higgs invisible width is not derived for this model; the paper only cites a similar-model calculation, so no quantitative direct-detection or invisible-Higgs exclusion can be produced.
