members.proposed_resolution: Extend a public dark-photon recasting package (e.g. Darkcast) to accept per-mode effective epsilon_n and branching fractions for the first two KK modes, and compute the DM-electron/nucleon direct-detection cross section from the summed KK propagators for comparison with sub-GeV direct-detection limits.

members.model_name: Two-component cold dark matter with self-heated light component
members.description: No calculation exists of the present-day boosted chi_1 flux from Galactic chi_2 annihilation and the resulting elastic-scattering event rates with detector response in Super-Kamiokande, XENONnT, or JUNO, so the proposed terrestrial-detection observable cannot be evaluated at all.
members.proposed_resolution: Derive the local boosted chi_1 flux from the Galactic chi_2 density profile and annihilation rate, then extend an existing boosted-dark-matter event-rate framework with kinetic-mixing-mediated electron/nucleon cross sections and published detector efficiencies for Super-K, XENONnT, and JUNO.

members.model_name: Dark-photon portal scalar millicharged dark matter
members.description: Direct-detection constraints cannot be applied or dismissed rigorously: the card's evacuation caveat (millicharged DM depleted from the Galactic disk by magnetic fields plus terrestrial shielding) rests on qualitative propagation assumptions with no dedicated model, leaving the XENON10/COHERENT applicability undetermined (robustness: low).
members.proposed_resolution: Develop a propagation model for the millicharged subcomponent in Galactic magnetic fields plus an Earth/atmosphere shielding calculation for epsilon about 1e-6 to 1e-4 and m_phi 10-80 MeV, yielding the local density and velocity distribution at detector depth needed to recast terrestrial scattering limits.

members.model_name: Five-dimensional Majorana dark photon fermion dark matter
members.description: Dark-photon intensity-frontier and direct-detection recasts for the multi-mode KK tower are missing: public recast machinery assumes a single dark photon with standard couplings, whereas here the lightest two gauge KK modes have boundary-condition-dependent couplings and the Majorana splitting plus axial couplings suppress or kinematically modify elastic scattering.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend a public dark-photon recasting package (e.g. Darkcast) to per-mode effective epsilon_n and branching fractions for the first two KK modes, and derive the Majorana inelastic/axial direct-detection response (splitting-dependent) for comparison with sub-GeV electron- and nuclear-recoil limits.

members.model_name: Asymmetric dark matter nuggets with scalar and vector forces
members.description: Existing direct-detection recast tools assume point-particle recoils; they lack the finite-size form factors, coherent enhancement, and low-number-density/multiscatter statistics required to recast xenon-experiment limits for ultraheavy composite nuggets.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend a public direct-detection recast framework (e.g. DDCalc-style detector response modules) with the composite form factor F(q R_nugget), coherence factor scaling with N_X, and Poisson flux statistics for large nugget masses, validated against the point-particle limit as R_nugget goes to zero.

members.model_name: Higgs Parity mirror-electron dark matter
members.description: No public direct-detection recast pipeline handles superheavy (m > 1e6 GeV) mirror-electron dark matter scattering on nuclei through photon--mirror-photon kinetic mixing, whose long-range mediator gives strong 1/q^4 momentum dependence outside the contact-operator assumptions of standard recoil calculators, and no XENON1T/LZ likelihood is attached to the route.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the long-range kinetic-mixing recoil spectrum (millicharge-like 1/q^4 form factor, superheavy-mass flux normalization) in an open recoil calculator such as DDCalc or WimPyDD and couple it to the public XENON1T and LZ likelihoods to replace the paper's approximate reinterpretation.

members.model_name: Scalar freeze-in inelastic dark matter with dark photon portal
members.description: No public code computes the exothermic electron-recoil spectrum dR/dE for a MeV-mass split scalar down-scattering on xenon electrons with keV energy release; existing DM-electron ionization codes assume elastic scattering and lack the required detector response tables.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend QEdark or DarkART to exothermic kinematics by adding the splitting delta to the energy deposited in the ionization rate integral, keep the existing xenon atomic ionization form factors, and convolve with the published XENON1T efficiency and resolution curves.

members.model_name: Spinor freeze-in inelastic dark matter with dark photon portal
members.description: No public code computes the exothermic electron-recoil spectrum dR/dE for a MeV-mass pseudo-Dirac excited state down-scattering on xenon electrons with keV energy release; existing DM-electron ionization codes assume elastic scattering and lack the required detector response tables.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend QEdark or DarkART to exothermic kinematics by adding the splitting delta to the energy deposited in the ionization rate integral, keep the existing xenon atomic ionization form factors, and convolve with the published XENON1T efficiency and resolution curves.

members.model_name: Millicharged dark matter subcomponent with a massless dark photon
members.description: No public code models millicharged-subcomponent transport through the Earth's atmosphere and crust (stopping, thermalization to ~300 K, accumulation and flux conservation) to predict the local density n_chi,local and velocity distribution at the detector; the route relies on the paper's order-of-magnitude estimates, and the same missing transport model sets the direct-detection thermalization ceiling.
members.proposed_resolution: Build a Monte Carlo or diffusion-based mCP Earth-transport module (extending existing strongly-coupled-DM terrestrial transport codes) parameterized by (epsilon, m_chi, f_chi) that outputs local density and velocity distribution profiles, validated against the paper's thermalized-regime estimates and its direct-detection ceiling.

members.model_name: Scalar boosted dark matter with semi-annihilation production
members.description: No public rate calculator combines the scalar semi-annihilation boosted-DM flux with DM-electron scattering and the XENON1T SR1 detector response (efficiency and energy resolution), so the 1-7 keV electron-recoil spectrum can only be estimated without detector effects.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend a public DM-electron scattering rate code such as wimprates or DarkELF with a boosted-DM monochromatic-velocity flux module and fold in the published XENON1T SR1 efficiency and resolution curves.

members.model_name: Near-continuum Z-portal dark matter
members.description: No public code computes the regulated near-gap spectral density and the resulting inelastic continuum direct-detection recoil rate; the published continuum formalism exists only as paper-level derivations, so the direct-detection suppression cannot be scanned over (mu0, spectral shape, portal coupling).
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the soft-wall Green's-function spectral density and the continuum inelastic recoil-rate integral in a small public package, validated against the discrete KK sum from the paper's regulator, and interface it to standard halo-model recoil kinematics.

members.model_name: Scalar boosted dark matter with annihilation production
members.description: No public rate calculator combines the scalar annihilation boosted-DM flux with DM-electron scattering and the XENON1T SR1 detector response (efficiency and energy resolution), so the 1-7 keV electron-recoil spectrum can only be estimated without detector effects.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend a public DM-electron scattering rate code such as wimprates or DarkELF with a boosted-DM monochromatic-velocity flux module and fold in the published XENON1T SR1 efficiency and resolution curves.

members.model_name: Annihilation-product direct-detection dark matter
members.description: No public code computes nuclear-recoil spectra for a relativistic dark-sector particle flux: existing direct-detection rate calculators assume nonrelativistic halo kinematics, so the distinctive Y recoil spectrum and E_min-space comparison cannot be produced with released tools.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend DDCalc or WIMPrates with relativistic Y-nucleus scattering kinematics for the paper's vector and scalar Y-quark operators, including nuclear form factors at large momentum transfer and the halo-independent E_min mapping.

members.model_name: SU(2)_D complex vector dark matter with electromagnetic multipole moments
members.description: No public direct-detection code maps spin-1 electromagnetic multipole form factors (mu_V, d_V, Q_V, tilde_Q_V, g1A, g5A) to nuclear recoil spectra across the xenon, germanium, fluorine, and CaWO4 targets, including the multi-form-factor interference the published single-operator limits ignore.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend an NREFT direct-detection package such as WimPyDD or DMFormFactor with the spin-1 multipole operator basis and its nonrelativistic reduction, allowing simultaneous form factors sourced from the SU(2)_D loop formulas.

members.model_name: Composite Inelastic Dark Matter
members.description: No public direct-detection code computes inelastic nuclear-recoil spectra with CiDM composite dark-meson form factors and the axial U(1)_A' hyperfine transition current; existing calculators implement point-particle inelastic DM at best.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend an existing open direct-detection framework (e.g. WimPyDD or DDCalc) with inelastic kinematics keyed to delta, the CiDM meson transition form factor, halo-integral modules for the inelastic threshold velocity, and NaI/Xe/Ge detector responses.

members.model_name: Three-scalar inelastic scalar dark matter model for muon g-2 and XENON1T
members.description: No public calculator produces the inelastic (keV-splitting, exothermic) dark-scalar-electron ionization spectrum in xenon for few-hundred-MeV to few-GeV dark matter with a light leptophilic scalar mediator; existing electron-recoil codes assume elastic scattering.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend QEdark or DarkELF xenon atomic response tables with down-scattering kinematics (energy deposit delta_m plus kinetic contribution) and a Maxwellian halo integral, validating against the paper's 1-5 keV spectrum with the roughly 2 keV peak.

members.model_name: Light dark photon force dark matter
members.description: Direct-detection comparisons use contact-limit curves with representative momentum transfers Q of 5-35 MeV inserted by hand; no rate calculator with the full light-mediator propagator momentum dependence was applied for m_Ap near or below tens of MeV, where the card says contact-limit curves break down.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend an existing direct-detection rate code (DDCalc or WimPyDD) with the (q^2 + m_Ap^2)^-2 propagator form factor and recast current LUX/LZ, CDMSlite, and SuperCDMS limits onto (epsilon, m_Ap, m_chi), replacing the source's fixed-Q approximation.

members.model_name: Light exothermic inelastic dark matter with vector mediator
members.description: No public code computes electron-recoil and Migdal-effect ionization spectra for exothermic inelastic dark matter with keV-scale mass splitting; existing electron-scattering tools (QEDark, DarkELF) and published Migdal probability tables assume elastic kinematics, so the delta_m-dependent spectral shapes central to this model cannot be generated off the shelf.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend DarkELF (or QEDark) xenon ionization-rate routines to inelastic kinematics by shifting the energy-conservation delta by delta_m in the atomic response convolution, and couple the same kinematic modification to the Ibe-et-al Migdal transition-probability tables, parameterized by (m_X, delta_m, q_e, q_p, q_n).

members.model_name: Late-forming PBH dark matter from a fermion-scalar fluid
members.description: No public, simulation-validated treatment exists of scalar-radiative cooling and collapse of dense fermion-scalar halos into PBHs; the collapse criterion, cooling time, and the fraction of halo mass ending in the black hole rest on the paper's uncalibrated semi-analytic estimates, which directly set the predicted PBH mass function.
members.proposed_resolution: Develop a public semi-analytic halo cooling/collapse code for the fermion-scalar fluid (Fermi pressure plus attractive scalar force plus scalar-radiation losses) and calibrate it with dedicated numerical simulations of dark halo collapse with a light-scalar fifth force, parameterized by z_T, m_phi, m_psi, and the fermion-scalar coupling.

members.model_name: Leptophilic non-thermal WIMP model from U(1)' cosmic strings
members.description: No N-body simulation of structure formation with the high-velocity nonthermal WIMP distribution from cosmic-string loop decay exists, so the cored halo profile that reconciles the large leptonic annihilation rate with HESS Galactic-center gamma rays is uncalibrated.
members.proposed_resolution: Run cosmological N-body (or controlled halo-relaxation) simulations initialized with the burst-produced monochromatic velocity distribution and its phase-space density Q, and extract the inner-profile slope and J-factor as functions of T_c and m_chi for use in the gamma-ray recast.

members.model_name: Confining dark-baryon inverse-seesaw dark matter model
members.description: No dedicated simulation exists for the neutrino and photon spectra from the annihilation chain B B -> M M -> N N -> SM at m_B ~ 10^4-10^5 TeV, including electroweak showering of the heavy sterile-neutrino decay products; current limits are only approximate rescalings of Majorana-benchmark line searches.
members.proposed_resolution: Compute the boosted N decay spectra with HDMSpectra (valid at these ultra-heavy masses), convolve with the M -> N N and B B -> M M decay-chain kinematics including the spin-3/2 Dirac degree-of-freedom rescaling, and build recast limits from published ANTARES/IceCube/KM3NeT line-search and Fermi-LAT/HESS/CTA tables.

members.model_name: Preheating-produced sterile-neutrino fermionic dark matter
members.description: The production calculation relies on analytic interpolation ansaetze for the scale factor and time-varying mass, valid only for fast/instant preheating with backreaction neglected; no numerical solver exists for fermion mode functions in a realistic (possibly oscillatory or slower) Palatini Higgs-inflation preheating background including backreaction of the produced fermions.
members.proposed_resolution: Numerically integrate the fermion mode equations on the actual Palatini Higgs-inflation background field evolution (from a standard inflaton/lattice preheating solver) rather than the analytic interpolation, scanning tau, M_i, M_R, and c_5, and estimate backreaction to delimit where the analytic scalings hold.

members.model_name: B-L charged scalar dark matter triggering nucleon decay
members.description: No event generator or nuclear-response model exists for DM-induced neutron removal in oxygen/argon targets: the invisible-neutrino plus nuclear de-excitation and hadronic final state has no simulation of intranuclear cascades and de-excitation gammas for this signal.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend an existing neutrino/nucleon-decay event generator (e.g. GENIE's nucleon-decay and final-state-interaction modules) with the DM-induced neutron-removal vertex, producing event spectra including nuclear de-excitation photons for water-Cherenkov and liquid-argon targets.

members.model_name: Sub-keV decaying fermion dark matter in anomaly-free hidden U(1)_X
members.description: The degenerate-fermion core-cusp prediction for dwarf spheroidals is qualitative: no structure-formation simulation or calibrated semi-analytic model exists for sub-keV fermions with this nonthermal phase-space history including fermionic quantum pressure and baryons.
members.proposed_resolution: Build Thomas-Fermi hydrostatic dwarf-halo models using the derived nonthermal phase-space density, and calibrate against dedicated N-body simulations initialized with the model's f(q) and transfer function (WDM-style zoom simulations with fermionic-pressure initial phase-space constraints) before confronting dwarf-spheroidal kinematics.

members.model_name: Fermionic dark matter from linear non-minimally coupled inflaton decay
members.description: The yield is computed assuming purely perturbative two-body decay of the inflaton condensate; no lattice or non-perturbative preheating calculation exists for the linear non-minimal coupling beta M_P phi R to quantify how parametric/tachyonic particle production corrects the fermionic DM abundance, a risk the card's validity domain explicitly flags.
members.proposed_resolution: Run a lattice preheating study (e.g. with CosmoLattice extended to the Einstein-frame interactions induced by the linear non-minimal coupling) of inflaton fragmentation and gravitational particle production for representative beta in the O(0.1)-O(100) range, and publish correction factors to the perturbative yield.

members.model_name: Degenerate neutrino-portal scalar-fermion self-interacting dark matter
members.description: No N-body or gravothermal simulations exist for this model's off-diagonal monopole-dipole 1/v^2 self-interaction between degenerate scalar and fermion components, so halo density-profile, core-formation, and subhalo predictions are uncalibrated (the card marks all nonlinear effects unknown).
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the model's velocity-dependent differential cross section (including the two-component scalar-fermion scattering structure) in an SIDM-capable N-body code such as Arepo or GIZMO, or in a calibrated gravothermal fluid model, and simulate dwarf-to-cluster halos across the favored sigma_T/m band.

members.model_name: Non-minimally coupled scalar dark matter from inflationary fluctuations
members.description: Nonlinear collapse and survival of the predicted small-scale clumps (scales of order 1e4 km to 1e4 AU) have never been simulated, so the clumpy-dark-matter observable cannot be turned into predictions for lensing, pulsar timing, or indirect detection.
members.proposed_resolution: Run zoom-in N-body (or Press-Schechter-calibrated semi-analytic) simulations seeded with the peaked P_delta(k) to obtain a minihalo mass function, concentrations, and tidal survival fractions, then connect these to existing microlensing, pulsar-timing, and annihilation-boost constraint frameworks for compact minihalos.

members.model_name: Dark SU(2)_D neutron-decay freeze-in dark matter
members.description: No neutron-star equation-of-state recast capability exists for neutron dark decay n -> chi phi with the dark self-interactions the model invokes to evade maximum-mass bounds; consistency with observed two-solar-mass neutron stars is currently only a qualitative flag.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend a TOV/EoS solver with a dark-fermion component in chemical equilibrium through the n -> chi phi channel, including W^a-mediated dark repulsion in the dark-sector EoS, and confront the maximum-mass curve with observed pulsar masses over the benchmark (m_chi = 938 MeV, m_W' = 8 MeV).

members.model_name: Broken-Z2 mirror baryon dark matter
members.description: The claim that mirror halos avoid catastrophic bremsstrahlung/ionization cooling when m_e2 is raised rests on an analytic timescale estimate; no simulation of dissipative mirror-baryon halos with mirror-electromagnetic and mirror-strong cooling exists to establish the halo-stability boundary in (m_e2, m_mirror_baryon).
members.proposed_resolution: Run hydrodynamic halo simulations with a mirror-sector cooling function (mirror atomic and bremsstrahlung rates rescaled to the heavier mirror fermion masses), mapping the cooling-stability boundary as a function of m_e2/m_baryon and halo mass.

members.model_name: Fermi-ball collapse primordial black hole dark matter
members.description: The Fermi-ball formation and collapse dynamics (trapped fraction, remnant shrinkage, and the regime where remnants collapse directly to PBHs without an intermediate Fermi-ball) have no numerical simulation; the route caveat explicitly flags that direct collapse requires simulation.
members.proposed_resolution: Run coupled scalar-field plus fermion-fluid simulations of a shrinking false-vacuum remnant with Yukawa attraction to calibrate the trapped fraction F_trap, the collapse temperature, and the Fermi-ball-to-PBH mass relation beyond the analytic energy-balance estimate.

members.model_name: Scalar-extended accidental composite dark matter
members.description: No lattice or other nonperturbative calculation exists for the dark-hadron spectrum of SU(N) dark color with light vectorlike fermionic dark quarks plus a scalar dark quark, including hybrid fermion-scalar dark baryons and their mass ordering, which every signature route depends on.
members.proposed_resolution: Run dedicated lattice simulations (or matched large-N/quark-model estimates as an interim step) for SU(N) gauge theory with the paper's fermion-plus-scalar constituent content, delivering the low-lying baryon, hybrid, meson, and glueball spectrum as a function of Lambda_DC, M_phi, and M_psi.

members.model_name: Complex vector condensate dark matter with magnetic dipole coupling
members.description: The transition from the non-magnetic to the magnetic condensate and the resulting magnetic-field power spectrum and coherence length have never been simulated; the paper's homogeneous-condensate estimate gives only an amplitude, and PMF observables (CMB anisotropy bounds, gamma-ray lower bounds on intergalactic fields) depend on B(k) and coherence scale, not amplitude alone.
members.proposed_resolution: Run classical lattice field simulations of the complex vector field coupled to electromagnetism through the dipole operator (extending existing axion-magnetogenesis/vector-instability lattice codes) to follow the classical instability, extract the generated B(k) spectrum and coherence length, and track its MHD evolution to z=0.

members.model_name: Co-interacting conformal two-component dark matter
members.description: No structure-formation simulations or emulator exist for the co-interacting regime, where a subdominant (f ~ 0.1) heavy component with sigma/m up to ~10 cm^2/g exchanges heat with a dominant ultra-light scalar bath; existing SIDM simulations assume a single self-interacting species, so the predicted dwarf-core and cluster-merger responses are only qualitative.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend an existing SIDM N-body implementation (e.g. the GIZMO or Arepo SIDM modules) to two species — a fractional interacting fermion component scattering off a fuzzy-DM-like scalar background — scan over (f, sigma/m(v), m_phi), and calibrate a core-size/central-density emulator for dwarf-to-cluster halos.

members.model_name: Late-forming PBH from thermal balls and Fermi balls
members.description: No simulation calibrates the trapping of asymmetric dark fermions by FOPT bubble walls or the resulting thermal-ball population, so the remnant abundance, trapping fraction, and Fermi-ball mass function that seed the PBH prediction are order-of-magnitude analytic estimates only.
members.proposed_resolution: Run lattice or hydrodynamic simulations of a dark-sector FOPT with fermion transmission/reflection at the walls (extending existing bubble-wall friction and filtered-dark-matter simulation setups) to calibrate the trapping fraction and remnant mass function as functions of wall velocity, beta/H, and the Yukawa coupling.

members.model_name: Relativistic Bose-Einstein condensate scalar dark matter cosmology
members.description: No nonlinear simulation calibration exists for the collapse of self-interacting BEC condensates into halos in this model (simulation_calibrated: no), so halo density profiles, rotation curves, and the subhalo/halo mass function cannot be predicted beyond Thomas-Fermi analytic estimates.
members.proposed_resolution: Adapt a public Gross-Pitaevskii-Poisson solver (e.g. PyUltraLight or an AxioNyx-class cosmological code) to include the quartic self-interaction term, run collapse simulations across the (m, a_s) plane, and calibrate a core-halo relation usable in rotation-curve and minimum-halo fits.

members.model_name: Techni-Pati-Salam semi-integer-baryon-number composite dark matter
members.description: The Sp(4)_HC composite spectrum (mass of the lightest neutral semi-integer-baryon-number state, splittings among exotic components, and confirmation of the walking regime needed for partial compositeness) is unknown; the paper explicitly defers this to future lattice calculations, and even the DM candidate's spin/statistics are listed as unknown on the card.
members.proposed_resolution: Run lattice simulations of Sp(4) gauge theory with the model's mixed fundamental plus antisymmetric hyper-fermion content to determine the exotic-baryon spectrum, mass splittings, and the (near-)conformal behavior of the coupling, following existing Sp(4) lattice programs but extended to this fermion content.

members.model_name: Atomic dissipative dark matter with dark black holes
members.description: No simulations exist of dark-atomic gas cooling, fragmentation, and direct collapse for this model's chemistry (heavy fermion x, light fermion c, alpha_D, molecular cooling gap), so the cooling curves and the numerical coefficient of the minimum dark Jeans mass — which set the DBH mass function — are only order-of-magnitude analytic estimates.
members.proposed_resolution: Run hydrodynamic collapse simulations with a dark-chemistry network (dark recombination, bremsstrahlung, atomic and H_D,2 molecular cooling, parameterized by m_x, m_c, alpha_D) to calibrate cooling functions and the minimum-Jeans-mass coefficient, analogous to Population-III star-formation simulations.

members.model_name: Rotating Bose-Einstein-condensate cold dark matter with possible vortices
members.description: No public solver covers rotating, strongly self-interacting (Thomas-Fermi regime) Gross-Pitaevskii-Poisson haloes with quantized vortices at the paper's benchmark (g/g_H ~ 68, lambda ~ 0.05); existing Schroedinger-Poisson codes for fuzzy dark matter omit the g|psi|^2 self-interaction and angular-momentum configurations, so vortex formation and core-depletion predictions cannot be computed beyond the paper's analytic energy estimates.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend a public Schroedinger-Poisson solver of the PyUltraLight class with the repulsive g|psi|^2 psi self-interaction term and rotating initial conditions, and simulate virialized haloes across (m/m_H, g/g_H, lambda) to calibrate vortex stability, core sizes, and density profiles against the paper's analytic criteria.

members.model_name: Thermal dark matter freeze-out during kination
members.description: The microhalo abundance and boost prescription for kination-enhanced small-scale spectra is only partially simulation-calibrated; microhalo survival and tidal disruption in host halos dominate the boost uncertainty.
members.proposed_resolution: Run N-body zoom simulations initialized with kination-enhanced transfer functions (spanning T_KR and cutoff scale k_cut) to calibrate the microhalo mass function, concentrations, and survival fractions used by the semi-analytic boost model.

members.model_name: Minimal LRSM N1 dark matter with right-handed triplet scalar dilution
members.description: Nonlinear structure formation is uncalibrated for the mixed cold+hot N1 population: halo and subhalo mass-function effects are unknown, simulation_calibrated is no, and the paper's matter-power treatment is explicitly linear-only.
members.proposed_resolution: Run mixed cold+hot dark matter N-body simulations parameterized by (m_N1, Br_Delta_to_N1) to calibrate nonlinear power and halo/subhalo mass-function suppression, following existing mixed-WDM simulation suites.

members.model_name: WIMPflation stable inflaton dark matter
members.description: No nonperturbative preheating/thermalization calculation exists for annihilation-driven reheating of a stable inflaton across the five studied potential classes; the card notes thermalization after reheating is model-dependent and precision requires a nonperturbative treatment, which controls whether the thermal freeze-out assumption holds.
members.proposed_resolution: Run lattice preheating simulations (CosmoLattice or LATTICEEASY) for each WIMPflation potential class with the Higgs-portal coupling included, extract the reheating temperature and verify inflaton-SM kinetic equilibration, and publish fitting functions for T_RH(potential parameters, lambda_phiH).

members.model_name: Late-universe two-body decaying dark matter
members.description: No simulation-calibrated nonlinear matter power spectrum or halo mass function exists for the two-body decay scenario (card: simulation_calibrated 'no'), so weak-lensing and cluster-count S8 constraints can only be applied at linear or mildly nonlinear level.
members.proposed_resolution: Run N-body simulations with two-body decaying dark matter (parent decay to massless plus warm massive daughter, parameterized by tau and epsilon) and fit a nonlinear boost/suppression formula or emulator relative to LCDM for use in weak-lensing likelihoods.

members.model_name: Oscillon-forming axion-like fuzzy dark matter
members.description: Oscillon lifetimes and radiated-ALP momentum spectra are only simulated for a few benchmark pure-natural potentials; no calibrated mapping tau_osc(p, M, m) and f(k) covering the model's parameter space exists, and the single-decay-temperature approximation is uncontrolled.
members.proposed_resolution: Run a lattice campaign with a public scalar-field code (CosmoLattice-class) scanning the pure-natural exponent p and scale M, tabulating oscillon lifetime, surviving fraction r_osc, and emitted momentum distribution, and release the tables as an interpolable product.

members.model_name: Nucleophilic scalar Co-SIMP dark matter
members.description: No transport/attenuation code models the boosted Co-SIMP population: in-Earth 3-to-2 conversion accelerates dark matter, and the resulting flux must be propagated through rock/atmosphere with the same elastic cross section; existing boosted-dark-matter transport tools (elastic-only Monte Carlos) lack the conversion source term.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend an existing overburden/boosted-DM Monte Carlo transport code (DaMaSCUS/verne-class) with a Co-SIMP conversion injection spectrum and Earth material profile, outputting the attenuated boosted flux at detector depth as a function of sigma_elastic and the conversion rate.

members.model_name: Light collisional cold dark matter
members.description: Nonlinear predictions rely on WDM-cutoff transfer functions as proxies; no N-body simulations have been run with the model's true oscillatory damped spectrum, so power regeneration at z < 1, halo abundance, and reionization-era first-halo suppression are only bracketed, not computed.
members.proposed_resolution: Once gap_1 provides exact oscillatory transfer functions, run N-body simulations (GADGET-4 or AREPO with MUSIC-style initial conditions from the tabulated P(k)) covering representative damping masses up to ~10^3 M_sun, measuring the halo mass function and nonlinear P(k) against matched CDM and WDM runs.

members.model_name: Dark-matter-coupled scalar-field fifth-force model
members.description: No public coupled scalar-field N-body code covers this model's regime: the modified MLAPM multigrid solver with chameleon screening is author code, and the paper explicitly defers quantitative nonlinear matter power spectra and halo profiles to future simulation work, so no calibrated nonlinear predictions exist in the (beta, lambda) space.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the dark-matter-only C(phi) coupling in a public modified-gravity N-body code (ECOSMOG or ISIS/RAMSES-style multigrid scalar solver), run a simulation suite over (beta, lambda) sufficient to calibrate nonlinear P(k) and halo profiles, and check the quasi-static approximation flagged on the card.

members.model_name: Interacting cold dark matter-dark radiation drag model
members.description: The nonlinear response to drag-damped growth is not simulation-calibrated (simulation_calibrated: no), yet the key S8/weak-lensing and cluster-count observables depend on the nonlinear matter power spectrum in this suppressed-growth cosmology.
members.proposed_resolution: Run a small suite of N-body simulations with initial conditions and growth histories from the modified CLASS, and validate or recalibrate halofit/HMcode emulation for the drag-suppressed spectra used in lensing and cluster likelihoods.

members.model_name: Hidden-sector early cannibal-dominated dark matter cosmology
members.description: The mapping from the ECDE-enhanced transfer function to a present-day microhalo population is uncalibrated: no N-body simulations exist for cannibal-shaped peaked spectra, so microhalo mass function, concentrations, and tidal survival in the Galactic halo are unquantified.
members.proposed_resolution: Run a suite of high-resolution N-body simulations seeded with ECDE transfer functions (peak plus Jeans cutoff) across the (k_pk, cutoff) plane to calibrate a semi-analytic microhalo mass-concentration model and survival fractions under tidal stripping.

members.model_name: Extended Ma model with inert scalar dark matter and preheating symmetry restoration
members.description: No public code covers the preheating dynamics of this model: explosive singlet-scalar production after inflation, radiative symmetry restoration, and the resulting nonthermal lepton asymmetry from inflaton decay to the right-handed neutrino sector, which set the cosmological history that the dark-matter parameters must be consistent with.
members.proposed_resolution: Simulate the inflaton-singlet system with a lattice preheating code (CosmoLattice or LATTICEEASY class) to obtain the singlet occupation and effective-potential symmetry restoration, then couple the output to a set of Boltzmann equations for N_i decays and lepton-number transfer, parameterized by g_S and the inflaton couplings.

members.model_name: Non-canonical scalar unified dark matter-dark energy model
members.description: Nonlinear structure formation for the unified scalar is not simulation-calibrated (simulation_calibrated: no); halo and subhalo suppression at smaller alpha is only inferred from the linear sound-speed argument, so halo-scale observables cannot be evaluated quantitatively.
members.proposed_resolution: Run N-body simulations initialized with the model's suppressed transfer function, including the scale-dependent growth from finite sound speed (or verify that a pressureless N-body treatment suffices for large alpha), and calibrate the halo mass function response versus alpha.

members.model_name: Spin-zero no-freeze-in/no-freeze-out warm dark matter
members.description: The paper explicitly notes unknown corrections from residual velocity dispersion and nonlinear regeneration of small-scale power; no simulation calibration exists for this colder early-decoupled scenario, leaving the nonlinear cutoff-to-observable mapping uncalibrated.
members.proposed_resolution: Run N-body/hydro simulations with initial conditions from the exact transfer function plus thermal velocities drawn from the model's f(p) (WDM-style simulations at M_S ~ 150 eV, T_S/T_gamma = 0.345) to calibrate nonlinear power regeneration and the first-galaxy/halo mass cutoff.

members.model_name: Type-I seesaw Majoron warm dark matter completion
members.description: Nonlinear small-scale predictions (halo statistics for the warm, decaying Majoron) lack a calibrated N-body suite; the source points to N-body simulation as the forward model but simulation_calibrated is only partial and no pipeline is attached to the card.
members.proposed_resolution: Run WDM-style N-body simulations (e.g. Gadget-4 with truncated initial power from the gap_2 transfer functions, including thermal-velocity treatment) for representative keV Majoron benchmarks to calibrate the halo and subhalo mass-function suppression.

members.model_name: ULAP oscillon dark matter
members.description: The oscillon fraction r_osc, formation efficiency, and survival to z~10 are taken from the authors' unreleased lattice simulation code and were computed only for the p=-3/4 monodromy example, so the oscillon population inputs cannot be regenerated across the (m, F, p) parameter space.
members.proposed_resolution: Run public 3+1D scalar-field lattice simulations (e.g. CosmoLattice or LATTICEEASY-class codes) of oscillon formation and decay for a grid of monodromy-type potentials, and release fitted tables of r_osc, oscillon mass spectrum, and lifetime versus (m, F, p) for use in the power-spectrum step.

members.model_name: Surface-type DBI dark matter
members.description: The paper's predictions are valid only to linear order and the card records nonlinear halo and subhalo mass-function effects as unknown with no simulation calibration, so the claimed late-time smoothing of structure (the S8-tension motivation) cannot be propagated to nonlinear weak-lensing and small-scale-structure observables.
members.proposed_resolution: Run cosmological simulations treating the s-DBI component as a pressured fluid (an N-body code extended with the effective pressure/sound-speed terms, or a fluid-particle hybrid) across the a_d parameter range to calibrate the nonlinear matter power spectrum and halo mass function relative to CDM.

members.model_name: Kination freeze-out Majorana dark matter
members.description: No tool exists for the kination-enhanced small-scale power spectrum, its kinetic-decoupling cutoff, and the resulting microhalo annihilation boost factor B needed to include post-2018 substructure constraints; the substructure step is entirely unimplemented.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the kination-era perturbation growth in a modified CLASS run with the appropriate early expansion history, attach a kinetic-decoupling cutoff from the model's scattering rate, and feed the resulting transfer function to a semi-analytic microhalo model (Press-Schechter/peaks formalism calibrated on existing enhanced-power N-body simulations) to output boost factors versus T_R and the decoupling temperature.

members.model_name: Light scalar dark matter clumps with angular momentum
members.description: No dynamical-stability certification exists for the l > 0 variational clump branch: cited follow-up simulations find rotating Bose stars with attractive or negligible self-interactions unstable, but no public Gross-Pitaevskii-Poisson simulation suite maps stability across (l, self-interaction sign and strength, M), so it is unknown which angular-momentum configurations survive as long-lived dark-matter clumps.
members.proposed_resolution: Run 3D Gross-Pitaevskii-Poisson evolutions of the paper's stationary l > 0 profiles across attractive, negligible, and repulsive quartic couplings, recovering the spherical l = 0 limit as validation, and publish a stability map plus lifetime estimates as a registry data product.

members.model_name: Velocity-dependent SIDM thermally coupled through millicharged dark matter
members.description: Halo-core predictions rest on benchmark relative velocities and Maxwell-Boltzmann averaging; no N-body SIDM simulations calibrated for this model's specific light-scalar sigma_T(v) shape exist, so the mapping from cross section to core sizes and substructure is uncalibrated.
members.proposed_resolution: Run a small suite of cosmological zoom-in SIDM simulations (e.g. with the Arepo/GIZMO SIDM modules) sampling the paper's Yukawa sigma_T(v) benchmarks at m_SIDM = 10-40 GeV to calibrate the halo-average step against actual core formation.

members.model_name: Pre-inflationary QCD axion minicluster scenario
members.description: No nonlinear simulation follows the collapse of pre-inflationary axion clump seeds (hilltop self-interaction resonance or enhanced small-scale primordial power near the QCD horizon) into miniclusters; existing minicluster simulations use post-inflationary white-noise initial conditions, so the mass function, density profiles, minicluster fraction f_MC, and survival probability are unknown for this scenario.
members.proposed_resolution: Run Schroedinger-Poisson or N-body simulations (e.g. adapting AxioNyx-class codes) initialized with the primary paper's linear QCD-epoch perturbation spectra for hilltop and enhanced-P_zeta cases, evolving through matter-radiation equality to extract the minicluster mass function, profiles, f_MC, and tidal survival.

members.model_name: 5D U(1) repulsive-axion ultralight scalar dark matter
members.description: No simulation-calibrated nonlinear halo predictions exist for an ultralight scalar with a repulsive quartic self-interaction; the polytropic core profile is a zero-temperature, baryon-free analytic estimate the card itself flags as not robust.
members.proposed_resolution: Run Gross-Pitaevskii-Poisson simulations (e.g. extend a PyUltraLight-style spectral solver) including the repulsive lambda4_eff term, finite-temperature corrections, and a baryonic potential, and calibrate a core-radius/core-mass relation over the (m, f, lambda4_eff) plane.

members.model_name: Self-interacting Dirac fermion dark matter with light scalar mediator for dark stars
members.description: No simulation capability exists for coupled SIDM gravothermal evolution plus baryonic gas collapse in 10^6-10^8 solar-mass protohalos at z~20, which is required to establish whether central SIDM densities actually reach the values needed for annihilation-powered dark stars; the paper parametrizes the SIDM-to-baryon ratio instead.
members.proposed_resolution: Run cosmological zoom-in hydrodynamic simulations of first-star minihalos with an SIDM module (e.g. the Arepo or GIZMO SIDM implementations) including primordial gas cooling, or extend SIDM gravothermal fluid codes with an adiabatically deepening baryonic potential, scanning sigma_self/m over the favored galaxy-scale range.

members.model_name: SU(2) x U(1) five-plet accident dark matter
members.description: The mass floor from long-range dark-photon self-interactions rests on a literature halo-ellipticity bound with an assumed simple mapping from Q_D^2 alpha_D to halo shapes; no simulation-calibrated constraint or likelihood exists for unscreened long-range forces in this model's charged-scalar dark matter.
members.proposed_resolution: Run N-body/hydro simulations of halos with unscreened 1/r^2 dark Coulomb interactions across the relevant (Q_D^2 alpha_D)/m_DM^3 range, calibrate the ellipticity and core response, and construct a likelihood against measured X-ray and lensing halo-shape data.

members.model_name: Cosine self-interacting scalar dark matter
members.description: The core-existence domain of the bounded cosine potential rests solely on spherical hydrostatic equilibrium (simulation_calibrated: no); no simulations test whether non-spherical dynamics, mergers, or cosmological assembly preserve the predicted loss of solitonic cores in massive halos.
members.proposed_resolution: Run halo-scale and cosmological simulations of the scalar with the cosine self-interaction (Gross-Pitaevskii/Schrodinger-Poisson solvers extended with the bounded nonpolynomial potential, or an effective-fluid solver with the cosine pressure law) to map the core-existence boundary across halo mass.

members.model_name: Dark matter vortex filament model
members.description: The parallel, singly quantized, filament-aligned vortex configuration is a fitting ansatz with no simulation support: no Gross-Pitaevskii-Poisson simulation of cosmic filaments has established whether vortices of the required number (~3000 for m=1e-22 eV), alignment, and survival actually form, which the paper itself flags as needing simulations.
members.proposed_resolution: Run Gross-Pitaevskii-Poisson (Schroedinger-Poisson with optional self-interaction g) simulations of filament formation in a cosmological setting, e.g. by extending AxioNyx or PyUltraLight-class solvers to filament-scale boxes, and measure vortex number density, alignment with the filament axis, and lifetime to calibrate or replace the Gaussian parallel-vortex template.

members.model_name: SU(3) x U(1) ten-plet accident dark matter
members.description: No cosmological or halo-scale simulation capability exists for a six-component dark matter multiplet interacting through two massless dark photons (long-range dark electromagnetism), so the halo-shape and substructure response to these forces cannot be predicted.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend existing SIDM N-body frameworks (e.g. Arepo/Gizmo SIDM modules) with a multi-species dark-plasma module implementing Rutherford-like scattering under two U(1) charges, starting from the effective dark-Coulomb cross sections derived for the accident multiplet, and calibrate halo-shape and core observables on a small suite of zoom-in runs.

members.model_name: Self-interacting scalar field dark matter
members.description: No nonlinear simulation or halo solver includes this model's cosh-potential self-interaction: public Schrodinger-Poisson codes target free (non-self-interacting) fuzzy dark matter, so the predicted core radii, ~1e12 M_sun halo masses, and cluster-scale multistate profiles cannot be computed for the actual model.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend a Schrodinger-Poisson / Gross-Pitaevskii solver (e.g. PyUltraLight- or AxioNyx-class codes) with the self-interaction term from the cosh potential, run cosmological or isolated-halo simulations over the fixed parameter set, and calibrate a core radius-halo mass relation and cluster mass profiles for comparison with LSB and Chandra data.

members.model_name: Dissipative dark electromagnetism model
members.description: No cosmological or halo-scale simulations exist for the two-species H-L dark plasma with dark-photon radiative cooling; fragmentation, the compact-object mass spectrum, and survival of collapsed substructure under tides are therefore unpredicted (nonlinear block is all unknown, simulation_calibrated: no).
members.proposed_resolution: Run dissipative-dark-matter N-body/hydro simulations (e.g. extend the GIZMO/Arepo dissipative-SIDM modules with the paper's H-L Coulomb, bremsstrahlung, recombination, and collisional-excitation cooling functions) over the alpha_D, m_H, m_L benchmarks to obtain a collapsed-object mass function and density profiles.

members.model_name: Fuzzy dark fluid unified scalar
members.description: Small-scale structure predictions (transfer-function cutoff, soliton cores) are uncalibrated for this model: existing Schrodinger-Poisson solvers assume a free m^2 phi^2 field, while here the quartic self-coupling lambda and non-minimal coupling may alter the cutoff and core structure (card assumption fdf_classic_fuzzy_mapping is unverified).
members.proposed_resolution: Add the quartic self-interaction term (a Gross-Pitaevskii-type nonlinearity) to a public Schrodinger-Poisson solver such as PyUltraLight or the GAMER wave-DM module, run cosmological boxes over the m ~ 1e-22 to 1e-21 eV, allowed-lambda region, and fit a transfer-function/core-size parameterization.

members.model_name: Self-interacting scalar field dark matter soliton model
members.description: The modified soliton-halo relation and its assumed factor-of-two peak-velocity scatter are not calibrated for self-interacting SFDM: no cosmological or merger Schrodinger-Poisson simulations including the quartic term validate how soliton mass tracks halo mass when lambda is non-zero.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend an existing pseudo-spectral Schrodinger-Poisson code (e.g. PyUltraLight- or AxioNyx-class) with the cubic nonlinearity and run halo-formation/merger simulations across lambda_ini to measure the soliton-halo relation and its scatter with self-interactions.

members.model_name: Millicharged atomic dark matter with elastic nuclear scattering
members.description: The halo-ellipticity and Bullet Cluster consistency checks use rough analytic dark-atom self-interaction cross sections; no calibrated atomic-DM elastic self-scattering computation or structure-formation calibration exists for this model (the card marks all nonlinear structure fields unknown/uncalibrated).
members.proposed_resolution: Compute the velocity-dependent dark-atom elastic self-scattering cross section from quantum atomic-scattering calculations (partial-wave hydrogen-hydrogen-analog rescaled to alpha_prime, m_H), then apply existing SIDM halo-shape constraint machinery to replace the order-of-magnitude ellipticity check.

members.model_name: Quartic self-interacting superfluid scalar dark matter with core fragmentation
members.description: No numerical simulations exist of superfluid core thermalization and Jeans fragmentation for a repulsive-quartic complex scalar starting from NFW-like halos; the fragmentation-into-droplets prediction is a semi-analytic, uncalibrated estimate sensitive to the assumed pre-thermalization profile.
members.proposed_resolution: Run Gross-Pitaevskii-Poisson (or wave-DM plus self-interaction) halo simulations — e.g. extend PyUltraLight or AxioNyx with the repulsive lambda|phi|^4 pressure term and a collisional thermalization treatment — initialized from NFW halos over the (m, sigma/m) plane, and calibrate the analytic R_T/R_deg/Jeans criteria against the simulated core morphology.

members.model_name: Nonlinear charged dark matter with K-mouflage screening
members.description: No N-body or calibrated spherical-collapse implementation exists for charged dark matter with environment-dependent K-mouflage screening, so cluster number counts, peculiar velocities, and halo self-interaction limits (the screening recast of ordinary charged-DM bounds) have no quantitative prediction.
members.proposed_resolution: Adapt an existing screened-force N-body code (of the type built for K-mouflage/Vainshtein modified gravity) to apply the screened dark-electric force between dark matter particles only, calibrate the halo mass function, velocity statistics, and merging-cluster behavior, and recast collisionless-halo charged-DM bounds with screening included.

members.model_name: Late-decay self-interacting dark matter production mechanism
members.description: No nonlinear halo modeling or simulation calibration exists for the two-component ultrastrong SIDM regime at tau_S > 10 Gyr (all nonlinear structure-formation fields are unknown), so galactic-scale predictions of this regime cannot be evaluated.
members.proposed_resolution: Run cosmological N-body/hydro simulations with a two-component dark sector (residual pseudo-WIMP plus ultrastrong-SIDM daughter produced post-recombination), scanning tau_S and the self-interaction cross section, and calibrate halo density-profile and subhalo-population responses for comparison with galactic-scale data.

members.model_name: BEC/SFDM self-interacting ultralight scalar dark matter for cluster collisions
members.description: No numerical simulations exist of cluster-scale collisions of self-interacting BEC/SFDM halos: the kinetic-energy-dependent transition between soliton-like pass-through and merger with a repulsive quartic self-interaction has never been computed beyond the primary paper's qualitative analytic argument.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend a public Gross-Pitaevskii-Poisson / Schroedinger-Poisson solver (PyUltraLight- or AxioNyx-class) to include the lambda|phi|^4 self-interaction and run cluster-mass halo collisions over a grid in (m, lambda, v_coll, impact parameter), calibrating the pass-through/merger boundary against the Bullet Cluster and Abell 520 velocity scales.

members.model_name: Minimal LRSM N1 dark matter with N2 entropy dilution
members.description: Nonlinear structure formation for the mixed cold+warm/hot N1 population is uncalibrated: the card marks halo and subhalo mass-function effects unknown, simulation_calibrated no, and the paper defers nonlinear Boltzmann corrections to future work.
members.proposed_resolution: Run N-body simulations with two-component initial conditions (cold diluted N1 plus hot secondary fraction Br_N1) to calibrate a halo/subhalo mass-function fitting formula versus (m_N1, Br_N1), analogous to existing mixed-WDM suites.

members.model_name: Electromagnetically coupled ALP misalignment dark matter targets
members.description: For the early-matter-domination, kination, and temperature-dependent-mass variants the card records unknown small-scale power and transfer-function shape: the growth of ALP density perturbations in these nonstandard histories can put a large fraction of the local dark matter into compact minihalos, changing the smooth local density that the haloscope target bands assume, and no simulation-calibrated prediction exists for these benchmarks.
members.proposed_resolution: Simulate ALP perturbation growth through the nonstandard era (linear Boltzmann evolution of the ALP fluid during EMD/kination plus N-body follow-up of the enhanced small-scale spectrum) to predict the minihalo mass function and the surviving smooth local ALP density fraction, and propagate that fraction into the haloscope signal targets.

members.model_name: Z' portal thermal squeezeout dark-baryon model
members.description: The dark-baryon and glueball survival factors through the first-order confinement transition rest on a rough analytic pocket-contraction approximation; the source itself notes the maximum viable mass could move from O(10^6) to O(10^7) TeV, so the relic-abundance line carries an order-of-magnitude theory uncertainty.
members.proposed_resolution: Run dedicated numerical simulations of deconfined-pocket contraction and quark survival during the SU(3) confinement transition (bubble-wall dynamics plus quark transport, with lattice input for the surface tension and latent heat) to replace the analytic survival factor with a calibrated function of m_q/Lambda_D and R.

members.model_name: Composite sterile Dirac neutrino warm dark matter
members.description: The entropy dilution factor Delta ~ 1e4 required by the thermal variant depends on the degree of supercooling of the hidden-sector confining first-order phase transition, which is strongly coupled and was only estimated analytically; no nonperturbative calculation of the transition (latent heat, nucleation temperature, entropy release) exists for this composite sector.
members.proposed_resolution: Compute the confinement-transition thermodynamics nonperturbatively (lattice study of the hidden gauge group's deconfinement transition, or a calibrated holographic/PNJL effective model) and couple the resulting entropy injection to the freeze-out calculation, e.g. via a CosmoTransitions-style nucleation analysis where an effective potential is available.

members.model_name: Dark 't Hooft-Polyakov monopole dark matter from first-order SU(2)_D phase transition
members.description: The monopole production efficiency per bubble collision (factor p) in the first-order SU(2)_D -> U(1)_D transition is unsimulated; the card notes exact production depends on bubble merging and is left to future lattice simulations, so the monopole relic abundance carries an order-of-magnitude-level normalization uncertainty.
members.proposed_resolution: Run 3D classical lattice field-theory simulations of SU(2)_D-adjoint-scalar bubble nucleation, collision, and merging (extending existing bubble-collision lattice codes to a non-abelian gauge-adjoint system) to measure the monopole number produced per bubble as a function of wall velocity and beta/H, and fit a calibrated p(v_w, beta/H).

members.model_name: Defect-free dark photon dark matter
members.description: The tachyonic-resonance production of transverse dark-photon modes by the rolling scalar, including backreaction on the dark Higgs and verification that the defect-formation threshold is never crossed, is treated only with analytic estimates; no nonlinear lattice simulation of the W(phi)-coupled scalar-gauge system validates the relic abundance and momentum spectrum.
members.proposed_resolution: Run classical lattice simulations of the coupled runaway scalar, dark Higgs, and U(1)_D gauge field with the field-dependent kinetic function (extending a CosmoLattice-type code with W(phi) F_D^2 couplings) over the phi_0/f ~ 150-250 benchmark region to confirm defect-free production and extract the dark-photon spectrum.

members.model_name: Inflaton-coupled ultralight vector dark matter
members.description: No preheating simulation exists for resonant amplification of the Y_mu vector by the oscillating inflaton, so the relic abundance n_Y and its momentum spectrum — the input to every downstream observable — are only sketched qualitatively in the source.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the inflaton-U(1) system (g'''^2 Y_mu Y^mu F_0^2 coupling) in a public preheating lattice code such as CosmoLattice, or solve the linear mode equations across the resonance bands, to obtain Omega_Y and the Y momentum distribution as functions of g''' and V_0.

members.model_name: Fragmenting non-periodic-potential axion-like dark matter
members.description: No public, reusable lattice pipeline for parametric-resonance fragmentation of the non-periodic power-law ALP potential; the paper's evolved density power spectra over the (m_a, f_a, p) plane are not released, so downstream halo predictions cannot be regenerated.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the V(phi) = m_a^2 f_a^2 [(1+phi^2/f_a^2)^p - 1]-type potential in CosmoLattice, validate against the paper's fragmentation spectra and relic-density contours, and release tabulated post-fragmentation power spectra on an (m_a, f_a, p) grid.

members.model_name: WIMP dark matter inflation with a singlet scalar inflaton
members.description: The relic-density step assumes complete thermalization after Higgs-portal preheating, but no dedicated preheating/reheating calculation exists for this quartic inflaton with non-minimal coupling xi phi^2 R and portal g^2 phi^2 |H|^2, leaving the reheating temperature and thermalization assumption unverified.
members.proposed_resolution: Run a lattice preheating simulation (e.g. CosmoLattice) of the quartic inflaton with the Higgs-portal coupling, including the non-minimal coupling in the Einstein frame, to compute the reheating temperature and confirm thermalization before freeze-out.

members.model_name: Gauge-mediated Affleck-Dine Q-ball dark matter with seed PBHs
members.description: The gauge-mediated branch assumes the Affleck-Dine condensate inside small non-collapsing bubbles fragments into stable Q-balls with a survival fraction that saturates the dark-matter abundance, but no fragmentation simulation or charge-spectrum calculation for this inhomogeneous high-baryon-bubble environment exists, leaving the Q-ball relic abundance and mass spectrum unquantified.
members.proposed_resolution: Run lattice simulations of Affleck-Dine condensate fragmentation with gauge-mediated (flat) potentials inside high-baryon-bubble initial conditions to extract the Q-ball charge spectrum and surviving mass fraction as a function of c_I' and the bubble size, following existing AD fragmentation lattice studies.

members.model_name: Baby-Zilla vector dark matter from electroweak bubble collisions
members.description: The bubble-collision production yield rests on an analytic approximation for ultrarelativistic (gamma_w ~ 10^14-10^15) electroweak bubble walls; no numerical simulation of bubble collisions with Higgs-portal particle production exists to validate or calibrate the yield in this extreme-boost regime, on which the relic abundance depends exponentially.
members.proposed_resolution: Run (semi-)classical lattice simulations of colliding runaway/elastic electroweak bubble walls coupled to a heavy Higgs-portal vector, using phase-transition parameters computed with CosmoTransitions, and fit a calibrated production-efficiency function of (gamma_w, lambda_V, M_V/T_EW) that replaces the analytic source formula.

members.model_name: Chaotic braneworld inflaton-remnant dark matter
members.description: No preheating simulation validates the model's central assumption that incomplete preheating through the g^2 phi^2 chi^2 coupling leaves a residual condensate of amplitude phi_* = m/g in the brane-modified expansion history; the entire relic-abundance prediction inherits this unverified analytic estimate.
members.proposed_resolution: Run lattice preheating simulations (CosmoLattice or LATTICEEASY extended with the brane-modified Friedmann equation) for the quadratic inflaton plus g^2 phi^2 chi^2 coupling over the paper's (m/M_5, g) window, and extract the actual residual condensate amplitude and its variance against phi_* = m/g.

members.model_name: Gravitational freeze-in Dirac dark matter from Higgs preheating
members.description: No reusable lattice data products (out-of-equilibrium Higgs occupation numbers and backreaction histories over the g_quartic = (2-16)e-7, lambda_H <= 0.13 window) are public, so the gravitational freeze-in relic calculation cannot be reproduced or rescanned without redoing the nonperturbative preheating simulations.
members.proposed_resolution: Rerun the T-model inflaton plus Higgs parametric-resonance setup in a public lattice code such as CosmoLattice, publish tabulated Higgs phase-space distributions and endpoint energy densities over the scanned coupling grid, and couple them to a released implementation of the paper's gravitational production integrals.

members.model_name: Two-component baryon-scattering dark matter for cool-core cluster heating
members.description: The long-term collisional evolution of a two-component halo with a strongly self-coupled subcomponent is uncomputed: the card notes possible relaxation toward quasi-isothermal profiles and distorted (non-thermal) velocity distributions are deferred, so the assumed thermal single-temperature fluids and persistent kinetic equilibrium in clusters are unvalidated.
members.proposed_resolution: Run N-body/hydro simulations of cluster halos with a two-component dark sector (dominant CDM plus an f_chi subcomponent with baryon drag and dark self-scattering) to test kinetic-equilibrium maintenance, halo-core evolution, and the stability of the heating solution over cluster lifetimes.

members.model_name: Gauge-mediated O'Raifeartaigh R-ball dark matter
members.description: No numerical simulation exists of the fragmentation of an R-charged O'Raifeartaigh flat-direction condensate (with one-loop Coleman-Weinberg lifting) into R-balls, so the R-ball charge distribution and relic density Omega_R rely on analytic estimates carried over from ordinary Affleck-Dine Q-ball studies.
members.proposed_resolution: Adapt an existing 3D classical lattice scalar-field code used for Affleck-Dine Q-ball fragmentation (e.g. a CosmoLattice-type solver) to the R-charged X flat-direction potential with the paper's Coleman-Weinberg lifting and inflation-induced soft mass, extracting the R-ball charge spectrum and Omega_R(T_e) across the D1-D3 thermal domains.

members.model_name: Chiral vorton dark matter from Witten-type superconducting strings
members.description: The vorton relic density rests on a 1998 semi-analytic velocity-dependent one-scale network model with an uncalibrated vorton-formation efficiency and a density fit accurate mainly at s=0 and s=1; no modern superconducting-string network simulation calibrates loop production and current retention across the phase-transition-strength range.
members.proposed_resolution: Run field-theory or current-carrying Nambu-Goto network simulations of superconducting strings through the friction-dominated epoch to calibrate loop production and vorton-formation efficiency versus s, then refit the Omega_V(Gmu, s) coefficients and regime boundaries used in the analytic route.

members.model_name: Supersymmetric B-L neutralino LSP dark matter with metastable cosmic strings
members.description: The metastable-string stochastic GW prediction (h^2 Omega_GW ~ 1e-8 at interferometer frequencies) depends on cosmic-string loop distributions and monopole-nucleation decay modeling that are not calibrated for SO(10)-embedded metastable B-L strings, which the card flags as the dominant theory uncertainty.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend an existing public cosmic-string spectrum calculator to metastable strings with the sqrt(kappa) breaking parameter, calibrating the loop-number density against Nambu-Goto network simulations and quantifying the spread between loop-distribution models as a systematic band on Omega_GW(f).

members.model_name: CMSSM stop-coannihilation neutralino dark matter
members.description: The viable strip boundary depends strongly on the Higgs-mass calculator at large A_t; the paper flags FeynHiggs 2.13.0 versus other calculators as a leading uncertainty, and only an approximate likelihood treatment exists.
members.proposed_resolution: Cross-calibrate FeynHiggs against SusyHD/HimalayaLib/FlexibleSUSY along the large-A_0 stop strip and publish a per-point Higgs-mass theory-uncertainty band to use as a Gaussian likelihood instead of a hard 125 GeV cut.

members.model_name: CP-violating AKS Higgs-resonance scalar dark matter
members.description: The mapping of the AKS scalar sector onto HiggsBounds/HiggsSignals inputs (effective couplings of the CP-mixed H1,H2,H3 and H+, plus flavor observables for the charged states) has not been constructed or validated.
members.proposed_resolution: Build the coupling-input translation from the AKS parameters to HiggsBounds/HiggsSignals (and a 2HDM flavor tool such as SuperIso/FlavorKit for b->s gamma-type limits) and verify it reproduces the paper's benchmark acceptance.

members.model_name: CP-violating AKS heavy scalar dark matter
members.description: The mapping of the AKS scalar sector onto HiggsBounds/HiggsSignals inputs (effective couplings of the CP-mixed H1,H2,H3 and H+, plus flavor observables for the charged states) has not been constructed or validated.
members.proposed_resolution: Build the coupling-input translation from the AKS parameters to HiggsBounds/HiggsSignals (and a 2HDM flavor tool such as SuperIso/FlavorKit for b->s gamma-type limits) and verify it reproduces the paper's benchmark acceptance.

members.model_name: Sub-GUT stop-coannihilation neutralino dark matter
members.description: Viability of the heavy (up to 8 TeV) sub-GUT benchmarks hinges on the FeynHiggs 2.13.0 Higgs-mass prediction in an extreme large-A-term, heavy-spectrum regime where the paper itself says corroboration by independent calculators is essential.
members.proposed_resolution: Cross-check the strip-tip Higgs mass with EFT-based calculators (SusyHD, FlexibleSUSY/HSSUSY) suited to multi-TeV spectra, quantify the inter-calculator spread, and encode it as a theory-uncertainty band in the Higgs-mass filter.

members.model_name: Two-flavor chiral composite asymmetric dark matter
members.description: The dark hadron spectrum (m_A_prime, m_pi_prime, dark baryon masses) and the dark-baryon annihilation cross section rest on naive chiral-effective-theory scaling; no lattice calibration of this two-flavor SU(3) theory with chiral U(1)_D gauging pins down the O(1) factors that propagate into every downstream observable.
members.proposed_resolution: Reuse existing N_f=2 QCD-like lattice spectra rescaled to Lambda_D, and commission a lattice determination of the dark baryon sigma-term and annihilation matrix elements for the composite ADM regime.

members.model_name: Hylogenesis antibaryonic dark matter
members.description: The nucleon-to-meson hadronic matrix elements for the induced-nucleon-decay process are only estimated by analogy with standard nucleon decay; the specific neutron-portal flavor/spin contractions at IND momentum transfer have no calibrated values, leaving sigma_IND uncertain at the rate level.
members.proposed_resolution: Match the model's X U^c D^c D^c contractions onto the lattice-QCD nucleon-decay matrix-element basis (chiral-perturbation-theory extrapolated) and evaluate them at the IND kinematics, propagating the lattice uncertainties into the sigma_IND prediction.

members.model_name: Sub-MeV scalar-mediator dark matter
members.description: Target-specific response functions for scalar-mediated sub-MeV scattering in the proposed low-threshold targets (semiconductors, superconductors) are not attached to the route: the analytic cross section cannot be converted into per-detector recoil rates without material form factors and energy-loss functions for this momentum-dependent light-mediator interaction.
members.proposed_resolution: Adapt public electron-recoil response tools (DarkELF energy-loss functions for semiconductors and superconductors, QEDark-style crystal form factors) to the light-scalar-mediator matrix element with its 1/(q^2+m_phi^2)^2 momentum dependence, and add nuclear-recoil structure factors for the g_N-coupled case.

members.model_name: Scalar singlet dark matter with two-step electroweak phase transition
members.description: The two-step EWPT prediction (T_n, S3/T, and hence the GW amplitude) carries uncontrolled gauge and perturbative uncertainties from the daisy-resummed one-loop finite-temperature potential, which the card flags can shift T_n and GW amplitudes; no gauge-invariant or higher-order calibration of the transition exists for this two-singlet potential.
members.proposed_resolution: Recompute the transition in a dimensionally reduced 3d EFT (DRalgo-style construction of the two-singlet model) to obtain gauge-invariant T_n and latent heat, and propagate the uncertainty band into the GW spectrum.

members.model_name: Rapid-turn multifield inflation seeded primordial black holes
members.description: The P_zeta(k) -> beta(M) -> f_PBH(M) mapping is uncalibrated for this model: the collapse threshold and the non-Gaussianity generated by the rapid turn are unquantified, and abundance is exponentially sensitive to both, so no reliable extended mass function can be produced.
members.proposed_resolution: Compute the non-Gaussianity of zeta from the rapid-turn dynamics (e.g. with the transport bispectrum or delta-N on the numerical background), then apply a critical-collapse/compaction-function formation calculation with that non-Gaussian statistics to produce a calibrated beta(M) and extended f_PBH(M) for the feature shapes this mechanism generates.

members.model_name: Hidden supersymmetric N=1 Yang-Mills dark sector
members.description: The generalized Veneziano-Yankielowicz EFT that supplies the glueball/gluino-ball masses, mixing parameter alpha, and self-couplings is not calibrated against first-principles N=1 SYM results, so the predicted spectrum and sigma_DM/m_DM carry uncontrolled uncertainty.
members.proposed_resolution: Match the gVY EFT parameters (Lambda normalization, alpha, quartic couplings) to existing lattice N=1 SYM spectrum results (e.g. the DESY-Muenster collaboration bound-state measurements) and, where scattering data are absent, run dedicated lattice or large-N_c calculations of the lightest-multiplet 2-to-2 scattering length.

members.model_name: Composite Inelastic Dark Matter
members.description: The dark-QCD matrix elements entering the rate prediction (hyperfine splitting, meson transition form factor) are known only from analytic spin-symmetry estimates; no lattice or non-perturbative calibration of the confining SU(N_c) dark sector exists.
members.proposed_resolution: Perform a lattice or quark-model calculation of the heavy-light dark meson spectrum and the spin-0 to vector transition matrix element as functions of m_H/m_L and the confinement scale, and publish the results as a parameterized form-factor table for the recoil calculator.

members.model_name: Charged Q-ball dark matter from B and L direction
members.description: The response of ancient-mica track detection to slow, heavy, atom-like or negatively charged ion-like macroscopic relics is uncharacterized; the MICA flux bound F = 2.3e-20 cm^-2 s^-1 sr^-1 is applied under an untested assumption about stopping power and track formation for these exotic charge states.
members.proposed_resolution: Compute the electronic and nuclear stopping power and etchable-track formation threshold in muscovite mica for charged Q-balls screened by captured electrons (SRIM-style energy-loss calculation adapted to macroscopic charge Z_Q ~ alpha^-1 and mass ~1e28 GeV), and republish the mica exclusion as a charge-state-dependent flux limit.

members.model_name: Flavor-broken scalegenesis hidden-sector scalar dark matter
members.description: The hidden-sector spectrum and effective couplings rest entirely on a mean-field approximation to the strongly coupled scale-invariant SU(N_c) scalar theory, with no lattice or other non-perturbative calibration, so the mapping from fundamental quartics to m_DM, m_L, and G_phi_h carries unquantified systematic error.
members.proposed_resolution: Run lattice simulations of the SU(N_c) gauge-scalar system (or apply functional renormalization-group methods) to compute the bilinear condensate and low-lying scalar spectrum, and calibrate the mean-field masses and portal coupling against those results.

members.model_name: CMSSM Q-ball bino co-genesis dark matter
members.description: The Q-ball evaporation branching between quarks and gauginos/higgsinos, which directly sets the predicted baryon-to-dark-matter ratio, is known only to order one from analytic estimates; no simulation-calibrated treatment of Q-ball formation, charge omega_0, and decay in the relevant CMSSM flat directions exists, so the co-genesis region boundaries carry uncontrolled systematic uncertainty.
members.proposed_resolution: Run lattice simulations of Affleck-Dine condensate fragmentation and Q-ball decay for the relevant flat directions to calibrate the charge distribution and the evaporation branching into LSPs versus quarks, and publish fitted branching functions of the CMSSM spectrum for use in the co-genesis ratio formula.

members.model_name: Field-Theory String Decay WIMP dark matter with p-wave annihilation
members.description: The mapping from string tension Gmu to the injection amplitude q_X and power index p assumes field-theory strings decay predominantly into particles, a normalization that is only supported by limited Abelian-Higgs lattice simulations and is not encoded in any tool, so the reported Gmu bounds cannot be updated reliably.
members.proposed_resolution: Calibrate the (Gmu, network-decay efficiency) to (q_X, p) mapping against modern field-theory (Abelian-Higgs) lattice string-network simulations of particle emission and package it as a lookup usable by the source-term module.

members.model_name: Field-Theory String Decay WIMP dark matter with s-wave annihilation
members.description: The mapping from string tension Gmu to the injection amplitude q_X and power index p assumes field-theory strings decay predominantly into particles, a normalization that is only supported by limited Abelian-Higgs lattice simulations and is not encoded in any tool, so the reported Gmu bounds cannot be updated reliably.
members.proposed_resolution: Calibrate the (Gmu, network-decay efficiency) to (q_X, p) mapping against modern field-theory (Abelian-Higgs) lattice string-network simulations of particle emission and package it as a lookup usable by the source-term module.

members.model_name: Six-flavor quark matter nugget dark matter
members.description: No digitized, reusable compilation of macroscopic-dark-matter constraints exists in (M_nugget, R_nugget or sigma_geo, f_DM) space: the card's lensing/seismic/femtolensing constraint entry has likelihood_available: no and coverage of the 1e10 g benchmark region is patchy and undigitized.
members.proposed_resolution: Digitize the published EROS, MACHO, Subaru/HSC, femtolensing, seismic, and red-giant macro exclusion curves and package them as a maintained mass-radius constraint database (analogous to PBHbounds but with explicit cross-section dependence), including finite-size and finite-source lensing corrections relevant at R_nugget ~ 1e2 cm.

members.model_name: Sterile right-handed-neutrino dark matter from RHN oscillations
members.description: Machine-readable X-ray line limit tables (sin^2 2theta versus sterile mass from Chandra/XMM/NuSTAR searches) are not packaged with the card, so the s3 likelihood step cannot be run automatically even though the published limits exist.
members.proposed_resolution: Digitize and package the published X-ray line exclusion curves (including the NuSTAR limits cited in the card) as interpolable tables keyed to (M1, theta_active) for direct use in the route's likelihood step.

members.model_name: Cosmological gauge field dark matter
members.description: The supplemental SageMath/mpmath notebooks that implement the CGF equation of state and dark-star TOV solutions have no resolved URL, DOI, or archive location, so the paper's numerical results cannot currently be reproduced or validated.
members.proposed_resolution: Retrieve the supplemental material from the journal or arXiv source package, archive it with a DOI (e.g. Zenodo), and verify the OCR-degraded mass/radius units against the PDF; if the notebooks are unrecoverable, reimplement the analytic EoS plus TOV integration in a short Python script.

members.model_name: CKM-aligned heavy-quark freeze-in ALP dark matter
members.description: The X-ray/gamma photon-line exclusion curves (Chandra, XMM-Newton, NuSTAR, INTEGRAL, COMPTEL, EGRET) are imported at figure level and not digitized into machine-readable limit tables on tau_a(m_a), so the decay constraint cannot be re-evaluated programmatically over the model's parameter space.
members.proposed_resolution: Digitize the compiled keV-MeV decaying-dark-matter line and diffuse-continuum limits into tabulated tau_a lower bounds versus m_a (drawing on existing public compilations of X-ray/gamma decay constraints) and attach them as a lookup likelihood to the decay step.

members.model_name: Single-flavor-transition heavy-quark freeze-in ALP dark matter
members.description: The X-ray/gamma photon-line exclusion curves (Chandra, XMM-Newton, NuSTAR, INTEGRAL, COMPTEL, EGRET) are imported at figure level and not digitized into machine-readable limit tables on tau_a(m_a), so the decay constraint cannot be re-evaluated programmatically over the model's parameter space.
members.proposed_resolution: Digitize the compiled keV-MeV decaying-dark-matter line and diffuse-continuum limits into tabulated tau_a lower bounds versus m_a (drawing on existing public compilations of X-ray/gamma decay constraints) and attach them as a lookup likelihood to the decay step.

members.model_name: mu-negative 4-2-2 Yukawa-unified neutralino dark matter
members.description: No machine-readable scan table or benchmark-point file for the paper's allowed regions was extracted (constraint caveat: 'No machine-readable scan table was extracted'), so the quoted benchmark classes and the ~43 GeV lightest-neutralino point cannot be reproduced or recast without regenerating the scan from scratch.
