members.description: No public simulation or calibrated semi-analytic pipeline converts an Affleck-Dine flat-direction condensate (given initial charge density and potential shape) into a Q-ball charge distribution; the paper relies on linear-instability estimates and identifies the nonlinear fragmentation as unsolved future work.
members.proposed_resolution: Run 3D lattice simulations of a complex scalar with MSSM flat-direction potentials (adapting a public lattice code such as CosmoLattice or GABE to conserved-charge initial conditions), scan initial charge density and potential flatness, and fit the resulting Q-ball charge distribution into a reusable semi-analytic emulator.

members.model_name: Axion quark nugget dark matter
members.description: The AQN-visible-matter annihilation efficiency kappa, which multiplies every environmental heating and radiation prediction, has no first-principles calculation or empirical calibration (card status: unknown), leaving all environment-dependent rates uncertain by an unquantified factor.
members.proposed_resolution: Perform a dedicated microphysical calculation of matter accretion and annihilation on a color-superconducting nugget surface with its electrosphere (velocity, density, and ionization dependence of kappa), and publish kappa(n, v, T) tables usable by the heating step.

members.model_name: Gluophilic Z-prime portal FIMP dark matter
members.description: The ATLAS 139 fb^-1 monojet exclusion (A sigma > 0.3 fb at E_T^miss > 1200 GeV) is applied at parton level with approximated selection efficiency, so the collider bound and Run-3 projections carry uncontrolled detector-level systematics for this UFO model.
members.proposed_resolution: Run the gluophilic Z-prime UFO through MadGraph5+Pythia8 showering and a validated detector-level recast of the ATLAS monojet analysis (CheckMATE or MadAnalysis5 PAD implementation) to replace the parton-level cutflow with full-efficiency exclusion contours.

members.model_name: Post-recombination reheating decaying cold dark matter
members.description: The near-blackbody photon-injection assumption that underlies the entire scenario has not been checked with a thermalization calculation: no computation exists of the FIRAS mu/y distortion produced by this model's post-recombination (z_X ~ 40-190) photon injection for a given microphysical spectrum.
members.proposed_resolution: Run a CosmoTherm-style (or Chluba Green's-function) thermalization calculation for candidate injected spectra, e.g. the 0.1 eV excited-state dark-photon line, and map out which (f_DCDM, z_X, spectrum) regions survive the FIRAS distortion limits.

members.model_name: Nambu-Goto Cusp Emission WIMP dark matter with p-wave annihilation
members.description: The mapping from string tension Gmu and Nambu-Goto network evolution to the injection amplitude q_X and power index p is only a normalization assumption; no simulation-calibrated cusp-emission efficiency is encoded in any tool, so the reported Gmu bounds cannot be updated reliably.
members.proposed_resolution: Calibrate the (Gmu, loop-size distribution) to (q_X, p) mapping against modern Nambu-Goto string-network simulations of cusp particle emission and package it as a lookup usable by the source-term module.

members.model_name: Nambu-Goto Cusp Emission WIMP dark matter with s-wave annihilation
members.description: The mapping from string tension Gmu and Nambu-Goto network evolution to the injection amplitude q_X and power index p is only a normalization assumption; no simulation-calibrated cusp-emission efficiency is encoded in any tool, so the reported Gmu bounds cannot be updated reliably.
members.proposed_resolution: Calibrate the (Gmu, loop-size distribution) to (q_X, p) mapping against modern Nambu-Goto string-network simulations of cusp particle emission and package it as a lookup usable by the source-term module.

members.model_name: CP-conserving complex singlet scalar dark matter with biased domain walls
members.description: The possible nonthermal dark-matter contribution from direct domain-wall collapse is noted in the card as unresolved: no derivation exists of the Im S yield and momentum distribution produced when the biased walls annihilate, which could shift the relic-density viable region away from the pure freeze-out result.
members.proposed_resolution: Derive the particle-production yield from wall annihilation (energy budget of the network times the branching into Im S quanta, cross-checked against lattice-simulation energy loss rates) and add it as a nonthermal correction to the micrOMEGAs freeze-out abundance across the PTA-favorable v_S range.

members.model_name: Inflection-point inflation primordial black-hole dark matter
members.description: The scalar-induced stochastic gravitational-wave background sourced by the enhanced small-scale spectrum is identified as an observable but was not computed, so no prediction exists to compare with GW detectors.
members.proposed_resolution: Feed the computed P_R(k) through the standard second-order induced-GW kernel integrals using a public implementation such as SIGWfast, including the reheating-era equation-of-state dependence already parameterized by w_reh.

members.model_name: Nonzero-initial-velocity axion misalignment dark matter
members.description: No implemented calculator exists for the stochastic gravitational-wave spectrum sourced by a rotating/kinetic ALP with gauge-field couplings; the card only cites related-paper formulae without a usable spectrum pipeline for this model's parameter space.
members.proposed_resolution: Derive and implement the GW spectrum from the rotating-ALP gauge-field instability following the related kinetic-misalignment papers, parameterized by (f_a, alpha/f_a, dot_theta_i), and output Omega_GW(f) for comparison with PTA and interferometer sensitivity curves.

members.model_name: Low-scale hypercolor axion-domain-wall dark sector
members.description: No gravitational-wave spectrum has been computed for the low-scale HC confinement transition and collapsing wall network: the transition strength, latent heat, and wall-tension parameters needed to evaluate Omega_GW(f) in the nanohertz band were never extracted, leaving only a qualitative detectability claim.
members.proposed_resolution: Compute the HC confinement transition parameters (alpha, beta/H, wall tension) using holographic or matrix-model estimates for pure-glue SU(N) at Lambda_HC ~ 0.1-1 MeV, feed them into standard first-order-transition and domain-wall GW spectrum templates (e.g. via CosmoTransitions plus PTArcade-style PTA sensitivity overlays), and compare against NANOGrav/SKA curves.

members.model_name: Feebly coupled U(1)_X hidden-sector dark fermion dark matter
members.description: The GW amplitude relies on hydrodynamic fitting formulae calibrated to visible-sector transitions; the bubble wall velocity and sound-wave efficiency for a transition in a colder, feebly coupled hidden plasma (friction only from hidden species) are uncalibrated inputs scanned as free parameters.
members.proposed_resolution: Compute the bubble wall velocity from hidden-sector friction (extending existing wall-velocity codes to the U(1)_X particle content) and recalibrate kappa_sw efficiency factors with hydrodynamic simulations for the relevant alpha and xi range, replacing the flat v_w in (0,1) scan.

members.model_name: Yukawa-coupled dark sector model
members.description: Nonlinear structure is not modeled for this scenario: the scale-dependent coupled growth invalidates LCDM-calibrated halofit/HMcode prescriptions, degrading the DES-Y3 weak-lensing (S8) side of the analysis, which probes mildly nonlinear scales.
members.proposed_resolution: Run a small suite of N-body simulations with the scalar-dependent CDM mass and fifth-force terms (e.g. extending an interacting-dark-energy N-body code) to recalibrate a halofit/HMcode-style nonlinear boost over the viable beta and EDE parameter range.

members.model_name: Gauged U(1)_X vector Higgs-portal dark matter
members.description: The GW spectrum and detectability classification rest on assumed bubble-wall velocities and standard sound-wave efficiency fits not calibrated for this dark-sector multi-step transition, which the card flags as the dominant reach uncertainty.
members.proposed_resolution: Compute the bubble-wall velocity and hydrodynamic efficiency for representative benchmarks using current friction/hydrodynamics frameworks, and propagate updated sound-wave spectral fits into the GW-reach classification.

members.model_name: Thermal-equilibrium fermionic WDM primordial-spectrum model
members.description: The Press-Schechter halo mass function for this suppressed FD spectrum is not calibrated against WDM N-body simulations (card: simulation_calibrated partial; caveat that PS predictions need simulation calibration), degrading the delayed-halo-formation prediction at z ~ 4-12.
members.proposed_resolution: Calibrate a sharp-k or modified-barrier mass function against existing thermal-WDM N-body suites, parameterized by k_1/2/R_1/2 so the calibration transfers across the paper's variants, and adopt the calibrated form in place of raw Press-Schechter.

members.model_name: Light scalar dark matter clumps with angular momentum
members.description: The model predicts no cosmological clump abundance: the mass function, halo fraction, and angular-momentum distribution of clumps are unspecified (the card notes 'no cosmological abundance for these clumps is derived'), so no event-rate or flux prediction can be normalized.
members.proposed_resolution: Derive the clump mass and angular-momentum distribution from structure-formation simulations of the post-misalignment axion/scalar field (kinetic-relaxation or miniclusters-to-solitons pipelines), parameterized by (m, f_a, lambda), and store it as the input mass function for the microlensing and radio routes.

members.model_name: Ultralight axion dark matter from a dark SU(3)d confining phase transition
members.description: No calculation exists of the dark SU(3)d confining first-order phase-transition thermodynamics (latent heat/strength alpha, inverse duration beta/H, bubble-wall dynamics) at Lambda_a ~ 10 keV, which sets both the GW spectrum amplitude and the PBH-formation efficiency.
members.proposed_resolution: Compute the SU(3) pure-gauge (plus heavy vector-like quark) confinement transition parameters from existing lattice thermodynamics data or a matrix/Polyakov-loop effective model, then feed alpha and beta/H into standard FOPT GW fit formulas (Caprini-et-al templates as implemented in PTPlot-style calculators).

members.model_name: Gravitational-genesis two-component dark matter
members.description: No detector response model exists for Planck-scale PBH relics: the card notes the relic interaction channel (neutral geometric versus charged) is unspecified, so the direct-detection observable cannot be forward-modeled at all.
members.proposed_resolution: Specify the relic interaction model (neutral geometric cross section versus charged relic), derive the corresponding terrestrial flux and energy-deposition signature, and recast onto existing macroscopic/charged-relic search limits such as those framed for charged Planck-scale relics in the cited related work.

members.model_name: Spiked extended primordial black-hole mass-function dark matter
members.description: The modified Press-Schechter formalism is unreliable when the spike mass lies far below the extended-distribution cutoff, and the paper ignores the nonlinear enhancement expected for the strong spiked power spectrum, so the predicted mass function is uncalibrated in exactly the spiked regime of interest.
members.proposed_resolution: Recompute PBH formation from the spiked spectrum with peaks theory plus a nonlinear collapse-threshold treatment calibrated on numerical-relativity simulations of critical collapse (delta_c and mass-scaling for narrow spikes), and publish the corrected mass function as a drop-in replacement for the Press-Schechter step.

members.model_name: Hidden monopole dark matter via axion portal
members.description: The monopole relic fraction rests on a Kibble-Zurek estimate with order-of-magnitude uncertainty from the critical exponent and monopole-antimonopole annihilation modeling; no simulation-calibrated prediction of hidden SU(2) monopole production at a second-order phase transition exists for this parameter range.
members.proposed_resolution: Run classical-statistical lattice field-theory simulations of the SU(2)_H second-order phase transition (Kibble-Zurek defect formation plus subsequent monopole-antimonopole annihilation) to calibrate the relic-fraction formula against the critical exponent used in the benchmark.

members.model_name: Charged Planck-scale relic dark matter
members.description: No detector-response simulation exists for the CPR signature: energy deposition, ionization, scintillation, and bubble-nucleation yields for an order-e charged Planck-mass object moving at halo velocity, a regime (very slow, very heavy, straight track) outside the calibration range of standard SRIM/Geant4 workflows for each candidate technology.
members.proposed_resolution: Compute low-velocity electronic and nuclear stopping power for a unit-charge Planck-mass projectile (Lindhard-type formalism cross-checked with SRIM tables) and implement the track response in Geant4-style simulations for bubble chambers, liquid argon TPCs, and paleo-detector minerals, validating against published slow-monopole response studies.

members.model_name: Bubbletron-produced heavy fermion dark matter
members.description: The GW prediction rests on the untested assumption that the bulk-flow model captures the stress-energy of colliding ultra-relativistic free-streaming gauge shells; no simulation of shell collisions in this regime calibrates the spectrum amplitude and shape.
members.proposed_resolution: Run lattice or many-bubble semi-analytic simulations of colliding thin relativistic shells (extending existing bubble-collision GW codes to the free-streaming shell limit) and fit a calibrated correction to the bulk-flow template over the relevant gamma_coll and beta/H range.

members.model_name: Scalar-condensate electroweak non-restoration dark matter
members.description: The SNR mechanism assumes the initial charge asymmetry thermalizes into a Bose-Einstein condensate and that the condensate later evaporates leaving v_phi(0)=0; no nonperturbative simulation of condensate formation, stability, and evaporation in the electroweak plasma exists to validate this window, and public finite-temperature tools (e.g. CosmoTransitions) do not handle scalar potentials at finite charge chemical potential.
members.proposed_resolution: Run real-time classical-statistical lattice simulations of the charged scalar plus Higgs system at finite charge density to test condensate thermalization and evaporation, and extend a finite-temperature effective-potential code (e.g. CosmoTransitions) to include a charge chemical potential for the SNR condition scan.

members.model_name: Axion-SU(2) inflation vector boson dark matter
members.description: No worked recast maps published dark-photon dark-matter limits onto this model: the effective kinetic mixing epsilon ~ lambda m^2/(g^2 f^2) applies to only one of three degenerate SU(2) components, so limits must be rescaled by component fraction and degeneracy-breaking assumptions, and the cluster sigma/m ~ g^4/m^3 comparison is only a dimensional estimate with unquantified wave-regime corrections.
members.proposed_resolution: Derive the mixed-component energy fraction and effective epsilon across the (m, g, f) plane, rescale existing dark-photon DM absorption/haloscope exclusions by that fraction, and compute the actual non-Abelian vector self-scattering cross section (including wave-regime suppression at low m) for comparison with cluster sigma/m bounds.

members.model_name: Conformal freeze-in composite dark-pion dark matter
members.description: Stellar emission rates of dark-sector states through the suppressed portal have not been calculated for this model, so stellar-cooling bounds on light benchmarks cannot be evaluated beyond threshold arithmetic.
members.proposed_resolution: Derive dark-sector emission rates from stellar plasmas (plasmon mixing into the composite dark photon and CFT-state pair emission) as a function of (T_S, m_gap, epsilon), then compare against standard HB/RGB/SN energy-loss budgets to obtain cooling exclusions.

members.model_name: Non-minimally coupled relativistic BEC dark matter
members.description: Solar-system and local-gravity compatibility of the derivative coupling is argued only qualitatively (baryon dominance and constant local DM density); no quantitative PPN or fifth-force recast of the L^2 G_mu_nu operator with realistic local dark-matter density gradients exists.
members.proposed_resolution: Derive the PPN-level corrections induced by the derivative coupling for a local condensate density profile and compare them to Solar System (Cassini, lunar laser ranging) bounds, producing an exclusion region in the (L, local density gradient) plane.

members.model_name: Inhomogeneous dilaton oscillaton dark matter
members.description: The dilaton's coupling to ordinary matter has not been derived and recast against laboratory tests: the fifth-force and varying-constant risk from the nearly massless uncooled component is flagged only qualitatively, with no quantitative Eotvos/PPN exclusion in the model's (xi, coupling, effective mass) space.
members.proposed_resolution: Derive the effective dilaton-matter coupling in the Einstein frame from the given scalar-tensor action and compare it to equivalence-principle, PPN, and varying-constant bounds, producing the allowed region or the required screening condition.

members.model_name: Kreuzer-Skarke type IIB axiverse dark matter ensemble
members.description: Black-hole superradiance constraints must be recast spectrum-by-spectrum for each KS toy model, but no recast tables exist that account for the dense hierarchical mass spectra and quartic self-interactions that can quench superradiant growth (the primary paper defers this treatment).
members.proposed_resolution: Generate superradiance exclusion tables over (m_a, f_a) including self-interaction quenching using existing superradiance evolution codes and astrophysical BH mass-spin catalogs, then apply them per KS mass spectrum as a lookup in the population scan.

members.model_name: Self-interacting warm dark matter
members.description: The Boltzmann hierarchy uses a relaxation-time approximation with interpolated rates in intermediate regimes and neglects the mediator population; the accuracy of tau_rel-based perturbation evolution against the full collision integral has not been quantified for the massive-scalar and massive-vector cases, limiting confidence in the CMB-era predictions.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the full elastic collision integral for the scalar and vector amplitude ansatz in a Boltzmann code for a few benchmark points (following full-collision-term treatments developed for neutrino self-interactions) and calibrate or correct the relaxation-time tables in siwdm-class against it.

members.model_name: Composite pNGB dark matter with a massless dark photon
members.description: Halo-shape constraints on long-range (unscreened Coulomb-like) dark-photon-mediated self-interactions are not simulation-calibrated for this model: the quoted NGC720 ellipticity bound has been substantially revised in the literature and there is no validated likelihood connecting alpha_D/m_phi to halo-shape data.
members.proposed_resolution: Run cosmological or isolated-halo N-body simulations with a velocity-dependent, forward-peaked long-range scattering kernel appropriate to massless-mediator exchange, calibrate ellipticity and density-profile observables against elliptical-galaxy and cluster data, and release the resulting bound as a likelihood over alpha_D/m_phi.

members.model_name: Starobinsky-produced dark SU(N) glueball dark matter
members.description: The glueball self-interaction cross section sigma/m and the 3-to-2 number-changing rates are known only up to large-N naive-dimensional-analysis factors; these O(1)-or-worse uncertainties directly move the viability boundary in (Lambda, N).
members.proposed_resolution: Use lattice determinations of SU(N) glueball spectra and extract the elastic and 3-to-2 glueball couplings from lattice matrix elements (or large-N chiral-Lagrangian fits to existing lattice data) to replace the NDA estimates.

members.model_name: Dodelson-Widrow sterile-neutrino WDM spectrum model
members.description: The Press-Schechter halo mass function used for the delayed-structure observable is not simulation-calibrated for this variant's non-thermal cutoff spectrum (card marks simulation_calibrated: partial and caveats that PS needs calibration).
members.proposed_resolution: Calibrate a sharp-k/smooth-k mass-function barrier against a small suite of N-body simulations run with Dodelson-Widrow transfer functions over z=4-12, and release the fit as a drop-in replacement for the PS step.

members.model_name: Shi-Fuller resonant sterile-neutrino WDM spectrum model
members.description: The Press-Schechter halo mass function used for the delayed-structure observable is not simulation-calibrated for this variant's resonant cutoff spectrum (card marks simulation_calibrated: partial and caveats that PS needs calibration).
members.proposed_resolution: Calibrate a sharp-k/smooth-k mass-function barrier against a small suite of N-body simulations run with resonant Shi-Fuller transfer functions over z=4-12, and release the fit as a drop-in replacement for the PS step.

members.model_name: Dodelson-Widrow sterile-neutrino WDM halo model
members.description: The DW interpretation rests on an approximate scaling of a gravitino/thermal WDM transfer function to sterile-neutrino masses, and the underlying simulations omit random thermal velocities, so predictions are not calibrated on the true non-thermal DW phase-space distribution.
members.proposed_resolution: Compute the exact DW momentum distribution with the public sterile-dm code, feed it to CLASS/CAMB as an ncdm species to get the true T_wdm(k), and recalibrate the halo-model ingredients on a small suite of WDM N-body simulations that include thermal velocities.

members.model_name: Resonant MSM sterile-neutrino dark matter with technically natural N2-N3 degeneracy
members.description: Existing resonant sterile-neutrino production codes (Shi-Fuller type, e.g. sterile-dm) take a static pre-set lepton asymmetry and are not calibrated for the time-dependent asymmetry sourced by N2/N3 decays at T ~ 100 MeV in this scenario, so the N1 momentum distribution f_N1(p) is only approximately computable.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend a public Shi-Fuller production code to accept a time-dependent lepton-asymmetry history (coupled to the gap_1 solver output) and validate the resulting f_N1(p) against the published resonant-production spectra of the related nuMSM abundance papers.

members.model_name: keV sterile neutrino dark matter in a minimal extended seesaw A4 model
members.description: No Ly-alpha forest or phase-space likelihood is available for the nonthermal sterile-neutrino momentum distribution of this model; existing Ly-alpha likelihoods and emulators are calibrated on thermal-WDM transfer functions, and the mapping for Dodelson-Widrow versus Shi-Fuller spectra is production-mechanism dependent.
members.proposed_resolution: Feed the production-solver momentum distribution into CLASS/CAMB to obtain the linear transfer function, then recast onto an existing Ly-alpha flux-power likelihood or emulator (thermal-WDM-equivalent mapping validated against non-resonant and resonant spectra), and add the Tremaine-Gunn phase-space bound analytically.

members.model_name: Non-resonant sterile neutrino dark matter
members.description: No packaged X-ray decay-line likelihood exists for arbitrary (m_s, sin^2(2 theta)): the Chandra M31 bound on the card is a fixed published limit tied to Dodelson-Widrow assumptions, with no rerunnable line-flux calculator plus instrument/background model to recast it across the parameter plane or newer datasets.
members.proposed_resolution: Build a decay-flux likelihood module combining the standard Gamma(m_s, theta) radiative rate with dark-matter column-density models for M31/clusters/blank-sky fields and digitized flux limits from Chandra, XMM, and NuSTAR analyses, exposing it as a function of (m_s, sin^2(2 theta)) times the model's computed relic fraction.

members.model_name: Non-resonant sterile neutrino dark matter
members.description: The Ly-alpha constraint is applied only through an approximate thermal-equivalent WDM mass mapping; no pipeline evaluates a Ly-alpha flux-power likelihood directly on transfer functions computed from the actual non-resonant sterile-neutrino f_s(p), and hydrodynamical/IGM-thermal uncertainties are not propagated.
members.proposed_resolution: Interface the CLASS NCDM transfer functions generated from the sterile-dm distribution with an existing public Ly-alpha likelihood or emulator (e.g. the BOSS/eBOSS flux-power likelihood used in non-cold dark matter analyses such as 1706.03118, with marginalized IGM thermal-history nuisance parameters) to bound m_s directly rather than via the thermal-mass proxy.

members.model_name: Gravitationally produced sterile neutrino dark matter
members.description: No digitized, reusable likelihood exists for the sterile-neutrino decay constraints relevant here: the NuSTAR 10-50 keV X-ray line limits, CMB distortion bounds, and Dodelson-Widrow overproduction contours are only available as published figures assuming a fully thermal-relic population, not recast for a cold gravitational relic with free abundance fraction and mixing angle theta.
members.proposed_resolution: Digitize the NuSTAR/X-ray, CMB-distortion, and Dodelson-Widrow exclusion curves from the cited sources into (M, theta) data tables, and wrap them in a likelihood that rescales line-flux limits by the model's predicted abundance fraction and adds the thermal DW contribution computed from theta, so the gravitational-production parameter space can be scored directly.

members.model_name: Freeze-twin electron and positron dark matter
members.description: The asymmetric-reheating depletion of the twin sector is an unspecified initial condition: without a quantitative depletion model there is no way to compute the residual twin radiation Delta N_eff or a possible mirror-baryon subcomponent that the relic and CMB comparisons assume negligible.
members.proposed_resolution: Specify and solve a concrete asymmetric-reheating implementation (e.g. late decay of a reheaton preferentially into the SM sector) coupled to the Higgs-portal heat-flow equations, deriving the twin-sector temperature history and Delta N_eff at BBN/CMB as a function of the depletion efficiency.

members.model_name: Many-copy Standard Model hidden-baryon dark matter
members.description: The optional millicharged hidden-baryon detection channel has no defined interaction model: the millicharge epsilon is not specified and no scattering or annihilation rate model exists to recast against direct or indirect searches.
members.proposed_resolution: Specify a concrete kinetic-mixing/millicharge benchmark for the hidden photon copies, derive the hidden-baryon-nucleus and hidden-baryon-electron scattering cross sections as functions of epsilon and mass, and recast against existing millicharged-DM direct-detection and CMB limits.

members.model_name: Approximate-PQ electroweak supersymmetry with singlino LSP dark matter
members.description: The pre-BBN entropy-generation mechanism required to dilute the thermal singlino abundance by 10^4-10^5*(m_s/100 keV) is not specified, so the post-dilution singlino phase-space distribution needed for all downstream cosmology cannot be derived.
members.proposed_resolution: Specify a concrete dilution model (e.g. a late-decaying heavy field or the G sector itself) and derive the resulting singlino f(p) and reheated N_eff analytically, parameterized by the decay temperature and dilution factor D, so the pipeline is closed without leaving D a free hand-put number.

members.model_name: Fragmenting non-periodic-potential axion-like dark matter
members.description: No event-level likelihood exists for dense-minihalo encounters with stellar streams (GD-1-like gaps) or pulsar-timing arrays for this model; the card frames both channels as qualitative prospects with encounter-rate and population modeling absent.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend existing GD-1 subhalo-impact inference frameworks and PTA Doppler/Shapiro static-limit searches to the model's minihalo mass function and density profiles, folding in the encounter-rate calculation from the predicted halo population.

members.model_name: Vector wave dark matter in the nonrelativistic Schrödinger-Poisson limit
members.description: No likelihood exists for vector wave dark matter against dwarf-galaxy core, stellar-stream heating, or substructure data, and the lowest-energy vector soliton is density-degenerate with the scalar case, so scalar fuzzy-DM bounds cannot be recast without vector-specific (spin/polarization and multi-component) corrections.
members.proposed_resolution: Recast existing scalar fuzzy-DM dwarf-core and stream-heating likelihoods by replacing the scalar core-halo relation and granule statistics with the vector-calibrated versions from gap_2, and add spin/polarization-sensitive observables to break the scalar-vector density degeneracy.

members.model_name: Dissipative dark electromagnetism model
members.description: No likelihood connects the predicted compact collapsed dark substructures to data; the card's caveat notes no microlensing (or other compact-object) likelihood was run, and con_self_scattering_dao_window has likelihood_available: no with recasting needed.
members.proposed_resolution: Once a collapsed-object mass function exists (gap_1), recast it through existing compact-object constraint machinery: microlensing survey likelihoods, stellar-stream perturbation likelihoods, and strong-lensing substructure likelihoods parameterized by object mass and compactness.

members.model_name: Freeze-twin electron and positron dark matter
members.description: No supernova-cooling likelihood or recast exists for the twin sector: existing dark-photon SN1987A cooling bounds do not include the twin-electron pair-production and trapping channels of this model, so the epsilon-m_gamma_prime cooling region is only a qualitative overlay.
members.proposed_resolution: Adapt an existing dark-photon supernova energy-loss calculation (Chang-Essig-McDermott-style, including finite-temperature mixing and trapping) to add twin-electron final states, and publish the resulting exclusion contour as a reusable likelihood in the epsilon-m_gamma_prime plane.

members.model_name: Non-Abelian Goldstone absorption dark matter
members.description: No likelihood or systematic recast exists for the combined cosmological and stellar-cooling bounds on the Goldstone coupling scale (likelihood_available is 'no', recasting_needed is 'yes'), so the constraint overlay on the absorption signal is only qualitative.
members.proposed_resolution: Recast published stellar-cooling (red giant, horizontal branch, supernova) and overproduction limits into the (m_pi, Lambda) plane for each choice of flavor generator, and package them as a simple bound-overlay likelihood alongside the absorption-rate prediction.

members.model_name: Charged-excitation WIMP Case A
members.description: No reusable likelihood exists for MeV-scale energy deposits in EXO-200, KamLAND-Zen, SNO, and Borexino: only published high-energy spectra with conservative background subtraction were used, and detector effects such as gamma escape can shift limits by a factor of about two.
members.proposed_resolution: Digitize the published high-energy event spectra, model each detector's response (energy resolution, gamma-escape probability, fiducial acceptance) with a lightweight Monte Carlo, and package a binned Poisson likelihood over (Delta m, tau, capture rate), extendable to current-generation data such as KamLAND-Zen 800 and nEXO projections.

members.model_name: Sterile-neutrino portal interacting fermion dark matter
members.description: No public semi-analytic subhalo pipeline maps the sterile-neutrino-portal DM-neutrino scattering (constant and T^2 cross-section regimes, T_kd around 0.1-1 keV) through the dark-acoustic transfer-function cutoff to Milky Way satellite abundances with an attached likelihood.
members.proposed_resolution: Feed CLASS_nu-DM transfer functions into an existing semi-analytic subhalo code (e.g. SASHIMI or Galacticus) with a satellite-forming condition, and couple the resulting subhalo mass function to the public DES/Pan-STARRS1 Milky Way satellite likelihood used for WDM-style suppression models.

members.model_name: Invisible dilaton misalignment dark matter
members.description: No public solver exists for the screened scalar-field profile around finite-size sources with the model's quadratic m_f phi^2/Lambda_f^2 matter coupling; the paper's analytic screened/unscreened limits do not cover general source densities and Newtonian potentials needed for Earth, satellite, and test-mass geometries.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement a 1D/3D nonlinear Klein-Gordon boundary-value solver (extending existing chameleon/symmetron screening codes such as those used for fifth-force forecasts) parameterized by (m_phi, Lambda_f, source density profile, ambient condensate amplitude), validated against the paper's screened and unscreened analytic limits.

members.model_name: axino LSP superWIMP dark matter
members.description: The forward-model chain has no step computing the decay-produced axino velocity distribution or the suppressed matter transfer function, so the warm-dark-matter-like small-scale suppression observable cannot be evaluated beyond qualitative statements (phase_space distribution_function_available: no).
members.proposed_resolution: Add a transfer-function step using the public two-body decaying-CDM CLASS extension, feeding the parent lifetime and mass splitting to obtain the daughter phase-space distribution and free-streaming cutoff, then compare against Ly-alpha and satellite-count WDM bounds.

members.model_name: U(1) late-decaying dark matter
members.description: No worked nonthermal production mechanism exists for chi/chi*: the paper shows Standard Model mixing production falls short by orders of magnitude, so the relic abundance and the initial momentum distribution (distribution_function_available: unknown) are unspecified rather than derived.
members.proposed_resolution: Derive a concrete production channel — e.g. freeze-in through the weak-bath mixing at higher temperatures or a direct inflaton coupling — and compute the resulting abundance and f(p), which would also fix any free-streaming imprint on the linear power spectrum.

members.model_name: Quantum-environment dark neutrino dark matter component
members.description: No Lagrangian-level or kinetic-theory formulation of the pure-dephasing dark-neutrino coupling exists, so the early-universe production rate, relic fraction f_dark_nu, and momentum distribution f(p) of the dark-neutrino component cannot be derived; without f(p) no free-streaming scale or transfer function can be computed.
members.proposed_resolution: Promote the Kraus-operator dephasing map to an interaction model (e.g. an effective neutrino-baryon operator generating the dephasing channel), derive the dark-neutrino production rate and f(p) via early-universe scattering kinetics, then evaluate the mixed hot/warm/cold transfer function with CLASS multi-ncdm species using the tabulated distribution.

members.model_name: Confined colored relic dark matter
members.description: No controlled calculation of the quarkonium (X Xbar) bound-state formation cross section sigma_BSF in the strong-coupling confining regime; the card notes only tractable toy limits bracket the radiation/rearrangement rates, and this uncertainty dominates the relic abundance.
members.proposed_resolution: Derive sigma_BSF from a lattice or NRQCD-style effective-theory calculation of heavy-light hadron rearrangement in a dark SU(N), parameterized by m_X/Lambda_D and m_q/Lambda_D, and publish it as a tabulated cross-section model usable in a Boltzmann code.

members.model_name: Fermionic dark matter with scalar mediator for electroweak baryogenesis
members.description: The electroweak phase-transition assessment relies on a gauge-dependent high-temperature analytic potential without bubble-nucleation dynamics, so the EWBG viability region carries uncontrolled theoretical uncertainty.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement V_eff(h,s,T) in CosmoTransitions to compute the nucleation temperature and transition strength with daisy resummation, and compare a gauge-invariant criterion against the paper's v_c/T_c > 1 analytic condition.

members.model_name: Non-thermal electroweak-phase-transition vector WIMP dark matter
members.description: The bubble-collision production efficiency entering the source term is an uncalibrated analytic approximation whose output the paper itself notes is extremely sensitive to the strength and wall dynamics of the first-order electroweak phase transition.
members.proposed_resolution: Compute the phase-transition strength and wall Lorentz factor for concrete Higgs-sector completions with CosmoTransitions and calibrate the particle-production efficiency against numerical bubble-collision simulations, replacing gamma_w as a free input with a derived quantity.

members.model_name: Fermionic dark matter with pseudoscalar mediator for electroweak baryogenesis
members.description: The electroweak phase-transition assessment relies on a gauge-dependent high-temperature analytic potential without bubble-nucleation dynamics, so the EWBG viability region carries uncontrolled theoretical uncertainty.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement V_eff(h,s,T) in CosmoTransitions to compute the nucleation temperature and transition strength with daisy resummation, and compare a gauge-invariant criterion against the paper's v_c/T_c > 1 analytic condition.

members.model_name: cosmological wetting transition scalar dark matter
members.description: No quantitative criterion or numerical model exists for when the chi symmetry-breaking transition is blocked in overdense environments: the survival of cold dark matter in galaxies and clusters rests on a qualitative stalled-expansion argument with no density/temperature threshold, bubble-nucleation treatment, or halo-scale simulation.
members.proposed_resolution: Derive the local effective chi potential as a function of ambient density and expansion rate, obtain the critical overdensity for transition blocking (including bubble nucleation rates via a CosmoTransitions-style bounce calculation in the local background), and validate it with a semi-analytic spherical-collapse or small-volume N-body treatment of the coupled fields.

members.model_name: CGF cosmological SU(2)-weak gauge-field dark matter stars
members.description: The abundance distribution of CGF dark matter stars along the mass-radius curve — i.e. the formation history and mass function from gravitational collapse of initial CGF fluctuations — has not been computed, so no halo-population prediction (lensing optical depth, event rates, transition rates) can be made despite the M(R) curve being known.
members.proposed_resolution: Derive the star mass function from first principles as the paper suggests: evolve initial CGF fluctuations through collapse with hydrodynamic/GR simulations of the CGF perfect fluid (Press-Schechter-style collapse statistics as a first pass), yielding the number density of stars per mass bin on the TOV curve.

members.model_name: Dark atoms with massive dark photon and millicharged subcomponent
members.description: Direct-detection rates for neutral dark-hydrogen dipole scattering require the atomic charge form factor and ionized/neutral fraction weighting; no reusable rate code or likelihood implements this beyond the paper's constraint overlays (point-particle millicharge limits are insufficient).
members.proposed_resolution: Derive the dark-hydrogen induced-dipole scattering cross section with the atomic form factor as a function of (alpha_D, B_D, m_A, a_D), implement it as a custom cross-section module in DDCalc or an equivalent rate calculator, and weight ion and neutral channels by f_e.

members.model_name: Conformal freeze-in quark-portal dark matter
members.description: Existing Lyman-alpha flux-power likelihoods and emulators are calibrated on thermal-WDM (or sterile-neutrino) transfer functions and are not validated for COFI nonthermal spectra, so a one-to-one thermal-WDM mass mapping can misstate the excluded quark-portal region.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend a Lyman-alpha emulator to accept generalized transfer-function shape parameters (e.g. the alpha-beta-gamma parameterization of noncold DM cutoffs) and validate it on CLASS transfer functions computed from COFI f(q) ansatzes before deriving exclusion contours.

members.model_name: Intermediate-mass pseudo-Goldstone boson partial dark matter
members.description: The strongest historical constraint comes from the Lyman-alpha forest, but existing Lyman-alpha flux-power emulators and hydro-simulation grids are calibrated for pure WDM or full-density ultralight axions, not a fractional (f_I < 1) ultralight component mixed with CDM.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend an existing Lyman-alpha hydrodynamic emulator grid with mixed CDM plus ultralight-scalar initial conditions parameterized by (m_I, f_I), analogous to existing mixed cold-plus-warm dark matter Lyman-alpha analyses, and expose it as a flux-power likelihood.

members.model_name: Composite asymmetric dark matter with a dark photon portal
members.description: The composite dark-baryon form factor for dark-photon-mediated nuclear scattering is not available: direct-detection recasts currently assume pointlike dark matter, while the card flags that compositeness and the light-mediator recoil spectrum can alter the predicted spectra.
members.proposed_resolution: Compute the dark-baryon charge-radius form factor from the dark QCD spectrum (scaled from lattice QCD nucleon results at the dark confinement scale) and add it, with the light-mediator 1/(q^2 + m_Aprime^2)^2 propagator, to a DDCalc or wimprates recoil pipeline covering PandaX-II through DARWIN exposures.

members.model_name: Three-flavor chiral composite ADM with B-L portal
members.description: The dark baryon octet spectrum, mass splittings, and meson masses of the three-flavor theory come from chiral-effective-theory scaling only; splittings decide which components are stable and U(1)_D charged, which directly controls the direct-detection and displaced-decay targets.
members.proposed_resolution: Rescale existing three-flavor lattice QCD spectroscopy to the dark confinement scale with the model's chiral (U, D) plus vector-like (S) mass pattern to fix the stable-state content and splittings.

members.model_name: Massive dark photon from axion tachyonic production
members.description: No public, validated lattice simulation exists for tachyonic production of a massive dark photon from an oscillating ALP condensate (m_X up to m_a/2, alpha_D ~ 10-100 with backreaction), so the vector occupation spectrum that sets Omega_X, gamma_eq, and the GW source is only estimated analytically; the paper's improved Python code is not released.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend a public lattice framework such as CosmoLattice with the phi X Xdual coupling and a Stueckelberg/Proca mass term, and tabulate final vector spectra, relic fractions, and GW spectra over (m_X/m_a, alpha_D, f_a) validated against the published templates.

members.model_name: Light-vector-meson dark pion SIMP model
members.description: No public dark-shower configuration exists for this spectrum: a Pythia8 Hidden Valley setup with mass-degenerate dark quarks, stable dark pions, and dark rho mesons that decay only to SM particles through kinetic mixing (m_rho < 2 m_pi), including hadronization tuning for the confining SU(N_c) sector.
members.proposed_resolution: Build and publish a Pythia8 Hidden Valley card set for this model (N_c, N_f, m_pi, m_rho, f_pi, epsilon), fixing the visible/invisible fractions and rho lifetime consistently with the thermalisation lower bound on the portal width.

members.model_name: Inflation-produced dark photon dark matter with Proca-star substructure
members.description: No survey-recast machinery or likelihood exists to convert the predicted soliton/compact-halo population (M_s, M_h, density profiles) into pulsar-timing, microlensing, photometric microlensing, or extragalactic strong-lensing constraints, and finite-size, fuzzy-envelope lenses are not covered by point-mass PBH limits.
members.proposed_resolution: Build a population-to-observable recast: fold the substructure mass function into finite-size-lens magnification maps for Subaru/HSC and OGLE microlensing likelihoods, PTA Doppler/Shapiro delay statistics, and strong-lensing flux-ratio/perturbation likelihoods, with survey selection functions parameterized in (m, H_I).

members.model_name: Three-body interacting superfluid dark matter around black holes
members.description: No likelihood exists comparing the predicted three-body superfluid black-hole-environment observables to EHT shadow, strong-lensing, or GW data; the card records likelihood_available: no and the route as planned.
members.proposed_resolution: Once the forward models exist, wrap published EHT shadow-size posteriors (Sgr A*, M87*) and GW upper limits into a likelihood over (m, Lambda, rho_0, M_BH), marginalizing over black-hole spin and inclination.

members.model_name: Pseudo-scalar mediator dark matter with hidden neutrinos
members.description: No nonlinear structure-formation calibration exists for transfer functions with enhanced/oscillatory DAO peaks that overshoot CDM power; halo-mass-function prescriptions are calibrated on suppressed or CDM-like spectra, blocking the mapping from the linear spectrum to low-mass halo abundance and the 21 cm signal.
members.proposed_resolution: Run a suite of N-body simulations with initial conditions drawn from the model's oscillatory enhanced transfer functions, calibrate a modified sharp-k/smooth-k halo-mass-function prescription against them, and couple the result to a semi-numerical 21 cm code (e.g. a 21cmFAST-class model) for cosmic-dawn predictions.

members.model_name: Intermediate-mass pseudo-Goldstone boson partial dark matter
members.description: Nonlinear structure formation for the mixed CDM plus intermediate-mass PGB component is uncalibrated (halo and subhalo mass-function effects unknown, simulation_calibrated: no), blocking quantitative weak-lensing and 21-cm forecasts that require nonlinear P(k).
members.proposed_resolution: Run N-body simulations with fractional ultralight-scalar initial suppression (or a Schrodinger-Poisson/fuzzy-DM hybrid at the lighter masses) to calibrate a nonlinear matter-power correction, then feed it into a standard weak-lensing/21-cm Fisher pipeline (e.g. CosmoSIS) for percent-level f_I forecasts.

members.model_name: Rapid-turn multifield inflation seeded primordial black holes
members.description: No numerical multifield perturbation pipeline is attached that evolves curvature and isocurvature modes through the rapid-turn history on the curved target space and outputs the enhanced P_zeta(k), so the O(1e7) enhancement rests on analytic estimates alone.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the two-field action with target-space metric gamma_ab(phi) in a public transport-method solver (PyTransport or MultiModeCode), parameterized by turn rate, Delta theta, Delta N, and feature scale k, and validate the analytic enhancement formula against the numerical P_zeta(k).

members.model_name: Gravitationally produced nonthermal X-boson dark matter
members.description: No public inflationary particle-production solver computes the gravitationally produced X spectrum, energy density, and isocurvature/bispectrum statistics as a function of m_X/H_e for general slow-roll backgrounds; the paper's mode-function computation exists only as its own numerics for chaotic m^2 phi^2 inflation.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement a public Bogoliubov/mode-equation solver for a minimally coupled spectator scalar across the end of inflation, parameterized by (m_X/H_e, inflaton potential, H_e), outputting n_X, the blue isocurvature power spectrum, and the isocurvature bispectrum, validated against the paper's f_NL ~ 30 window for m_X < 4 H_e.

members.model_name: Hidden Peccei-Quinn Higgs double-field axion-inflation model
members.description: No implementation of the double-field hidden-PQ-Higgs/SM-Higgs inflationary dynamics exists, so the trajectory, H_inf, and the effective f_a(t) during inflation — the inputs that decide whether isocurvature is actually suppressed — cannot be computed for given potential parameters.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the two-field potential with nonminimal curvature couplings in a public transport-method code (PyTransport or MultiModeCode), compute the background trajectory and perturbation spectra, and extract H_inf and effective f_a during horizon exit for comparison with Planck isocurvature bounds.

members.model_name: High-decay-constant QCD axion dark matter with PBH-seeded UCMHs
members.description: UCMH growth around PBH seeds and their tidal disruption into axion streams in the Galactic potential are modeled only with semi-analytic profiles and an assumed encounter rate; no simulation-calibrated model of stream density enhancement and Earth-encounter statistics exists.
members.proposed_resolution: Run N-body simulations of PBH-seeded minihalo secondary accretion and subsequent tidal stripping along Milky Way orbits, and fit a stream density and encounter-rate model as a function of M_PBH, f_PBH, and orbital parameters.

members.model_name: Post-inflationary ultralight axion string dark matter
members.description: Axion-string network simulations cannot reach the cosmologically relevant log(m_r/H) ~ 60-70, so the string tension, axion emission spectrum, and GW spectrum for this ultralight post-inflationary scenario all rest on a contested large-log extrapolation, and no public emulator of the emission/GW spectra as functions of (f_a, m_a, log) exists.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend adaptive-mesh global-string lattice simulations (AMReX-based codes of the Gorghetto/Buschmann type) to larger logs, quantify scaling violations, and release an emulator of the axion emission spectrum and dOmega_gw/df parameterized by log(m_r/H), f_a, and domain-wall number for downstream likelihood use.

members.model_name: Supersymmetric Nelson-Barr gravitino LSP dark matter
members.description: Affleck-Dine condensate fragmentation and Q-ball formation for the Nelson-Barr heavy-quark flat direction in gauge mediation have not been simulated, leaving the Q-ball charge, decay branching to gravitinos, and BBN consistency of the baryon-asymmetry prediction uncertain.
members.proposed_resolution: Run lattice simulations of the Affleck-Dine condensate fragmentation for this flat direction's gauge-mediated potential (or adapt existing Q-ball charge-distribution simulations) to determine whether Q-balls form and whether their decays stay inside the allowed BBN/gravitino-injection window.

members.model_name: Mirror-sector dark neutron WIMP-baryogenesis model
members.description: The requirement that dark nucleosynthesis fail (so dark matter stays as individual dark neutrons rather than dark nuclei or atoms) is asserted from qualitative rate arguments; no dark-sector nuclear reaction network exists to verify it across the dark confinement scale, mass splittings, and dark-electron mass.
members.proposed_resolution: Adapt a BBN reaction-network code (AlterBBN/PRIMAT-style) to the dark sector: compute dark deuteron binding and capture rates from rescaled nuclear EFT as functions of Lambda_QCD_prime and the p'-n' splitting, and map the parameter region where dark nucleosynthesis genuinely fails.

members.model_name: Framed Standard Model hidden-sector dark matter candidates
members.description: Portal phenomenology is limited to order-of-magnitude estimates (scattering at a few percent of neutrino cross sections, unspecified collider bump rates); no quantitative cross sections, widths, or event rates have been derived from the Z-G and Higgs mixing elements.
members.proposed_resolution: Derive explicit differential cross sections for hidden-state scattering on nucleons/electrons through the Z-G mixing portal and production rates for TeV co-quark/co-lepton thresholds, then encode them in a FeynRules/CalcHEP model so standard event tools can be used.

members.model_name: Conformal freeze-in composite dark-pion dark matter
members.description: Composite form factors for the vector-meson dark photon have not been computed, so elementary dark-photon search curves cannot be reliably recast onto the composite epsilon-m_A_D parameter space.
members.proposed_resolution: Compute the composite dark photon's production and decay form factors (vector-meson-dominance or holographic estimate) and fold them into an existing recast framework such as Darkcast to rescale published fixed-target and collider limits.

members.model_name: No-Scale F-SU(5) golden-strip Bino dark matter
members.description: The collider test of the golden strip rests on pre-Run-2 statements of LHC testability; no recast of the vector-like flippon production and high-multiplicity-jet SUSY cascade signatures against current LHC Run 2/3 search likelihoods has been implemented.
members.proposed_resolution: Build the model in MadGraph via a UFO from the gap_1 SARAH implementation, generate flippon and gluino/squark cascade events, and recast against current multijet plus missing-energy and vector-like-quark searches with CheckMATE or MadAnalysis5 recast databases.

members.model_name: Pure gravity mediation neutral wino dark matter
members.description: Disappearing-track recasting for the 155-170 MeV-split charged wino requires experiment-specific tracklet efficiency and soft-pion acceptance maps that are not fully public, so the collider route cannot produce reliable exclusion contours for the PGM spectrum.
members.proposed_resolution: Adopt the ATLAS/CMS HEPData tracklet efficiency maps for disappearing-track analyses inside a recast framework (CheckMATE or MadAnalysis5 long-lived module) and validate against the published pure-wino exclusion curves before applying to the PGM gaugino spectrum.

members.model_name: Atomic dark matter with cosmological dark magnetic fields
members.description: No ultrahigh-frequency gravitational-wave measurement or upper limit exists at the frequencies where graviton-to-dark-photon conversion would deplete the signal, so the gw_conversion observable has no dataset or likelihood to be evaluated against, only proposed detector concepts.
members.proposed_resolution: Adopt published sensitivity projections of ultrahigh-frequency GW detector concepts (e.g. cavity/Gertsenshtein-based proposals) as forecast likelihoods for the depletion signature, and update to real limits as instruments are built.

members.model_name: Dark-dimension dark graviton dark matter
members.description: No detector data or sensitivity model exists for gravitational waves at the characteristic frequencies of keV-mass dark gravitons, roughly 1e8 times above LIGO bands, so the proposed high-frequency GW probe cannot be evaluated at all.
members.proposed_resolution: Develop sensitivity curves for proposed high-frequency GW detection concepts (e.g. resonant cavities or levitated-sensor proposals) in the relevant band and build a forecast tool mapping (m_DM, coupling strength) to signal-to-noise in those concepts.

members.model_name: Filtered Dirac fermion dark matter at a first-order phase transition
members.description: The singlet scalar potential is left unspecified except for the requirement of a first-order phase transition, so the phase-transition thermodynamics (alpha, beta/H, v_w, T_n) and the scalar-Higgs mixing angle cannot be derived from Lagrangian parameters, blocking both the GW forecast and a self-consistent direct-detection map.
members.proposed_resolution: Specify a concrete renormalizable potential for phi (e.g. tree-level barrier or thermally driven), compute the finite-temperature effective potential and bounce action with CosmoTransitions to obtain (T_n, alpha, beta/H) and check wall-velocity consistency with the filtering benchmark v_w = 0.01, and derive sin theta and m_phi from the same potential.

members.model_name: Asymmetric higgsino dark matter
members.description: The required electroweak phase transition at T_EWPT ~ 1-10 GeV has no concrete, computable realization: the paper notes it may need degrees of freedom beyond the MSSM, so the abundance prediction is conditional on an unspecified scalar sector whose transition dynamics cannot currently be calculated.
members.proposed_resolution: Construct an explicit extended-Higgs/singlet sector that delays the electroweak transition to 1-10 GeV and compute its finite-temperature effective potential and transition temperature with CosmoTransitions, recording the viable parameter map as a registry input.

members.model_name: Radion misalignment dark matter in a five-dimensional weak-scale framework
members.description: The black-hole superradiance edge of the excluded region is flagged in the card as uncertain because radion self-interactions introduce nonlinear effects that the linear superradiance calculation does not capture; no calculation covering the self-interacting regime is attached.
members.proposed_resolution: Redo the superradiance spin-down bounds including the radion quartic/self-interaction terms (bosenova and level-mixing saturation effects) for the model's parameter-dependent self-coupling, following modern nonlinear superradiance treatments, and publish the corrected exclusion edge as a function of the self-coupling.

members.model_name: Dark glueballs with associated ultralight axion dark matter
members.description: The glueball component's late-time behavior needed for structure and BBN projections is uncalibrated: glueball self-interaction cross sections and lifetimes are only dimensional estimates, so whether the subcomponent acts as collisionless CDM, SIDM, or a decaying species in the recast step is not quantitatively fixed.
members.proposed_resolution: Derive glueball elastic self-scattering cross sections and portal-induced lifetimes from lattice matrix elements for the chosen gauge group, mapping (Lambda_dark, portal scale) onto a sigma/m and tau_glueball surface that the recast step can consume.

members.model_name: Generalized ultra-light axion-like cosmological field
members.description: No nonlinear matter-power prediction (simulation-calibrated fit or emulator) exists for the generalized-n ULA fluid, so galaxy-survey constraints on the axion fraction rely on linear theory plus untested bias/EFT modeling in the mildly nonlinear regime; the card marks simulation_calibrated as 'no'.
members.proposed_resolution: Run N-body simulations with the generalized ULA linear transfer functions as initial conditions (and quantum-pressure corrections where relevant), then build a small emulator or halofit-style correction for P_nl(k,z; n, z_c, f_zc) to plug into an EFT-of-LSS survey likelihood.

members.model_name: Chameleon-controlled density-dependent dark matter interactions
members.description: The worked model is an isolated dark sector with no specified visible-sector portal, so laboratory direct-detection rates for the density-dependent scenario (obs_chameleon_lab_density_response) cannot be computed at all; kinetic mixing is only mentioned as future work.
members.proposed_resolution: Specify a minimal visible portal (e.g. kinetic mixing of the dark U(1) with hypercharge), derive the environment-dependent nuclear/electron recoil rate with the terrestrial chameleon field value from step s1, and check the induced fifth-force/screening constraints.

members.model_name: Big-Bang Dark Nucleosynthesis nuclear dark matter
members.description: No coupling of the dark nucleons to the Standard Model is specified (portals: unknown), so the coherent direct-detection observable has no defined cross-section normalization to compute.
members.proposed_resolution: Define benchmark portal completions (e.g. a dark-photon kinetic-mixing or Higgs-portal coupling of the dark nucleon) and derive the per-nucleon SM coupling that the composite cross section coherently scales from, adding these benchmarks to the card's parameter space.

members.model_name: Self-interacting bosonic dark matter core in neutron stars
members.description: The dark-core mass fraction is an assumed benchmark: no capture/formation/population model exists to predict which neutron stars carry a dark core of a given fraction, so constraints cannot be converted into bounds on underlying particle parameters.
members.proposed_resolution: Derive the dark-core mass fraction from the formation channels the paper sketches (neutron-to-DM conversion, bremsstrahlung production, accretion) as a function of m_D and sigma_D, and couple it to a neutron-star population synthesis model to predict the fraction distribution across observed pulsars and merger events.

members.model_name: Gauge-mediated Q-ball dark matter
members.description: The neutron-star survival constraint on stable baryonic Q-balls, including the U(1)-breaking A-term suppression of Q-ball growth argued in rel_1912_06993, has no reusable implementation mapping (Q, M_F, m_3/2, A-term) to allowed/excluded regions.
members.proposed_resolution: Derive and code the neutron-star capture rate, neutron absorption rate, and A-term-modified growth equation from the related analysis as a parameterized module returning a survival-time bound versus Q-ball charge and A-term strength.

members.model_name: Cosine self-interacting scalar dark matter
members.description: No galaxy rotation-curve likelihood exists for the bounded-cosine core profiles, including the baryonic and halo-rotation modeling the card flags as necessary, so the (rho_a, scalar mass) parameter space cannot be constrained against observed cored galaxies.
members.proposed_resolution: Build a profile-by-profile rotation-curve likelihood on a public dataset such as SPARC that fits the cosine hydrostatic core solutions plus baryons and an outer halo envelope, testing both the low-density core predictions and the predicted absence of cores in massive halos.

members.model_name: Long-range scalar-interacting dark matter with screening species
members.description: No survey likelihood or covariance exists for confronting the model's void-density, halo-profile, and clustering predictions with modern data; the primary constraint is a qualitative recast with likelihood_available: no.
members.proposed_resolution: Build a summary-statistic likelihood over (beta, r_s) using published void-size/void-density functions (e.g. SDSS/BOSS void catalogs), galaxy two-point clustering, and halo-profile constraints, with covariances estimated from mock catalogs generated by the modified N-body pipeline.

members.model_name: Vector coherent-oscillation dark matter with curvaton-generated curvature perturbations
members.description: The paper's viable-region contours exist only as figures; no reusable scan code maps (m_A, H_inf, R_A, Gamma_chi, kinetic-function exponent) to Omega_A, isocurvature power, and anisotropy amplitude, so the registry cannot re-evaluate the allowed region or extend it to new data.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the paper's analytic abundance and perturbation formulae in a small public scan package (Python) that reproduces the quoted m_A = 1e-21 eV to 1 eV window and H_inf/R_A boundary, exposing the derived isocurvature and g_* amplitudes for downstream likelihoods.

members.model_name: Oscillating asymmetric dark matter (fermion variant)
members.description: No public solver exists for the coupled oscillation-plus-annihilation evolution of fermionic asymmetric dark matter: a density-matrix/Boltzmann system tracking Y_particle and Y_antiparticle with X=2 mass mixing (Delta m), large annihilation, and elastic-scattering decoherence from freeze-out to today; the paper's own integration was released with no code artifact.
members.proposed_resolution: Implement the paper's coupled density-matrix Boltzmann equations as a public Python/C module parameterized by (m_1, Delta m, <sigma v>, initial asymmetry, decoherence rate), validated against the paper's 10 GeV and 1000 GeV benchmark exclusions, and expose the anti-DM fraction history as output for downstream likelihoods.

members.model_name: Conformal freeze-in composite dark-pion dark matter
members.description: There is no quantitative treatment of the confining transition that converts the dark CFT energy density into dark-pion (and heavier resonance) abundances and momenta; the matching is currently an assumption, leaving the dark-pion yield and phase space undetermined beyond scaling estimates.
members.proposed_resolution: Compute the confinement/hadronization of the near-conformal sector via a holographic (AdS/CFT dual) model or lattice simulation of a representative confining gauge theory, delivering a parameterized map from pre-confinement energy density to dark-hadron yields, momenta, and the IR kinetic mixing epsilon.

members.model_name: Baryonic-vector scalar light dark matter benchmark
members.description: No anomaly-canceling UV completion of the gauged baryon-number mediator is specified, so the gauge-consistency validation step cannot be run and the cosmological abundance and stability of chi cannot be defined for this benchmark.
members.proposed_resolution: Adopt and encode a minimal anomaly-canceling charge assignment (e.g. anomalons in a standard gauged-U(1)_B completion), derive the induced kinetic mixing and new-state constraints, and add the anomaly-cancellation check as a scripted validation of the charge table.

members.model_name: Two-body interacting superfluid dark matter around black holes
members.description: No ray-tracing/imaging forward model exists that takes the two-body superfluid n=1 Lane-Emden density profile around an SMBH and predicts photon-sphere shifts, shadow size, or strong-lensing deflections.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend an existing black-hole ray-tracing code (e.g. GYOTO or ipole) with a metric solved for the black hole plus the P_2 superfluid mass distribution, parameterized by (m, a, rho_0, M_BH), and output shadow/lensing observables on a model-parameter grid.

members.model_name: Three-body interacting superfluid dark matter around black holes
members.description: No ray-tracing/imaging forward model exists that takes the three-body superfluid density profile (n=1/2 Lane-Emden core plus inner degeneracy-breakdown region) around an SMBH and predicts photon-sphere shifts, shadow size, or strong-lensing deflections.
members.proposed_resolution: Extend an existing black-hole ray-tracing code (e.g. GYOTO or ipole) with a metric solved for the black hole plus the P_3 superfluid mass distribution, parameterized by (m, Lambda, rho_0, M_BH), and output shadow/lensing observables on a grid of model parameters.

members.model_name: Gravitational freeze-in Dirac dark matter from Higgs preheating
members.description: No experiment or public likelihood has sensitivity to the predicted 10-10^3 MHz stochastic gravitational-wave background, so the model's only late-time observable channel cannot currently be tested against data.
members.proposed_resolution: Compute the predicted Omega_GW(f) with a lattice GW module and compare against published sensitivity forecasts of proposed high-frequency GW detectors (levitated sensors, microwave-cavity concepts), packaging the comparison as a forecast likelihood; actual detection capability requires new instrumentation.

members.model_name: Ultralight L_mu-L_tau vector dark matter
members.description: The binary-pulsar exclusion boundary in the g-m plane used to check consistency of the PTA fit region exists only as an undigitized figure from the cited literature, with no machine-readable contour or public radiation calculator for muon-charge-sourced ultralight L_mu-L_tau emission.
members.proposed_resolution: Digitize the published binary-pulsar g-m exclusion contours (e.g. from arXiv:2210.03880) and reimplement the analytic orbital-period-loss formula for ultralight vector radiation from muon-charged neutron-star binaries as a small script producing machine-readable bounds.

members.model_name: Symmetric light-mediator self-interacting dark matter benchmark
members.description: No calibrated emulator or simulation suite maps the velocity-dependent Yukawa cross section sigma_T/m(v) of this benchmark (with both repulsive chi-chi and attractive chi-anti-chi channels) onto dwarf core sizes, halo shapes, and subhalo circular velocities across the (m_chi, m_phi, alpha_chi) space; existing SIDM simulations cover only selected cross-section models.
members.proposed_resolution: Run an SIDM N-body suite gridded in effective sigma_T/m at dwarf, Milky Way, and cluster velocity scales (or extend an isothermal-Jeans-type calibrated SIDM halo model to velocity-dependent Yukawa scattering) and fit an emulator for core size, halo shape, and subhalo V_circ including baryonic-feedback systematics.

members.model_name: Asymmetric light-mediator self-interacting dark matter benchmark
members.description: No calibrated emulator or simulation suite maps the velocity-dependent Yukawa cross section sigma_T/m(v) of this benchmark onto dwarf core sizes, halo shapes, and subhalo circular velocities across the (m_chi, m_phi, alpha_chi) space; existing SIDM simulations cover only selected cross-section models, so the halo recast is only partially calibrated.
members.proposed_resolution: Run an SIDM N-body suite gridded in effective sigma_T/m at dwarf, Milky Way, and cluster velocity scales (or extend an isothermal-Jeans-type calibrated SIDM halo model to velocity-dependent Yukawa scattering) and fit an emulator for core size, halo shape, and subhalo V_circ including baryonic-feedback systematics.

members.model_name: Primordial dark matter halos from scalar fifth forces
members.description: No model exists for the present-day local encounter rate and residual free-particle fraction of PDMHs in the Milky Way (including tidal disruption and survival), so the predicted direct-detection depletion cannot be quantified.
members.proposed_resolution: Model PDMH survival and tidal stripping in Milky Way-like potentials (semi-analytic subhalo-evolution machinery adapted to AU-scale, solar-mass clumps) to compute the unbound-particle density at Earth and the Earth-PDMH encounter rate versus M_PDMH.

members.model_name: Rotating Bose-Einstein-condensate cold dark matter with possible vortices
members.description: The card carries only a placeholder recovery route and a mislabeled direct-detection/recoil observable for what is an ultra-light BEC halo-structure model; the real theory-to-observable routing (GP-Poisson halo profiles, cores, vortex signatures, small-scale power suppression) was never extracted, so no physical observable of this model is currently connected to a forward-model chain.
members.proposed_resolution: Rerun the standard enrichment pass on the primary paper to replace the recovery route with physical routes: (m, g) to halo density profiles and rotation curves, (m, g, lambda) to vortex formation criteria, and (m, g) to the linear small-scale cutoff, with correctly labeled channels.

members.model_name: Strongly interacting hidden-sector pion cold dark matter
members.description: The card's only route is a recovery placeholder (data transform on the card itself); no forward-model routes exist from (Lambda_H, m_pi_h, lambda_3, tan beta) to concrete observables such as relic density, Higgs invisible/exotic decays, or direct detection, so no observable is currently evaluable.
members.proposed_resolution: Rerun the full enrichment on the primary paper to construct real routes: a freeze-out relic-density route (Boltzmann solver step using the gap_1 implementation), a Higgs-portal direct-detection route feeding public likelihoods (DDCalc), and a Higgs-mixing collider-constraint route (HiggsBounds/HiggsSignals).

members.model_name: Vectorlike-portal scalar FIMP dark matter
members.description: The routing block is a recovery placeholder: the single route contains only a card-reading data transform and defines no forward-model chain from (lambda, G, m_s, m_F, Delta) to any concrete observable or constraint, so there is no evaluable path even where tools exist.
members.proposed_resolution: Rerun the standard enrichment on the primary paper to build real routes: a freeze-in relic-density route (rate calculation to Omega h^2 target) and a structure-formation route (f(p) to CLASS transfer function to small-scale-structure likelihoods), with citation-supported constraints replacing the placeholder record.

members.model_name: Nonthermal warm wino LSP dark matter
members.description: The predicted imprint sits at k > 100 Mpc^-1, beyond current data; the proposed probe is high-redshift (z ~ 30-200) 21 cm fluctuations, for which no dataset or forward-model likelihood at these scales exists.
members.proposed_resolution: Develop a dark-ages 21 cm power-spectrum forward model reaching k > 100 Mpc^-1 with a suppression-template likelihood, ready for future lunar/space-based 21 cm arrays.

members.model_name: Charge-sequestration charged-X dark matter
members.description: The paper explicitly defers a complete realistic production model: no derivation ties the charge asymmetry, dark-photon annihilation, or parent X' decay history to the required abundance r_X and fraction f_X, so route inputs epsilon_X r_X and f_X are unanchored free parameters rather than outputs of a defined cosmology.
members.proposed_resolution: Construct explicit production histories for each viable window (asymmetric production with dark-photon annihilation for the MeV window; late X' parent decay for the sub-eV window), deriving r_X(m_X, epsilon_X, couplings) so relic-density and structure-formation consistency can be checked alongside the 21 cm signal.

members.model_name: Scalar-contact inelastic scalar dark matter EFT
members.description: The only route is a recovery stub (read_primary_model_card) with no physical forward-model chain from the EFT parameters (m_X, delta, Lambda_S) to the relic density and the XENON1T electron-recoil spectrum, so the card cannot route theory to data at all in its current form.
members.proposed_resolution: Rerun the normal enrichment pass for this card and rebuild the route with explicit steps: coupled freeze-out of XX'/XX/X'X' annihilation, late e X' -> e X conversion decoupling near T ~ 1 MeV, exothermic DM-electron scattering rate, and a XENON1T electron-recoil likelihood comparison.

members.model_name: Vector-contact inelastic scalar dark matter EFT
members.description: The only route is a recovery stub (read_primary_model_card) with no physical forward-model chain from the EFT parameters (m_X, delta, Lambda_V) to the relic density and the XENON1T electron-recoil spectrum, so the card cannot route theory to data at all in its current form.
members.proposed_resolution: Rerun the normal enrichment pass for this card and rebuild the route with explicit steps: XX' freeze-out through the vector current operators, late e X' -> e X conversion decoupling near T ~ 1 MeV, exothermic DM-electron scattering rate, a XENON1T electron-recoil likelihood, and collider mediator constraints relevant to the low Lambda_V ~ 75 GeV cutoff.

members.model_name: One-to-one resonantly produced mixed sterile-neutrino dark matter
members.description: Ly-alpha forest and strong-lensing constraints for this model rely on thermal-WDM-calibrated pipelines, but the resonant spectra are explicitly nonthermal and mixed with CDM, so no emulator or likelihood covers the model-specific T(k) shapes (thermal-WDM equivalent masses are only approximate per the card).
members.proposed_resolution: Extend existing Ly-alpha flux-power emulators and lensing substructure likelihoods from the thermal-WDM axis to a generalized suppressed-transfer-function parameterization (e.g. {alpha, beta, gamma} or {f, k_half}) that spans mixed cold-plus-warm spectra, validated with a small set of hydro simulations of representative mixed models.

members.model_name: Resonantly produced sterile neutrino dark matter
members.description: No public Ly-alpha flux-power likelihood or emulator accepts arbitrary resonant nonthermal sterile-neutrino distributions; the RPSN hydrodynamical grid covers only benchmark distribution shapes, and out-of-grid f_s(p) require new simulations (card assumption rpsn-hydrodynamical-grid, likelihood_available: no).
members.proposed_resolution: Build a Ly-alpha flux-power emulator trained on hydrodynamical simulations spanning generalized nonthermal transfer-function shapes (e.g. the alpha-beta-gamma parameterization) and wrap it with the BOSS/eBOSS flux-power data as a public likelihood, so computed f_s(p) can be constrained without per-model simulations.

members.model_name: Supercool radiative-symmetry-breaking phase-transition PBH dark matter
members.description: Semi-analytic GW spectrum templates (sound waves, bubble collisions, turbulence) are calibrated for weak-to-moderate transitions; their normalization and spectral shape in the strongly supercooled, vacuum-dominated regime relevant here are uncalibrated.
members.proposed_resolution: Run or adopt hydrodynamic/lattice simulations of strongly supercooled transitions (large alpha, relativistic walls) to calibrate an extended template parameterized by (alpha, beta/H_n, wall velocity), and propagate the resulting shape uncertainty into the PTA fit.

members.model_name: Sterile neutrino dark matter with dark-sector freeze-out
members.description: The higher-dimensional operator coupling the singlet scalar to the Standard Model is left unspecified, so the scalar lifetime entering the decay-before-BBN requirement cannot be computed from model parameters.
members.proposed_resolution: Specify a minimal decay portal (e.g. a Higgs-portal mixing or dimension-five operator), derive the scalar width analytically, and delimit the coupling range that gives tau_s shorter than about one second while keeping the dark sector decoupled from the SM bath.

members.model_name: Inflationary dark matter in the luminogenesis model
members.description: The dark-hadron self-interaction cross section sigma(v)/m of the confining SU(4)_DM sector is never computed: the card has no dark-sector spectrum, no scattering amplitude, and no velocity dependence, so the claimed dwarf-galaxy/cusp-core phenomenology cannot be evaluated.
members.proposed_resolution: Derive the lightest SU(4)_DM dark-hadron spectrum and low-energy self-scattering using lattice results and chiral-EFT methods developed for SU(N) dark-baryon models, parameterized by Lambda_4, and output sigma(v)/m for comparison with the 0.1-10 cm^2/g halo-scale window.
